Claims family on apply — landed on branch wt/claims (worktree .claude/worktrees/claims). Not committed.

New file: internal/job/apply_claims.go — applyClaimed, applyClaimExpired, applyHeartbeat, and applyReleased relocated out of apply_tasks.go (name and applyTable entry unchanged). Read-time expiry: still a read verb that writes, unchanged behavior, but now guarded by a cheap SELECT EXISTS so a read with nothing stale opens no transaction and writes no local.json. Only when something is stale does it run a real commit() batch of claim_expired events.

labels.go and criteria.go (the relations leaf's files) still open their own transactions, so their four handlers get a batch via a new `batchInTx(tx)` in envelope.go plus `b.persist()` after their commit, under a TODO(relations leaf) comment. Four small edits per file; the auto-extend tests for label add/remove would otherwise have to be deleted.

Behavior changes: (1) an auto-extend now records a heartbeat event, visible in `job log` — documented in docs/content/docs/concepts/leaves-and-claims.md; (2) applyHeartbeat stamps updated_at, so a label add by the claim holder now bumps updated_at where it previously did not.

Pre-existing defect found, NOT fixed: `job list` never sets ListFilter.Actor (cmd/job/list.go), so the claim_expired a read verb sweeps is recorded with an empty actor. Verified end to end. It predates this leaf and spans several read verbs; it wants its own leaf.

data.text:
Relations, criteria, provenance and kind are on apply, on branch wt/relations (worktree .claude/worktrees/relations). Not committed.

New files: internal/job/apply_relations.go (blocked, unblocked, labeled, unlabeled, found_in_set, found_in_cleared, kind_changed), internal/job/apply_criteria.go (criteria_added, criterion_state), internal/job/apply_relations_test.go. applyTable in apply.go gains nine entries, added as one block so the claims agent's edit to the same map does not collide.

Handlers moved to commit(db, func(tx, b)): RunBlockMany, RunUnblockMany, RunLabelAdd, RunLabelRemove, RunAddKind's inline labels, RunAddCriteria, RunSetCriterion, RunSetFoundIn, RunClearFoundIn, RunSetKind, and RunImport's whole Phase B. recordBlocksUnblockedOn / recordBlocksUnblockedOnCancel are replaced by one emitBlocksUnblockedOn(tx, b, blockerID, blockerShortID, reason, actor) in blocks.go; close.go and cancel.go call it, and the DELETE moved into applyUnblocked. No handler in the family calls recordEvent; the only remaining callers are claims.go and heartbeat.go (agent-claims').

Import's batch order: per task in pre-order DFS created -> labeled -> criteria_added; then every blocked event walking `flat` in document order; then every found_in_set. Both ends of a block therefore exist before the edge event. dbIDByParsed is gone: the events carry short ids, so nothing needs a row id except planNewCriteria.

Payload additions: CriterionEntry gains `sort_key` (apply must not mint a fractional key or a shuffled log reorders criteria), and its `short_id` is now filled by every writer. UnblockedPayload.Reason is now a typed UnblockReason with UnblockManual / UnblockBlockerDone / UnblockBlockerCanceled; the JSON strings are unchanged. Marshalling sample updated. No other JSON key changed.

Two writers had to split read from write, because apply's writes are idempotent and so cannot report what changed: labels.go gained splitLabelsByPresence (added vs existing, removed vs absent) and criteria.go replaced insertCriteria with planNewCriteria (validates, mints short id + sort key, writes nothing) and SetCriterionState with ResolveCriterion (read-only). RunUnblockMany's "not blocked by" check is now an explicit EXISTS rather than RowsAffected. criteria_test.go's four low-level tests were rewritten onto RunAddCriteria/RunSetCriterion — the functions they called no longer exist, by design.

Also fixed in passing: blocks.created_at, task_labels.created_at and found_in.created_at came from SQLite's strftime default (wall clock at insert); they now come from the event ts, and applyDump was widened to carry all three so a clock-reading apply is visible. That widening is what caught mutation 2 below.

Determinism: TestApplyDeterminism_ImportedPlanRebuildsFromAShuffledLog imports a plan with labels, criteria, a cross-ref blockedBy and a foundIn, then sets two criterion states, removes a label, unblocks one edge by hand, changes a kind and closes a blocker (auto-unblocking two edges) — shuffle, rebuild into a fresh database, dump-compare. TestApplyDeterminism_ImportedPlanRebuildsFromItsEventsAlone is the plain criterion: import once, rebuild from the events, identical. TestApplyDeterminism_RelationsFamilyRebuildsIdentically does the same over the handler-driven sequence, and TestRelationsHandlers_EmitPositionedEventsOnly fails on any events row with rep '' after that sequence.

Red first: the new test files failed to build on the missing UnblockManual and CriterionEntry.SortKey. Mutation-checked with two injected bugs — applyCriteriaAdded minting its own sort key (caught by the unit test) and applyLabeled stamping created_at from the clock (caught by the determinism dumps only after applyDump was widened; before that it survived, which is why the widening is part of this change).

Verification: go fix (two passes, clean), gofmt, go vet, go mod tidy, go build all clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; node --test internal/web/jstest/*.test.mjs 421/421. data.text:
The store landed on branch wt/store (worktree .claude/worktrees/store). Not committed.

New files: internal/migrations/0011_log_watermarks.sql, internal/job/store.go (open-time sync, watermarks, bootstrap), rebuild.go (replay + rekey rewrite + collision detection + RunRebuild), reconcile.go (the three repair rules), rekey.go (RunRekey), cmd/job/rebuild.go, cmd/job/rekey.go, plus store_test.go, reconcile_test.go, rekey_test.go, cmd/job/rebuild_test.go.

SEQ AGREEMENT. commit() now takes eventlog.AcquireLock(cachePath) around the whole span, primes the recorder from appender.LastSeqLocked() (a new one-line addition to eventlog: LastSeq takes the lock and would deadlock inside it), applies as events are emitted, appends with AppendLocked BEFORE tx.Commit, asserts each returned Seq equals the minted one (a mismatch rolls the transaction back), then advances log_watermarks in the same transaction. So the seq comes from the file, not MAX(seq) in the cache — which matters because purge erases event rows and the cache's seq has holes the file does not. newRecorder/persist became newRecorderLocked/persistLocked because UpdateLocalState takes the same lock; commit must never nest (flock is per open file description).

ON OPEN. Hot path: a stat per file against log_watermarks; equal everywhere and no unknown file, done. A rep whose events the cache holds but whose file is missing is bootstrapped from the cache (gapless run only, else a notice and no rebuild) — that covers both this repo's own pre-store history and, unexpectedly, `job merge`, which stages a copy of the other cache with no store beside it. Fresh clone: no watermarks, files present, rebuild. Foreign file grew: rebuild + reconcile. Legacy (any rep '' row): never rebuild, one-line notice, own writes still append and apply.

A DESTRUCTIVE CASE THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME. "Rebuild whenever sizes disagree" wipes any cache whose watermarked file is absent — it replays less than the cache holds. Found by the merge tests: RunMerge stages the other .jobs.db in a temp dir with no .jobs/ beside it, and the first version of this leaf silently emptied it. Fixed by the bootstrap-any-missing-rep rule above, plus a fourth state, StoreIncomplete ("log incomplete"), which refuses to rebuild and says so when a file cannot be written back.

REKEY. The doc says the mapping applies "from its position in the order". It cannot: the event a rekey exists to disentangle is the `created`, which is always earlier, so a positional fold would leave the collision and the rebuild would still fail. applyRekeys is therefore a pre-pass over the whole ordered stream, rewriting e.Task and every exact-match string inside the payload for that replica. Deterministic on every machine, so both caches dump identically (tested).

RECONCILE. Two deviations. (1) The claim repair emits TWO events, not one: a `released` for the loser (actor `reconcile`, payload gains Reason "lost-merge" and LostClaim, the loser's position string) and a `claimed` re-establishing the winner — releasing alone would leave the task unclaimed, which is not "the earlier one wins". (2) The re-establishing claim's envelope actor is the WINNER, not `reconcile`: applyClaimed reads the holder from e.Actor. LostClaim is what makes the repair idempotent across later rebuilds; both the close and the claim rules are tested for that.

ALSO CHANGED. eventlog.Appender opens its file lazily on first append — it used to create an empty file at OpenAppender, so every read verb that ran an empty commit() left a tracked zero-byte log file. `job status` gains a Store line in md and json ({replica, files, events, cache}). openDBFromCmd and findAncestorDB now accept a directory that has .jobs/log and no cache, which is what makes a fresh clone work on the first command. Two test harnesses had to move each side of a merge into its own directory: the store is the .jobs/ beside the cache, so two caches in one directory shared one log and one replica id.

VERIFIED. go fix/gofmt/vet/mod tidy clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; go build clean; node --test 421/421. Red confirmed first (11 undefined symbols, then three reconcile rules failing on behaviour). Driven against a copy of this repo's real .jobs.db: 2,772 legacy rows survive, its one positioned event bootstraps into a log file, a foreign file dropped in prints the notice and changes nothing, `job rebuild` refuses, and a new `job add` still works. Eight parallel `job add` processes produce a gapless 8-line log and 8 tasks.

data.note: Integrated. Facts for adopt and cursors: commit() holds the store lock across recorder, append (AppendLocked, seq primed from the file) and the SQLite transaction, and sets log_watermarks in the same transaction. syncStore in store.go runs on every OpenDB: in sync, rebuilt, "predates the store" (any rep '' row; never rebuilt), or "log incomplete" (a replica's file missing and not writable back). Rekey is a whole-stream pre-pass. StoreSyncOf(db) gives job status its line. Appender opens its file lazily so read verbs leave no empty file.

data.text:
Adoption landed on branch wt/adopt (worktree .claude/worktrees/adopt). Not committed.

New files: internal/job/adopt.go (probe + orchestration), adopt_commit.go (verify, append, swap), adopt_translate.go (legacy rows -> envelopes, cache -> snapshot payload), apply_snapshot.go, dump.go (dumpCache/dumpHistory — logicalDump lifted out of merge_test.go), adopt_test.go. Changed: internal/eventlog/envelope.go (+Legacy), internal/job/apply.go, database.go (OpenDB calls adoptIfLegacy before it opens anything), local.go (+AdoptFailed), gitignore.go, cmd/job/gitignore.go, gitignore tests, DOCS.md, docs/reference/setup.md, docs/getting-started/initialize.md.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS, and where it aborts: open the legacy cache (outside the lock, because openCache's config seed takes the lock and flock does not nest) -> take the store lock -> re-probe the path (another process may have adopted) -> mint the replica id if local.json has none -> translate every rep '' row into a `legacy` envelope with ts = created_at*1000 -> mint one `snapshot` envelope -> assign rep/seq from appender.LastSeqLocked -> build <cache>.adopting from the existing log plus those envelopes -> DUMP BOTH AND COMPARE. That is the abort point: any difference removes the candidate, writes the diff to <cache>.adopt-failed, appends nothing and renames nothing. Only then: append the lines, write the watermarks into the candidate, persist local.json, close both, rename <cache> -> <cache>.pre-adopt (sidecars too) and <cache>.adopting -> <cache>.

THREE FINDINGS THE BRIEF DID NOT PREDICT, all found by driving a copy of this repo's real database.

1. THE SNAPSHOT CANNOT GO LAST. The brief says ts = now, after everything. That silently breaks the cache: this repo's log already holds 25 positioned lines whose tasks were created by LEGACY events, so with the snapshot last those lines apply to a task that does not exist yet and their event rows get task_id NULL — `job log` and `job show` lose them. The snapshot's ts is therefore min(existing line ts) - 1: it summarizes the legacy history, which is what a snapshot is for, and everything the log already holds replays on top of it. Those lines' effects are already in the payload and every apply writes absolute values, so replaying them lands on the same state — and the dump comparison is what proves that rather than assuming it. With no existing lines (the ordinary case) the snapshot is last, as the brief describes.

2. applySnapshot CANNOT TRUNCATE `tasks`. events.task_id REFERENCES tasks(id) with no cascade, so emptying tasks fails the foreign key for every event already recorded against a task, and re-inserting could not restore the link because an event row does not carry the short id it was resolved from. Tasks are reconciled instead: upsert by short id (which keeps every row id, and so every event's link), then delete any task the snapshot does not name along with its events — exactly purge semantics. The other five tables are truncated and refilled as the brief says. `events` is untouched.

3. LEGACY EVENT ROWS ARE LINKED AFTER THE FACT. Their task is created by the snapshot, which is later in the order, so rebuildFromInTx records them with insertEventRowID and sets task_id at the end of the replay from the row id it got back. Deferring the whole row to the end (the obvious alternative) reorders `job log` within a second.

Also worth knowing: adoption is NOT fatal when it aborts — the legacy cache still works exactly as it did, and blocking every command on a conversion would be an outage. The refusal is printed and recorded as adopt_failed in local.json so the next open does not rebuild and compare the whole database again. JOBS_NO_ADOPT=1 reads a legacy database as-is for one invocation; that is what makes the `job log` byte-identity evidence possible.

One known, transitional imperfection in `job log` order: main still writes some rep '' rows (claims.go and heartbeat.go), so this repo's database has legacy rows interleaved with positioned ones inside the same second. A legacy row's ts is its created_at in whole seconds, so it now sorts before a positioned row from the same second whatever their row ids were. Two lines of 3,160 move, both within their own rendered minute. It cannot happen once no writer emits unpositioned rows.

Verification: go fix/gofmt/go vet/go mod tidy/go build all clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; node --test 421/421. Red confirmed first (11 undefined symbols). Mutation-checked with three injected bugs: applySnapshot dropping completion_note (caught), dropping a label's created_at (caught), and removing apply's legacy short-circuit (SURVIVED — the rebuild has its own path for legacy envelopes and never calls apply on them, so TestApply_LegacyEnvelopeWritesNoState was added to exercise that rule directly; it now catches it). Driven end to end against a consistent copy of this repo's database with a freshly built binary: 2,776 legacy events carried across, a snapshot of 465 tasks, 0 rows with rep '', `job status` says "cache in sync" on the first and second open, `job rebuild` now succeeds where it used to refuse, and `job add` works.

data.note: Integrated as f79885a. Two corrections to the plan worth keeping: the snapshot sorts immediately before the earliest line the log already holds, not last, because positioned lines written before adoption name tasks whose created events are legacy; and applySnapshot upserts tasks by short id rather than truncating, because events.task_id references tasks without ON DELETE. JOBS_NO_ADOPT=1 reads a legacy cache without converting it; a failed adoption is recorded in local.json (adopt_failed) with the diff at .jobs.db.adopt-failed so it is not retried on every command.

data.text:
Cursors are on the log position on branch wt/cursors (worktree .claude/worktrees/cursors). Not committed.

NAME. One word everywhere: `position`. Go keeps `eventlog.Position` and gains `EventEntry.Position()`; the API adds a `position` field beside `id` on every event; the query params are `?since=<position>`, `?at=<position>` and `/log?before=<position>`; the SSE `id:` line is the position, so a browser's Last-Event-ID is usable verbatim as ?since=; the island is `{headPosition, eventCount}` (was `headEventId`); `--at` on scripts/replay-snapshot takes a position; the JS calls it `position` too (`frame.position`, `xToPosition`, `positionToX`, `stepPosition`, `windowForPosition`, `parseAtFromQuery` returns one).

LEGACY CURSORS. position.go now accepts an empty rep, and `EventEntry.Position()` puts the cache row id in the seq slot for a legacy row ("<ts>--<rowid>"). Documented in position.go as meaningful only within one cache. This is not academic: this repo's own database is entirely legacy, so every cursor the dashboard exercised in the browser pass was of that form.

SQL. `job.EventPositionExpr(alias)` / `EventPositionArgs(p)` are the one place the (ts, rep, CASE WHEN rep='' THEN id ELSE seq END) tuple is written; every ordering and bound uses it, so SQL and Go agree on the legacy substitution. Ordering everywhere moved off (created_at, id) onto the tuple — the log query, the actors walk, the actor page's event list, /log's newest-first sort.

ORDINALS, NOT POSITIONS, IN THE FRAME CACHE. replay.mjs's FrameCache answers "how far apart are these two frames", which a position cannot answer, so a Frame now carries both `position` (the cursor) and `ordinal` (events since genesis) and the cache keys on the ordinal. The buffer holds one array ordered by position plus a position→index map; `frameAt(cursor)` resolves an unknown cursor by binary search to the newest event at or before it, so a bookmarked ?at= survives events arriving around it. `reverseEvent` cannot know the previous event's cursor (that is a fact about the ordered log, not the event) so it leaves position null and _replayBackward refills it.

A REAL BUG THIS FOUND, unrelated to cursors but fatal to them. Assets are content-fingerprinted, so `import … from "./position.mjs"` resolves against the importer's hashed URL and 404s; the layout's importmap is what maps unhashed specifiers onto fingerprinted URLs. A module missing from that map kills the whole graph downstream of it with ZERO console errors — `sleepy load` said 0 errors while the scrubber silently never entered history mode; `sleepy wire` showed the 404. Added internal/web/templates/importmap_test.go, which scans every relative import under assets/js and fails when one has no entry (red on position.mjs, and every pre-existing module was already covered). Gotcha recorded.

RED FIRST, with one exception I should name: position.mjs was written before its test file, so those 9 JS tests were green on the first run. Every other new test was watched fail first — the eventlog Legacy tests (undefined symbol), the four internal/job cursor tests (undefined GetEventsAfterPosition), the three handler tests (400 on a position ?at=), and the importmap test (position.mjs missing).

VERIFIED. go fix / gofmt / vet / mod tidy clean; `go test ./... -p 1` green; `go build ./...` clean; `make test-js` 431/431. Browser: served a copy of this repo's store on :7841 and loaded /, /plan, /log, /actors, /issues plus each of those under `?at=1788309934000--2833` — all 200, zero console errors, 40 resources with no non-200, one fetch (/events?limit=2772). The scrubber enters history from the URL and its banner reads "?at=1788309934000--2833 · 1h ago · 2026-09-02 00:45:34"; /log renders 500 live rows with zero duplicate positions; an SSE frame's `id:` line is the position; `job tail --format=json` frames carry it.

NOT DONE, deliberately. `internal/job/search.go`'s note search still orders by e.id DESC — that is a display ordering, and after a rebuild row-id order equals position order, so it is stable either way. Same for merge_snapshot.go's read of the legacy events table.

data.note: Added 8 failing tests in next_all_test.go covering: parent-with-open-children excluded from next/next-all/claim-next, deep-leaf descent, canceled/done children don't count as open, --include-parents flag, and parent-scoped leaf descent. Split queryAvailableTasks into two paths: queryAvailableDirectChildren (legacy, --include-parents) and queryAvailableLeafFrontier (new default, recursive CTE). Frontier descends through any parent with open children and returns tasks that have none. Open = status NOT IN (done, canceled). Depth-first preorder via printf-padded sort_path ensures sibling order is preserved across levels. Added --include-parents flag to next and claim-next; runClaimNext now has a Filtered variant. All 8 P1a tests green; full suite passes.

Added 5 P1b tests. 3 refusal tests fail red (parent-with-open-children refused, count included, --force does not bypass). 2 regression guards (leaf still claimable, parent-with-only-closed-children claimable) pass from the start — they guard against the implementation over-matching.

Added countOpenChildren helper. runClaim now checks open-children count before other status checks and errors: 'task X has N open children; claim a leaf instead, or run next X all to see them'. --force does not bypass (structural refusal, not a claim conflict). Full suite green.

Added 6 P1c tests. 5 fail red: last-child-done auto-closes parent; cascade to grandparent; canceled siblings do not block; CLI output shows 'Auto-closed' with ancestor IDs; event log records auto-close with detail.auto_closed and actor = closer of last child. 1 regression guard (parent stays open when sibling still open) passes from the start.

Added cascadeAutoCloseAncestors helper that walks ancestors upward after each done, auto-closing any parent whose open-children count is zero. ClosedResult now carries AutoClosedAncestors []AutoClosedAncestor; events record detail.auto_closed=true with detail.triggered_by=<closerShortID>, attributed to the agent who closed the last child. renderDoneAck prints 'Auto-closed: X "Title"' per ancestor. Obsoleted the 'Parent X complete — run job done X to close it' manual prompt (replaced by auto-close). Dropped ParentNowCloseable from DoneContext; replaced with ParentAutoClosed, computed by passing the auto-closed set into computeDoneContext (parent.Status=='done' alone was ambiguous). WholeTreeComplete no longer short-circuits — it falls through so NextAfterParent can surface sibling subtree work. Removed TestNextAll_ParentWithOnlyDoneChildrenIsLeaf — unreachable since done now cascades. Updated 3 existing tests for the new output.

Added 5 P1d tests. 4 fail red: auto-release on first child add (DB state), CLI output includes Released line and parent ID, idempotent (no double-release event), event log has detail.auto_released=true. 1 regression guard (unclaimed parent unaffected) passes.

runAdd now returns (*AddResult, error). AddResult carries ShortID + AutoReleasedParent + AutoReleasedByActor. When the parent is status='claimed' at add time, the claim is released in the same tx, emitting a 'released' event with detail.auto_released=true, triggered_by_child=<newChildID>, prior_claimant=<who>. CLI 'add' surfaces 'Released: <parent> (prior claim by <actor> auto-released — parent now has open children)'. Updated mustAdd/mustAddDesc helpers + 9 direct runAdd callers in tests + 1 CLI call site. All P1d tests green; full suite passes.

Updated README.md: next table row mentions leaf default and --include-parents; claim-next row same; added 'Leaf-frontier semantics' subsection describing the three linked behaviors (claim refusal, auto-close cascade, auto-release on decomposition). Did not touch docs/ — that directory doesn't exist in the repo despite CLAUDE.md reference. Help text on next / claim-next was already updated inline in commands.go during P1a/P1b. README is the canonical doc for now.

P1 (leaf-frontier semantics bundle) complete. Implemented: (a) next/claim-next default to leaf frontier with --include-parents escape; (b) claim refuses parents with open children; (c) done cascades auto-close upward; (d) add auto-releases a claimed parent. README updated with a 'Leaf-frontier semantics' section. 21 new tests + 3 updated existing. Full suite green.

Added 5 P2 tests: done --claim-next closes and claims next leaf, output shape matches bare claim ack (^Claimed: prefix with 'expires in'), no-next-leaf case succeeds without Claimed line, race (leaf taken by other agent) succeeds without error or claim, -m composes with --claim-next. All 5 fail with 'unknown flag'.

Added --claim-next flag to done. After a successful close, runs runClaimNextFiltered; on success emits a 'Claimed: X "Title" (expires in 15m)' line with the same shape as bare claim ack (greppable ^Claimed:). On race (leaf grabbed between done and claim) emits 'Next leaf unavailable: <reason>' — done still succeeds because done is irreversible, claim is opportunistic. No-next-leaf case omits the claim line entirely. -m composes naturally since it runs first through runDone. All 5 P2 tests green; full suite passes.

Added --claim-next row to done's flag table in README.md. Documented close+claim composition, race behavior (status line not error), and the close-irreversible / claim-opportunistic philosophy. Help text was already updated inline.

Added 6 P3 tests (5 red + 1 literal-string regression guard): -m @file reads file contents into note, -m - reads stdin, @nonexistent errors clearly, newlines preserved, note -m @file also works, literal string unchanged. Currently @file and - are passed through as literal string values.

Added resolveMessage helper (commands.go): -m @path reads the file, -m - reads stdin, plain string is a literal. Wired into both 'done' (guarded by Flags.Changed('message')) and 'note' -m (only when hasMessage). The existing 'note X -' positional stdin form is preserved. All P3 tests green; full suite passes.
Updated README: done -m table row notes @path and - forms; note -m row also notes @path and - (and preserves mention of the positional stdin form).

Added 4 P4 tests. 2 red: done with multi-word prose second positional suggests -m, done with single-word non-ID-shaped second positional suggests -m. 2 regression guards pass from the start: two valid 5-char IDs still works (multi-done), claim with prose already errors (from duration parse failure) — test accepts either 'duration' or '-m' in the message since claim's shape is <id> [duration], not <id> [note].

Added looksLikeShortID helper (5-char alphanumeric check) and an early-exit loop in done RunE that validates every positional arg. Error format: 'done: "X" does not look like a task ID (5-char alphanumeric). Did you mean -m "X"? (positional arg #N)'. All 4 P4 tests green.

Swept README: quickstart examples still make sense under leaf-frontier (claim/done examples target leaves by default). Leaf-frontier section added under Claiming covers claim refusal, auto-close cascade, and auto-release on decomposition. Completing tasks table has --claim-next row with race-behavior explainer. Note -m and done -m both mention @path and - forms. No references to docs/content/docs/ because that directory does not exist in the repo — README is canonical. Full test suite passes.

data.description:
Forward-only SQL migrations, numbered files, tracked in a
schema_migrations table, applied automatically on openDB.

Runner invariants:
  - schema_migrations(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER)
  - Baseline migration 0001_initial.sql captures the current schema
  - Subsequent migrations NNNN_description.sql applied in filename order
  - Each migration runs in its own tx; failure aborts startup
  - Idempotent: running on an up-to-date DB is a no-op

data.description:
Permissive-by-default attribution. The DB carries an optional
default identity; strict mode disables the default.

Precedence (first match wins):
  1. --as <name> flag
  2. DB-level default identity (unless strict mode is on)
  3. Error: "identity required. Pass --as <name> ..."

Surface area:
  - `job init [--default-identity <name>] [--strict]`
    Defaults to `--default-identity $USER` unless --strict.
    Emits a one-line note: "Default identity: ben (from $USER)".
  - `job identity set <name>` — change the default post-init.
    Requires --as on the call (bootstrap discipline).
  - `job identity strict on|off` — toggle strict mode.
  - Honest: no env var fallback, no OS-user inference at
    write-time. If you want strictness, `--strict` gives it
    to you cleanly.
data.title: P3: Default identity + strict mode

- --as <name> overrides the default

- identity strict on disables default; strict off restores it

data.description:
Canceling the last open child cascades upward like done does.
Destination status depends on sibling mix:
  - any sibling closed as `done` → parent cascades to `done`
  - zero siblings done (all canceled) → parent cascades to
    `canceled`

Attribution: the canceling agent is the actor on the cascade
event, same pattern as done.

Event detail: {auto_closed: true, trigger_kind: "cancel",
triggered_by: <shortID>, cascade_status: "done"|"canceled"}

data.description:

(1) Suppress "All tasks in X complete." line when X is the
    highest auto-closed ancestor (avoids duplicating the
    Auto-closed line that was just emitted).
(2) Fix `Next:` to point at a leaf, not a parent-with-open-
    children. Currently NextAfterParent returns the next
    sibling of the top auto-closed ancestor, which may itself
    be a non-leaf; walk into its subtree to find the first
    claimable leaf.
(3) Suppress `Next:` when --claim-next already produced a
    Claimed: line (don't tell the user what to do after
    telling them you already did it).

ordered `[]AckLine` plan in the context step, then the
renderer loops over it. The three improvements become
append/skip conditions on the plan builder, not nested
branches.

data.description:
Surfaces what the caller holds at a glance — fills the 'what am I working on right now?' gap that status's count term doesn't answer. Prefer reusing the existing list filter idiom (parallel to --label) over adding a new verb or overloading status. Positional form 'list <actor>' reads others' claims.

Shape to consider:
- 'job list --mine' — rows for tasks claimed by the caller (via the P3 resolution chain).
- 'job list <name>' — rows for tasks claimed by <name>. No --as required (read).
- Composes with existing list args: 'list --mine --label p0', 'list ben all', etc.
- Output: same tree/markdown shape as regular list, so it pastes into PRs cleanly.

Edge cases: expired claims should be excluded (match status's expireStaleClaims behavior). Empty result should be a friendly message, not an error. Consider whether --mine without --as in strict mode should error ('no caller to scope to') or fall through.

Motivation notes from the 2026-04-21 refactor session are in project/2026-04-21-refactor-and-polish.md's retrospective thread.

- When filter is active, bypasses default `filterTree` exclusion of claimed tasks

- Empty result: friendly 'No tasks claimed by X.' message
- Composes with `--label`, `all`, `--format=json`

Edge cases handled:
- Expired claims excluded (via existing expireStaleClaims)
- Done tasks excluded (status=claimed check in filter)
- Parent context preserved (subtree-preserving filter)

data.description:
/events SSE endpoint backed by a 1-Hz poll-based broadcaster
(same cadence as `job tail`). Event fanout to subscribers.
Reconnect via ?since=<event_id>. Degrades to JSON array
without Accept: text/event-stream. Serves both live updates
and future time-travel replay.

data.description:
internal/web/broadcast. One goroutine polls the events
table every 1s using the existing tail primitive. Fans
out new events to a slice of subscriber channels.
Thread-safe subscribe/unsubscribe.

data.description:

stream. Handshake replays events since ?since= (paged
with ?limit=), then subscribes to the broadcaster for
live tail. Filter params: actor, task, label, type.
data.title: /events SSE handler

data.description:

data.note: Wrote prototype/css/tokens.css. Translates every DESIGN.md color, typography, rounded, spacing, and motion token to CSS custom properties. Plus focus-ring variables and Level-3 shadow, for use by base and components stylesheets.

Wrote prototype/css/base.css. Box-model reset, body background/color, heading and typography utility classes (.t-display, .t-heading-*, .t-body-*, .t-label-caps, .t-anchor for rare all-caps anchors, .t-data-*). Surface utility classes for the three tiers. :focus-visible ring using primary + 40% outer ring. Dark-mode scrollbar styling. Layout helpers (.page, .main, .row/.stack with gap modifiers, .grow, .sr-only).

Wrote prototype/css/components.css. Every component from DESIGN.md §Components: avatars (dot/sm/md/lg + stack), status pills (todo/active/blocked/done), ID pill, label pill, signal card with ambient underline progress, data rows, buttons (primary/ghost/icon), input, tabs, header + footer chrome, scrubber pill with pulsing dot, peek sheet + underlay, code-block notes, graph node (fill=identity, ring=status), plan tree rows + disclosure + subtree indent, section headers, home grids, blocked strip, mini-graph placeholder, empty state, bell. Actor and label colors are expected via --actor-color / --label-color custom properties set inline by colors.js.

Wrote prototype/js/colors.js. FNV-1a string hash (stable across runtimes, zero-dep). actorColor(name) -> hsl(H 65% 55%); labelColor(name) -> hsl(H 40% 50%); initialOf(name) for avatar letters. paint(root) walks the DOM, sets --actor-color on [data-actor] (and fills the first-letter initial on empty avatars) and --label-color on [data-label]. Auto-runs at DOMContentLoaded; idempotent for re-call after DOM updates. Exposed as window.JobsColors. Production implementation graduates to a Go port in internal/web/render during Phase 2.

Wrote prototype/home.html. Header (brand, tabs with active state, search input, bell, theme toggle). Four signal cards (idle, newly blocked, longest claim, oldest todo) with ambient underline progress bars driven by --progress custom property. LTR mini-graph as inline SVG showing phase chain with done-check disks, active actor-colored hub, blocker arc (dashed amber), and +N topological collapse placeholders. Active claims + recent completions as data rows. Blocked strip. Footer metric strip with pulsing heartbeat dot and the collapsed ● Live scrubber pill. All actor avatars get their colors from data-actor via colors.js. Open prototype/home.html in a browser to view.

Wrote prototype/plan.html. Document-mode indented tree using the real Web dashboard v1 project structure as sample content. Phase 1 expanded with subtasks showing the live state (6rIG3/LGpqD/P5JAV/lPEW1 done, hru6q done, P4gto active, PECgy/WJFAK/9AWkj blocked); later phases collapsed. Each row carries disclosure chevron, title, ID pill, label pills (hash-colored via data-label), actor avatars, status pill (todo/active/blocked/done with matching icon), and a right-aligned updated timestamp. Blocked leaves render an inline 'Blocked by ...' sub-row below the main row. Top filter bar for active/archived/all + label chips. Footer includes a keyboard-hint strip (j/k nav, space toggle, / search) per DESIGN.md.

Wrote prototype/peek.html. Renders the plan view with the peek sheet open over it. Sheet at 440px pinned right, Level 3 surface (surface-popover bg + ambient shadow), dim underlay with slight backdrop blur. Sheet content: ID pill + status pill + title, Labels (hash-colored pills), Parent link, Blocks list, Notes rendered as a code block (monospace, preserved whitespace, per DESIGN.md §5.5), Event history with actor avatars and timestamps, 'Open full page' primary button. Bell in --active state to demonstrate the subscribed-to-task affordance.

Wrote prototype/home-empty.html and prototype/plan-empty.html. Home-empty: four signal cards flipped to primary-tinted underlines with quiet one-line context ('No one is waiting.', 'Nothing is blocked.', 'No active claims.', 'No todos.') and '—' where a numeric value would go. Mini-graph, blocked strip, claims, and completions each render a single muted .c-empty line instead of a blank panel. Footer heartbeat says 'waiting for first event'. Plan-empty: muted 'No plan imported yet' heading with a short instructional line ('Run `job import plan.md` to populate.'). No blank rectangles; every empty region is one quiet muted line.

data.note: Home v2 shipped per spec. Sticky chrome (body+page 100vh, main overflow-y:auto min-height:0), search field fills its label, stretched-link .c-row-link pattern (no JS, cmd/middle/right-click all work), avatars are actor anchors with hover ring, panels reordered to Recent Completions -> Active Claims -> Available -> Blocked, blocked rows link to the blocked task with blocker pills as separate real anchors. User confirmed visually.

Implemented: (1) Every task node is an <a href='#/tasks/ID'> with title tooltip (ID + task title + status), aria-label, and data-task-id. (2) Hover highlight — 3px currentColor outer box-shadow + 1px lift, transition from tokens. (3) :focus-visible uses the DESIGN.md focus-ring tokens (2px primary ring + 4px outer). (4) Collapsed +N cluster nodes link to filtered task lists; tooltip lists the collapsed IDs. (5) Bug avatars pulled out of the node anchor (nested <a> is invalid) into detached siblings positioned over the node's bottom-right corner — new .c-graph-node__bug--detached modifier. Each bug is <a href='#/actors/NAME'> with its own hover/focus ring (actor-color band around a background gap). data.description:
Accept multiple blockers in a single invocation so the
design-review-gate pattern (one gate blocked on N parallel
contributions) does not require N sequential calls.

Shape: `job block add <blocked> <blocker> [blocker ...]`.
- All blockers must exist and be open.
- Atomic: all-or-nothing in a single transaction.
- Reject self-block and any blocker that would introduce a
  cycle, checked across the full input set.
- Emit one "blocked" event per edge so the event stream stays
  one-event-per-edge; print one line per edge plus a summary.

  variadic blocker tail on `block add`.

  RunBlockMany or takes a []string; keep the per-edge
  recordEvent(..., "blocked", ...) call at line 51.
- Tests: cycle detection across multi-blocker input;
  duplicate blockers collapsed or rejected (pick one and
  document); atomicity on mid-list failure (nothing persists).

Blocked by R3: the canonical form after this plan is
`block add`; ship multi-value on the new surface, not the
legacy `block X by Y`.

data.description:
Settle the grammar inconsistency that cost the most
round-trips in the 2026-04-22 session, and catch two common
typos up front.

Rule: multi-operation verbs use subcommands; single-operation
verbs use positional + flags.

Concrete work:
1. Introduce `block add` / `block remove` as the canonical
   forms. Keep `block` and `unblock` as aliases; on every
   alias invocation emit a one-line stderr notice, e.g.:
     note: `job block` is an alias for `job block add`; prefer the canonical form.
   Same shape for `unblock` → `block remove`.
2. Alias `job ls` → `job list` with the same "prefer `list`"
   stderr notice.
3. Alias `job show <id>` → `job info <id>` with the same
   notice.
4. Add two lines to the top of `job --help`:
     Multi-operation verbs (label, block): job <verb> <add|remove> <args>
     Single-operation verbs: job <verb> <id> [--flags]

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/block.go, cmd/job/unblock.go — restructure into a
  `block` parent with `add` / `remove` subcommands; keep
  top-level `block` and `unblock` registered, delegating
  after printing the notice.
- cmd/job/list.go — register `ls` via Cobra's Aliases field
  + PersistentPreRun stderr notice gated on cmd.CalledAs().
- cmd/job/info.go — register `show` the same way.
- cmd/job/commands.go — help-text preamble.
- Tests: each alias emits the warning exactly once per
  invocation, exits 0, and runs the canonical action; help
  text contains both grammar lines; notice goes to stderr
  (not stdout) so pipelines are unaffected.

data.description:
Audit short flags across the CLI and add the ones an agent/human would reflexively guess. Concrete starter: cancel --reason should have a -r short form (guessed on 2026-04-22 while drafting project/2026-04-22-opus-feedback.md; no short form existed, wasted a round-trip).

Approach:
1. Enumerate every command's long flags and list the short forms Cobra would accept without clashing.
2. For each, decide whether the short form is obvious enough to be worth adding. Bias toward adding when the mapping is unambiguous (--reason -> -r, --desc -> -d if not taken, --label -> -l if not taken).
3. Add the selected short flags alongside existing long forms (non-breaking).
4. Document the convention in --help or README so future additions stay consistent.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/cancel.go — add -r for --reason as the leading case.
- cmd/job/{add,note,claim,release,...}.go — per-command audit.
- README commands table — short-form column, or inline in each command's flag list.

Tests: each new short flag parses to the same behavior as its long form; no regressions on existing short flags (e.g. -m on note).
data.title: Short-flag conventions — audit and align

data.new_desc:
Audit short flags across the CLI and add the ones an agent/human would reflexively guess — but avoid letters with strong established meanings elsewhere.

Leading case: cancel --reason needs a short form (guessed on 2026-04-22 while drafting project/2026-04-22-opus-feedback.md; wasted a round-trip). Recommend -m (matches note -m '<text>', so 'short flag for free-text body' becomes a cross-command convention). Explicitly AVOID -r on cancel: -r overwhelmingly means 'recursive' in CLI muscle memory (rm, cp, grep, chmod), and cancel already cascades to subtasks, so -r would read as 'recursively cancel' or 'skip the cascade' rather than 'attach a reason.'

Approach:
1. Establish the convention: -m = free-text body (reason, note text, etc.). Avoid letters with strong prior meaning (-r recursive, -f force, -v verbose/version, -h help) unless the command's semantics actually match.
2. Enumerate every command's long flags and list the short forms Cobra would accept without clashing.
3. For each, decide whether the short form is obvious enough to be worth adding. Bias toward adding when the mapping is unambiguous (--desc -> -d if not taken, --label -> -l if not taken, --title -> -t).
4. Add the selected short flags alongside existing long forms (non-breaking).
5. Document the convention in --help or README so future additions stay consistent.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/cancel.go — add -m for --reason as the leading case.
- cmd/job/{add,note,claim,release,edit,label,block,...}.go — per-command audit.
- README commands table — short-form column, or inline in each command's flag list.

Audit short flags across the CLI and add the ones an agent/human would reflexively guess — but avoid letters with strong established meanings elsewhere.

Leading case: cancel --reason needs a short form (guessed on 2026-04-22 while drafting project/2026-04-22-opus-feedback.md; wasted a round-trip). 2. Enumerate every command's long flags and list the short forms Cobra would accept without clashing.
3. For each, decide whether the short form is obvious enough to be worth adding. Bias toward adding when the mapping is unambiguous (--desc -> -d if not taken, --label -> -l if not taken, --title -> -t).
4. Add the selected short flags alongside existing long forms (non-breaking).
5. Document the convention in --help or README so future additions stay consistent.

data.note: Added IdentityDefault and Strict to StatusSummary; RunStatus reads them via GetDefaultIdentity/IsStrict; RenderStatus appends a second line: 'Identity: <name> (default) · strict mode <on|off>' when default is set, else 'Identity: none set · --as required on writes'. New tests cover all four cases plus 'rendered on second line' shape. Updated TestStatus_EmptyDB to use Contains since the second line is now always emitted (got user consent).

R3 complete. Canonical: 'block add <blocked> by <blocker>' and 'block remove <blocked> by <blocker>' (kept 'by' per Ben's grammar-clarity feedback — 'block add X Y' was ambiguous). Legacy 'block X by Y' and 'unblock X from Y' still work but emit a one-line stderr notice routing the user to the canonical form. 'ls' is an alias for 'list', 'show' for 'info', both with their own stderr notices. Root help grew a 'Grammar' subsection naming the multi-op vs single-op rule. All notices go to stderr so JSON pipelines stay clean.

R1 complete. New domain functions RunBlockMany / RunUnblockMany take []blockerShortIDs, run in a single transaction, and roll back atomically on any failure (missing task, self-block, cycle). RunBlock / RunUnblock now thin-wrap the multi versions for source compat. Cycle detection runs against the in-flight transaction so a multi-blocker call that would close a cycle through an earlier-applied edge is correctly rejected. Duplicates in the input collapse to a single edge (idempotent — chosen over rejection so callers can pipe arbitrary lists). CLI: 'block add <blocked> by <b1> [b2 ...]' and 'block remove ...' accept variadic blocker tail; one 'Blocked: ... (blocked by ...)' line per edge plus a summary when len > 1. Legacy 'block X by Y' / 'unblock X from Y' aliases stay single-blocker (deprecated forms shouldn't grow surface).

R4 complete. New notePreview helper builds 'Noted: <id> · <N chars> · "preview"' ack: rune-counted, newlines/tabs collapsed to spaces, snapped to last space in the back third of the 60-rune window before appending …. fmt's %q handles backtick/quote round-trip safely. Full body still stored unchanged via RunNote — preview is display-only.

R5 complete. TaskInfo grew Notes []NoteEntry (Actor, Text, CreatedAt). RunInfo loads them via getNotesForTask which queries event_type='noted' for the task in chronological order (created_at ASC, id ASC tiebreak — RunNote uses wall-clock time.Now() so multiple notes in the same second still sort by insertion). RenderInfoMarkdown emits a 'Notes:' section after Created (omitted when empty); each entry has '[ts] @actor (Xm ago)' followed by indented body. RenderInfoJSON gets a 'notes' array (empty array when none, never null).

R6 complete. Root cause: hard-wrap was in source text (YAML imports preserve author-supplied newlines); renderer dutifully emitted them. Fix unwraps at render time. New unwrapProse helper: collapses single \n inside a paragraph to space, preserves blank-line paragraph breaks, keeps bullet (- / *) and numbered (1.) list lines on their own line. Applied to Description and note bodies in RenderInfoMarkdown. Tabular fields (Children counts, Labels row) untouched. Verified job info njUQV now renders the description on one logical line.

R7 complete. Removed the 'note: <body>' branch from listStateParens. Done tasks now render as '- [x] `<id>` Title' with no parens (or just (labels: ...) when labels are present). Other markers untouched: (canceled), (reason: ...), claimed-by lines, blocked-on lines all preserved. Trees become scannable; rationale is one info call away. Deleted the now-obsolete TestList_DoneWithNote since the new TestRenderMarkdownList_DoneTask_* tests cover the new behavior with stronger assertions (got user consent).

R2 complete. New 'summary' verb gives a two-level rollup (target counts plus one line per direct child), filling the gap between status (whole DB, too broad) and 'list X all' (full subtree, too wide). Domain: SubtreeRollup struct (Done/Open/Blocked/Available/InFlight/Canceled/NextID); buildRollup walks descendants once with a BFS, openBlockerCounts groups blocker-count per task in a single SQL query, and Available/NextID delegate to the same queryAvailableTasks the next/claim-next verbs use, so we never drift from canonical leaf-frontier semantics. Render: 'Title · ID' header, '<done> of <total> done · <N> blocked · ...' rollup line, then 'Title (id): <child rollup>' per direct child (terminal status for closed/leaf children, 'X of Y done · next <id>' for in-flight subtrees). Verified against this very task: 'job summary njUQV' shows 7/10 done with the expected per-child status.

Short-flag audit complete. Convention: -m = free-text body across commands (note, done already had it; cancel --reason now does too — chose -m over -r since -r is overloaded with 'recursive' in CLI muscle memory and cancel already cascades). Added unambiguous short flags where the mapping is obvious: cancel -y (--yes), add -d/-b (--desc/--before), edit -t/-d, list/next -l (--label), log -s (--since), import -p/-n (--parent/--dry-run), tail -e/-u/-t/-q (--events/--users/--timeout/--quiet). Deliberately skipped: --format (no clean letter), --force/--cascade/--purge/--strict/--gitignore/--mine/--claimed-by/--include-parents/--default-identity (rare, destructive, or no obvious mapping). Added a 'Short flags' subsection to root --help documenting both the conventions and the reserved letters (-r/-f/-v/-h).

Docs sweep complete. README updates: new Commands preamble (grammar rule + short-flag conventions); status mentions identity line; new summary entry; list mentions ls alias and structural-line shape; info mentions Notes section and unwrap; note ack format documented; cancel uses -m and -y in examples; block/unblock now describe block add/remove canonical (with by) plus deprecation note on legacy aliases; import/log/tail flag tables show new short flags. CLAUDE.md gained a 'CLI conventions' section calling out: check default identity at session start, prefer canonical forms (aliases warn), and the -m / short-flag convention table — so future agent sessions inherit the right reflexes from day one.

When picking the next-available task with no blockedBy
edges among the candidates, prefer the lowest sort_order.

honour the author's import order for unconstrained

agent that follows the hint, this leads to wrong-order
execution.

data.description:
The bigger design move from the heartbeat retrospective.
When an agent writes to a task they currently hold
(`note`, `edit`, `label add`, `label remove`), the write
itself is an "I'm still working on this" signal — extend
the claim TTL by DefaultClaimTTLSeconds (P1's 30m).

Rules:
- Only extend; never shorten. If the existing
  claim_expires_at is further in the future than now+TTL,
  leave it alone.
- Only extend if the writing actor IS the current
  claim_holder. A `note` from a different actor must not
  silently override another agent's lock.
- Don't add a new event type. The existing `noted` /
  `edited` / `labeled` events already record the activity;
  the TTL bump is a side effect, not a notable event.

Decide before implementation: keep `job heartbeat` as a
low-level escape hatch for "I'm working but not writing"
(recommendation), or remove it entirely once auto-extend
covers the common case. If kept, demote it from the
quickstart and orchestration sections of README.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/tasks.go — RunNote, RunEdit (auto-extend
  block at the start of the transaction).
- internal/job/labels.go — RunLabelAdd, RunLabelRemove
  (same).
- New helper: maybeExtendClaim(tx, taskID, actor) used by
  all four call sites.
- Tests: extend on note as holder; no-op on note as
  non-holder; no-op when current expiry > now+TTL; combined
  with the P1 TTL bump.
data.title: P7 — Auto-extend claim TTL on writes to the claimed task

data.note: Implemented NextFallback in DoneContext. After the existing NextSibling / NextAfterParent walk, if both are nil, query queryAvailableLeafFrontier(db, nil, 1, '') and use its first result. Added third branch to buildDoneAckLines and to the JSON ack renderer. Covers two previously-silent cases: (a) closing the highest-sort_order sibling of a parent whose earlier siblings are still open; (b) closing the last leaf of the last top-level parent when earlier roots still have claimable work. The retrospective's 'sort_order isn't being used' framing was slightly off the mark — the real shape is Next: falling silent when forward-in-sort_order runs out. Live probes confirm. Full suite green.

data.reason: Pivoted to a larger unification: status and summary are doing structurally identical work (rollup + per-child block), differing only in scope (forest vs subtree) and session preamble. Old P6 (leaf-only collapse) is subsumed by unifying status and summary under the status verb. See replacement task.

data.description:
Replacement for cancelled P6 (ccWfW). `status` and `summary` are
structurally identical — aggregate-rollup-plus-per-child — and
differ only in scope (forest vs subtree) and in session preamble.
Consolidate under a single shared renderer; the `status` verb
becomes the unified entry point; `summary` retires as a
deprecated alias.
data.title: Unify `status` and `summary` under `status`

data.description:
Pull summary's rollup+per-child logic into a renderer that
takes (scope, opts) and works for both forest scope (all
roots) and subtree scope (one parent). Behavior-preserving
refactor at this stage: existing `summary <id>` continues to
call it, and every existing summary test still passes
unchanged. This task is purely mechanical — no output shape
changes here; those land in u2 / u3.
data.title: Extract shared subtree-rollup renderer

data.description:
Three refinements to the shared renderer's headline and
per-child block:

(1) Suppress zero-count status tokens. Render only non-zero
    states. "10 of 10 done · 0 blocked · 0 available · 0 in
    flight" collapses to "10 of 10 done".

(2) When the scope is fully complete (every descendant in
    done or canceled), append a closure timestamp to the
    rollup: "closed 2026-04-22 18:47". Source: latest
    done/canceled event within scope.

(3) In the per-child block, drop the trailing ": <status>"
    when the child's status matches the scope's dominant
    status (done when the scope is mostly-done; otherwise
    available). Surface only exceptions — claimed,
    canceled, blocked — so the eye lands on what deviates.
data.title: Tighten the rollup line

data.description:
When the scope's direct children are all leaves (no
descendants of their own), skip the per-child block entirely
— the rollup already says everything worth saying.

Exception: if any of those leaves is currently claimed,
list ONLY those claimed rows, suppressing the
done/available/blocked/canceled noise. Gives the
session-start "who's working on what" signal without the
bulk of the full block. If zero claimed, zero rows.
data.title: Leaf-only collapse with in-flight-only fallback

data.description:
Rewrite `status` without arguments to keep its session
preamble (the open/done/canceled tally line, the identity
line) and delegate the body to the shared renderer with
forest scope.

Output shape:
  <preamble line 1: counts + last activity>
  <preamble line 2: identity>
  <blank line>
  <shared renderer — one row per top-level task with its own
   rollup, per the u1/u2/u3 shape>
data.title: status (no-arg) renders top-level forest via shared renderer

data.description:
Add a `status <id>` form that scopes the shared renderer to
the subtree rooted at <id>. Behavior is what `summary <id>`
does today, plus the u2/u3 tightenings and u6/u7 additions
once they land. No session preamble at the node level — the
preamble is DB-wide metadata and doesn't belong on a subtree
view.
data.title: status <id> delegates to shared renderer

data.description:
After the rollup and per-child block, append:
  Next: <id> "<title>"
naming the first claimable leaf (unclaimed, unblocked,
leaf-frontier) within scope. Uses the same
queryAvailableLeafFrontier path as the P5 done-ack fallback
(jqkTc). Omit the line when scope has no claimable leaves
(fully done, or fully blocked). Forest scope: global
frontier; subtree scope: frontier under <id>.
data.title: Surface Next: in status output (forest + subtree)

data.description:
Surface any claim past its TTL on its own line(s):
  Stale: <id> "<title>" — claimed by <actor>, expired <dur> ago
Forest scope: every stale claim in the db. Subtree scope:
stale claims under the argument task. Multiple stale claims
render as multiple lines; omit the block entirely when none
are stale. Recovery signal for "an agent crashed, this work
needs picking up."

data.title: summary alias with stderr deprecation notice

data.note: Added maybeExtendClaim(tx, taskID, actor) helper in internal/job/claims.go. Called from RunNote, RunEdit, RunLabelAdd, RunLabelRemove immediately before tx.Commit. Rules: only extend when caller IS current claim_holder; only extend, never shorten (preserves long explicit durations); no new event type — the write's own noted/edited/labeled/unlabeled event already signals activity. 7 tests: 4 extension-fires cases, 1 no-shorten guard, 2 non-holder/unclaimed guards. Heartbeat kept per earlier decision. Red/green confirmed; full suite green.

data.description: job add sets sort_order correctly (0, 1, 2, ...) per sibling scope. job import does not — every imported task gets sort_order = 0, so all siblings collide. findNextSibling uses 's.SortOrder > closed.SortOrder' and returns no candidates when all siblings share 0, which breaks Next: hints on imported umbrellas. Fix: in internal/job/import.go's insert path, assign sequential sort_order at each level. Regression test: import a plan with N siblings, assert sort_orders are distinct and ascending. Backfill: one-shot script in scripts/ that renumbers per parent_id using id as tiebreak — not a schema migration since this only affects pre-existing local dbs.
data.title: Fix sort_order assignment in job import (+ backfill script)

data.note: Fixed import.go's hardcoded sort_order=0 by threading sortOrder through the recursive insert function. Children start at 0 (no pre-existing siblings); imported roots start at nextSortOrderForParent(tx, parentDBID), which reads MAX(sort_order)+1 of existing siblings under the import's anchor so we don't collide when importing under an existing parent. Added three regression tests. Also shipped scripts/backfill-sort-order.sh — idempotent renumbering via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY parent_id ORDER BY id), scoped to colliding parent scopes only so job-move-adjusted scopes are preserved. Ran against live .jobs.db: 28 colliding scopes, 162 rows renumbered, 0 remaining. Full suite green.

data.description: Current ComputeDoneContext has three shape-specific fields (NextSibling, NextAfterParent, NextFallback) cobbled together. Replace with a single hierarchical walk: forward siblings of closed, then earlier siblings of closed, then walk up to parent and repeat (forward then earlier at each level). Only hit the global frontier when the closed task's entire root tree has no remaining claimable leaves. Keeps the agent within the closed task's subtree as long as there is work there — 'close D under C; next goes to E' rather than jumping to another umbrella. See conversation 2026-04-23 for full algorithm.
data.title: Rewrite done-ack Next: as a hierarchical ancestor walk

data.note: Replaced NextSibling / NextAfterParent / NextFallback trio with a single Next *Task field on DoneContext, computed by new findNextClaimableLeafHierarchical helper in internal/job/tasks.go. Algorithm: starting at closed's parent, at each ancestor level scan forward siblings (sort_order strictly greater than came-from) then earlier siblings; descend into any parent-with-open-children to surface the first claimable leaf. Walk up until claimable work found or we exhaust closed's root tree; final pass treats the root-level forest as virtual siblings. Keeps SkippedBlocked / SkippedBlockedBy for the forward-sibling-blocked hint (only fires at the immediate parent level). Renderer simplified to one Next: branch. Two new red tests covered the distinct failures of the old path: close-highest-sibling-when-earlier-root-has-lower-sort_path, and walk-up-earlier-sibling-beats-decoy-root. Live probe of the user's example tree confirms close D returns Next: E. Full suite green.

Extracted BuildRollup(db, target *Task) as the shared subtree-rollup engine. target \!= nil is subtree scope (what summary <id> has always rendered); target == nil is forest scope, where DirectChildren enumerates every root-level task. RunSummary becomes a thin wrapper: resolve shortID to *Task, delegate. RenderSummary now skips the headline target line when Target is nil and renders only per-child rows — behaviour-identical for every existing caller (they always pass a non-nil Target). Two new tests pin the forest-scope path: roots-as-children aggregation and no-headline rendering. Existing summary tests untouched and green. Sets up u4 (status no-arg) and u5 (status <id>) to route through the same engine.

Three refinements to the shared rollup renderer: (1) zero-count tokens suppressed — the scoreboard line now only renders non-zero states, so a fully-done scope reads 'N of N done' instead of 'N of N done · 0 blocked · 0 available · 0 in flight'. (2) Closure timestamp appended when the scope is fully complete: 'closed YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' sourced from the latest done/canceled event in the subtree via a new subtreeClosureTime helper. Only fires when Open == 0 and at least one descendant closed. (3) Per-child exception rule: leaf children whose status is 'done' or 'available' (the scope's natural background state) drop their trailing ': status' — the headline counts already cover them. Claimed, canceled, and blocked children retain their status to surface genuine exceptions. Added IsBlocked bool to SubtreeRollup so an 'available' task with an open blocker renders ': blocked'. 5 new tests, all red→green. Existing summary tests preserved.

Added leaf-only collapse to RenderSummary. When every direct child is a leaf (no descendants of its own), the per-child block is padding — the headline scoreboard already conveys done/available/blocked/canceled counts. Only claimed children still render (the 'who's working on what' coordination signal). Mixed scopes (any non-leaf child) keep the full block so the nested rollups stay visible. Two red tests: (1) flat umbrella with done+available+canceled leaves → block fully suppressed; (2) flat umbrella with one claimed leaf → only that row renders. Existing CLI-level summary test was updated (with user consent) to give the child a grandchild so it exercises the non-collapse path; the leaf-only collapse is covered by unit tests in internal/job/summary_test.go.

Status now delegates the body to the shared renderer in forest scope. Flow: RenderStatus writes the preamble (claimed/open/done tally line + identity line), then BuildRollup(db, nil) produces the forest rollup — one Summary with Target=nil and DirectChildren = every top-level task. If there are any direct children, a blank line separates the preamble from the forest block; empty-DB output stays preamble-only, no stray blank line. Claim short updated to reflect the new shape. Live probe on the working DB surfaces the whole top-level landscape at session start: dashboard, papercuts, other umbrellas, each with their own rollup and next hint — which was the motivating use case for the unification. One red test covered the forest-rollup addition. Existing status test suite (Contains-style assertions) unaffected.

status now accepts an optional [id]. With an id, resolves it via GetTaskByShortID, calls BuildRollup(db, target), and renders via RenderSummary. No session preamble at the node level — the preamble is DB-wide metadata and doesn't belong on a subtree view. Without an id, the forest-scope path from u4 still applies. Long/short strings updated to reflect the dual-mode shape. Two red tests: subtree-renders-without-preamble, and output-parity-with-summary. The two verbs are now behaviorally equivalent in the subtree case, setting up u8 to demote summary to a deprecated alias.

Added Next *Task field to Summary, populated by BuildRollup via queryAvailableLeafFrontier — the same canonical path next/claim-next use, so behaviour doesn't drift. Forest scope: queries from all roots; subtree scope: scopes under target. RenderSummary appends 'Next: <id> "<title>"' when Next \!= nil; omitted when the scope has no claimable leaves. Tightened two u3 assertions from 'title not in output' to 'per-child row pattern not in output' so the new Next hint line (which may legitimately name a claimable leaf) doesn't trip them. Live probe: job status surfaces a global Next hint under the forest rollup; job status <id> surfaces a subtree-scoped Next hint — which just pointed me at the next task I need to work on.

Added FindStaleClaims(db, scopeID *int64) and RenderStaleClaims(w, claims) in internal/job/status.go. The status command now snapshots stale claims BEFORE calling RunStatus (which expires them as a side effect) so the snapshot survives. Forest scope: queries all status='claimed' rows with claim_expires_at < now. Subtree scope: the same query wrapped in a recursive CTE rooted at scopeID. Ordered by expired-longest-ago first. Rendered as 'Stale: <id> "<title>" — claimed by <actor>, expired <dur> ago' lines, each on its own line; block preceded by a blank-line spacer when present, omitted entirely when empty. Two red tests covered both scopes and the ordering contract. Subtree test also verifies out-of-subtree stale claims don't leak in. Live probe works — no stale claims currently in the DB, but the snapshot path is wired.

Added 'summary' as a cobra Alias on the status command with a PreRun that emits a stderr notice when CalledAs() == 'summary'. Matches the existing info/show and list/ls deprecation pattern exactly. Deleted cmd/job/summary.go since the old RunSummary→BuildRollup→RenderSummary path is already what status <id> takes after u5. Removed the newSummaryCmd() AddCommand. Stdout parity with status is automatic (same underlying codepath); test confirms. The JxyAc umbrella's unification arc is complete — status is the canonical verb, summary is a deprecated alias, and both forest-scope and subtree-scope paths share the BuildRollup engine.

Docs sweep for JxyAc. README: rewrote the Viewing tasks table — status row now describes session briefing + forest rollup + Next/Stale; status <id> row covers subtree scope with zero-count suppression, leaf-only collapse, closure timestamp, and Next/Stale trailers; summary noted as a deprecated alias; JSON caveat updated. Completing tasks: -m note line mentions the ack echo; new paragraph after the table explains the hierarchical Next: walk (forward siblings preferred, earlier siblings next, walk up the ancestor chain, cross roots only when the local tree is exhausted). Cancellation: reason preview echo documented. Claiming: claim row shows the title ack shape, heartbeat demoted with explicit 'rarely needed' framing, Claims paragraph mentions auto-extend on writes. CLAUDE.md CLI conventions: opening with status is now the landscape briefing rather than just an identity check; summary→status added to the aliases list; -m bullet expanded with ack echo shapes; new bullet explains you rarely need heartbeat because auto-extend covers writes. Full go test ./... green throughout.

data.description:
Six ergonomics findings from a long-session use of `job` to drive
the JxyAc umbrella end-to-end. F1–F4 are real frictions hit
during the session; F5–F6 are polish items to weigh. See
project/2026-04-23-session-feedback.md for the full experience
report and the rationale for each.
data.title: CLI papercuts from the 2026-04-23 session

data.description:
Adding a task with labels currently requires two calls:
`job add ...` then `job label add <id> a b c`. Thread labels
into RunAdd's transaction so the created + labeled events
land atomically and the common case is one call.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/add.go — StringSliceVarP on --label/-l
- internal/job/tasks.go — RunAdd signature gains []string
  labels; insertLabels called inside the existing tx; the
  "labeled" event recorded alongside "created"
- Tests: add with one label, add with multiple labels, add
  with a label containing a comma (validator rejection),
  add with --label omitted (no regression)
data.title: F1 — `job add` accepts `-l, --label <name>` (repeatable)

data.description:
When a plan has a single fenced YAML block but the YAML
fails to parse (e.g., unquoted colon in a title
`title: Surface Next: in status output`), the current error
is the probe-loop's generic
`no YAML tasks: block found in <file>`. The real
`yaml.Unmarshal` error (mapping values not allowed, line N
col M) is swallowed.

Fix: in extractTasksYAML's probe loop, capture the most
recent yaml.Unmarshal error encountered in a candidate
fence. If no block yielded a usable tasks key AND at least
one candidate errored during Unmarshal, surface that error
(with its line/col) instead of the generic message.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/import.go — extractTasksYAML probe loop
  tracks lastErr; RunImport uses it when no block matched
- Tests: plan with one yaml fence and a bad-colon title
  asserts the error text names the parse failure (line
  number or "mapping values are not allowed")
data.title: F2 — Surface real YAML parse errors on import

data.description:
Agents fall back to `job list | grep` when searching by
title fragment, losing parent context and tree structure.
Add --grep <pattern> to list — case-insensitive substring
match by default — that composes with existing filters
(--label, --mine, --claimed-by) and respects --format=json.

Decide before implementation: substring-only, or allow
regex via a separate --grep-regex? Lean substring; it's
what every agent would try first.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/list.go — --grep StringVar, plumbed through
- internal/job/tasks.go — list query adds LIKE filter on
  title (or post-filter, depending on perf on larger dbs)
- Tests: substring match, case-insensitive, no match,
  composes with --label, respects --format=json shape
data.title: F3 — `job list --grep <pattern>` for task search

data.description:
Current dry-run lists imported tasks but omits the block
graph. Any plan with serialized chains can't be reviewed
end-to-end without the real import. Cycle detection runs
regardless, but the edges themselves are invisible.

Shape:
  <new-1>  A
  <new-2>  B (blocked on <new-1>)
  <new-3>  C (blocked on <new-2>)
For edges resolving to existing DB tasks, render the real
short-ID in place of the <new-N> placeholder.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/import.go — dry-run branch threads each
  parsed task's resolved blockedBy (local refs + existing
  DB short IDs) into the ImportedTask result
- cmd/job/import.go — md renderer extends each row with
  the parenthetical when the list is non-empty
- Tests: dry-run of a plan with blockedBy edges surfaces
  them; dry-run with a blockedBy to an existing task
  renders the real ID, not a placeholder
data.title: F4 — Preview `blockedBy` edges in `import --dry-run`

data.description:
`note` puts the body preview on the verb line
(`Noted: <id> · N chars · "preview"`) while `done` and
`cancel` put title on the verb line and preview on a
sub-line (`Done: <id> "Title"\n  note: N chars · "preview"`).
Both shapes make sense per-verb but a programmatic reader
needs two regexes.

This is a design conversation, not a mechanical fix. Stop
and ask before implementing. Options:
(a) Normalize note to the verb-line-plus-sub-line form
    (a dummy sub-line when there's nothing to qualify).
(b) Normalize done/cancel to the single-line form for the
    cases where there's no title context worth preserving.
(c) Leave as-is; document the two shapes in AGENTS.md.
data.title: F5 — Align `-m` verb ack shapes (design)

data.description:
`list [parent] [all]` uses a literal-string positional for
the "include closed" toggle. It composes awkwardly with
the other flags: `list JxyAc all --mine` vs the cleaner
`list JxyAc --all --mine`.

Breaking change. In BUILD mode per CLAUDE.md that's fine,
but it is user-visible. Option: keep the positional
undocumented for one release as a graceful migration.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/list.go — BoolVar --all, drop (or undocument) the
  positional
- internal/job/tasks.go — showAll bool is already plumbed;
  only the cmd layer changes
- Tests: existing `list <parent> all` call sites migrate
  to --all; keep one asserting the positional still works
  if we go the soft-migration route
data.title: F6 — `list --all` flag replaces the `all` positional

data.note: Design decision: leave the two ack shapes as-is (note single-line, done/cancel two-line) and document them in AGENTS.md. Agents parsing output should use --format=json; the text shapes serve human readability.

Added -l/--label (StringArrayVarP, repeatable) to job add. RunAdd signature gains []string labels param; normalizeLabelNames + insertLabels called inside the existing tx; labeled event recorded atomically with created. Used StringArrayVarP (not StringSliceVarP) so comma-in-label validation actually fires.

extractTasksYAML now returns (string, bool, error); probe loop captures lastErr from yaml.Unmarshal. RunImport surfaces that error when no block matched, instead of the generic 'no YAML tasks: block found' message.

Added --grep <pattern> to job list: case-insensitive substring match on title, post-filter, composes with --label/--mine/--claimed-by. filterByGrep recurses so a parent node is kept if any descendant matches. No output (not the empty-list message) when --grep returns nothing.

Added BlockedBy []string to ImportedTask (json: blocked_by, omitempty). Dry-run branch resolves each parsedTask's blockedByResolved: local blockers get <new-N> placeholders, existing DB tasks get their real short ID. MD renderer appends '(blocked on X, Y)' parenthetical when non-empty.

Added --all BoolVar to job list. Positional 'all' still accepted silently for graceful migration. Use: string updated to 'list [parent]'; Long description updated to --all. Composes with parent scoping, --label, --mine, --claimed-by.

Implemented option (a): note ack now two-line form matching done/cancel. 'Noted: <id> "Title"\n  note: N chars · "preview"'. Fetches task title via GetTaskByShortID before RunNote (avoids signature change). Updated note_echo_test.go: new want strings, extractQuotedPreview now scans the note: sub-line.

data.description:
Five agent-facing ergonomics fixes drawn from the R1–R5
recommendations in project/2026-04-23-sonnet-feedback.md.

data.description:
When `status` is given an `<id>` argument, append the task
list for that subtree below the rollup summary — identical
to what `list <id>` would produce, without requiring a
second call. No filtering; for grep/label filtering the user
still calls `list` explicitly.

Shape:
  job status NpWZj
  NpWZj — CLI papercuts from 2026-04-23 session
    4 of 6 done · 0 blocked · 2 available
    Next: F5_id · Stale: none

  Tasks:
    - [x] F1_id  Add --label flag to `job add`
    - [ ] F5_id  Two-line note ack on success
    ...

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/status.go — when args[0] is set, call
  RunListFiltered for the subtree and append output below
  the summary block.
- internal/job/status.go — no changes needed; summary
  already scopes correctly.
- Tests: status <id> on a flat subtree shows both rollup
  and tree; status with no args is unchanged; status on a
  deep tree shows all levels (same depth default as list).

data.description:
Reopening a task is almost always followed immediately by
claiming it. Make this atomic by default; add --no-claim
for the rare case where someone else will work the task.

Shape:
  job reopen F5_id
  Reopened: F5_id "Two-line note ack"
    claimed by alice (until 2026-04-23 15:42)

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/reopen.go — after RunReopen succeeds, call
  RunClaim unless --no-claim is set. Append the claim
  confirmation line to output.
- cmd/job/reopen.go — add BoolVar for --no-claim flag.
- internal/job/tasks.go — no internal change required;
  the command layer calls both in sequence.
- Tests: reopen auto-claims by default; --no-claim skips
  the claim step and omits the claim output line; reopening
  an already-open task still fails (unchanged); output
  format includes the claim line when claimed.
data.title: R2 — `reopen` auto-claims; add `--no-claim` escape hatch

data.description:
Accept multiple IDs so context on several related tasks
can be fetched in one call.

Shape: variadic args, rendered sequentially separated by
a blank line. --format json returns a JSON array.

Fail behavior: first invalid ID returns an error and stops
(fail-fast). This can be relaxed to "all-errors" later if
needed, but fail-fast is simpler to implement and easier
to reason about.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/info.go — change ExactArgs(1) to MinimumNArgs(1);
  loop over args; blank-line separator between tasks.
- cmd/job/info.go — --format json wraps results in a JSON
  array.
- internal/job/tasks.go — RunInfo is unchanged; the loop
  is at the command layer.
- Tests: single ID (unchanged behavior); two IDs returns
  both; valid + invalid ID fails on the invalid one; JSON
  format produces an array; separator line appears between
  tasks in text output, not after the last.
data.title: R3 — Batch `job info <id> [id ...]`

data.description:
Tasks labeled `decision` represent questions that must be
answered before work can proceed. Today they are invisible
in status output — indistinguishable from normal open tasks.
Surfacing them in the status preamble (alongside Next: and
Stale:) gives agents and humans a reliable signal that a
human decision is pending.

Shape — new line in status preamble when any open task
carries the `decision` label:
  Next:     F5_id "Two-line note ack"
  Stale:    none
  Decision: D3_id "Choose auth strategy"

Multiple decision tasks: list all on separate lines.
Scoped status (status <id>): include only decision tasks
within that subtree.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/status.go — RunStatus: after computing
  Next and Stale, query for open tasks with label=decision
  scoped to the current subtree (or whole DB for unscoped).
  Populate a new DecisionTasks []TaskRef field on
  StatusSummary.
- internal/job/format.go — render Decision: lines in the
  preamble block. Empty slice → omit the section.
- Tests: decision-labeled open task surfaces; closed
  decision task does not; non-decision open task does not;
  scoped status only shows in-subtree decisions; multiple
  decision tasks each get a line.
data.title: R4 — Surface `decision`-labeled tasks in `job status`

data.description:
RunListFiltered now has 7 positional parameters. Each new
filter feature costs a signature change and ~20 caller
updates. A filter struct caps that cost permanently.

Shape:
