      ParentID       string
      Depth          int
      ShowAll        bool
      ClaimedByActor string
      Label          string
      GrepPattern    string
  }
  func RunListFiltered(db *sql.DB, f ListFilter) ([]*TaskNode, error)

Breaking change to the internal API — acceptable in build
mode with zero external users.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/tasks.go — replace the 7-arg signature;
  update the implementation (no behavioral change).
- All callers (~20 sites across 5 files):
  cmd/job/list.go, cmd/job/labels_test.go,
  cmd/job/short_flags_test.go, cmd/job/database_test.go,
  cmd/job/format_listparens_test.go — replace positional
  args with struct literals.
- Tests: full suite should pass without behavioral change.
  The test for the refactor is a green suite, not a new
  test case.
data.title: R5 — Replace RunListFiltered positional params with ListFilter struct

Scaffolded internal/web/ with five sub-packages — server (Config, New, Run), handlers (one file per view with shared Deps), templates (//go:embed html/** + FuncMap), assets (//go:embed css/js/fonts + http.FileServer), render (ActorColor stub per DESIGN.md S65/L55). Routes mounted per vision §6.4. Deleted stale internal/server/server.go stub (no importers). go build / vet / fmt / test all clean.

Shipped cmd/job/serve.go (cobra command, --bind flag, loopback default, SIGINT via signal.NotifyContext, prints http://<bound-addr>/). Refactored internal/web/server to split Listen/Serve so the command binds synchronously and reports the OS-assigned port when --bind 127.0.0.1:0 is used. Tests: resolveServeAddr default/override/explicit-0.0.0.0 regression fence; server.Listen binds loopback + rejects malformed addr; server.Serve responds and shuts down on ctx cancel. Skipped README/docs update — handlers still 501, so the command isn't user-ready; whoever ships dARuR/skc56 (the first real view) should add the README entry then.

Shipped fingerprinted asset pipeline. internal/web/assets: BuildManifest walks the embedded FS, hashes each file with SHA-256 (first 8 hex chars), and maps logical paths (css/dashboard.css) ↔ fingerprinted URLs (/static/css/dashboard.<hash>.css). Manifest.Handler serves only fingerprinted paths with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; unhashed or wrong-hash paths 404, so a stale bookmark can never win against a fresh build. Wired in routes.go (switched mount from /assets/ to /static/ per task spec; old FileServer helper removed). Tests cover manifest build + determinism, immutable-cache header, unhashed 404, wrong-hash 404. End-to-end smoke confirmed via go build + curl.

Followup for 3gWDe: templates.FuncMap should take a *assets.Manifest so {{asset "css/dashboard.css"}} resolves to the fingerprinted URL. The server will need to thread the manifest from NewMux into templates — simplest path is to build the manifest once in NewMux and pass it both to the /static/ handler and to a template registry in Deps.

Shipped shared chrome. internal/web/templates: Engine clones a layout+partials base once, then parses each page under html/pages/ atop its own clone — per-page "content" blocks can coexist without collisions. Files: layout.html.tmpl (frame with dark-default data-theme), partials/header.html.tmpl (tabs: Home/Plan/Actors/Log, search with /-shortcut hint, bell, theme toggle), partials/footer.html.tmpl (metric strip, scrubber pill, animated heartbeat), pages/home.html.tmpl (placeholder body so GET / renders real HTML). {{asset "path"}} helper resolves through the manifest — missing asset errors the render loudly rather than silently emitting a broken <link>. dashboard.css: DESIGN.md color/type/space/radius/motion tokens as CSS custom properties, baseline reset, chrome styling. app.js: theme toggle (localStorage + prefers-color-scheme), /-focus search, active-tab derivation from pathname. API:
  New(db, pollInterval) *Broadcaster
  (*Broadcaster).Start(ctx) error       — blocks until ctx cancel
  (*Broadcaster).Subscribe() (ch, cancel) — idempotent cancel
  (*Broadcaster).Dropped() int64        — telemetry hook

Implementation: Start wraps job.RunTail(ctx, db, "", pollInterval, fanout) — one goroutine per process, not per subscriber. Fanout is a non-blocking send into per-subscriber buffered channels (DefaultBufferSize=64, DefaultPollInterval=1s matching job tail). A slow subscriber's buffer filling drops the event for just them; the rest keep flowing. Reconnect with ?since=<last_id> is the recovery path (sibling task owns /events endpoint). Drop count is aggregated in Dropped() for future /metrics exposure; first drop and every 64th drop log a line.

Cancel closes the subscriber's channel so consumers see a closed-channel signal rather than an infinite silent channel. sync.Once on cancel + the select-on-s.cancel guard in fanout make double-cancel safe and prevent send-on-closed. closeAll fires on Start shutdown to drain all subscribers.

data.note:
Shipped /events handler. Two code paths on the same endpoint:

JSON replay (default, no Accept: text/event-stream): GET /events?since=N&actor=X&task=Y&label=Z&type=T&limit=M returns a JSON array of events with id > since, with the four filters AND-composed, capped at limit (default 500).

SSE (Accept: text/event-stream): same query params; splices a backfill (events in (sinceID, cutoff]) into a live tail from the broadcaster, where cutoff is the Subscription.LastID captured at Subscribe time — so the live channel dedups any overlap against the backfill automatically. Headers: text/event-stream + no-cache + X-Accel-Buffering: no, with an immediate Flush after WriteHeader so http.Client.Do returns without waiting for the first frame (common SSE pitfall). Frame shape: id: N\nevent: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n.

Handler plumbing changes:
- NewMux(ctx, cfg) now threads ctx so the broadcaster's Start goroutine is tied to server lifetime; Listen/New/Run signatures updated. Broadcaster is nil when cfg.DB is nil (keeps the server unit tests usable without a real DB). Events handler returns 503 when the broadcaster is nil and SSE was requested.
- handlers.Deps gains Broadcaster *broadcast.Broadcaster.

Broadcaster API tweaks alongside this task:
- Subscribe() now returns Subscription{Events, LastID, Cancel} so consumers can snapshot the cutoff atomically with registration.
- Broadcaster.Start seeds lastID from job.GetMaxEventID so the first poll doesn't re-deliver every pre-existing event.
- Exported job.GetEventsAfterID + job.GetMaxEventID (previously unexported helpers).

Tests: JSON fallback returns array + Content-Type application/json; ?since filters by id; ?actor filter scopes; SSE with no broadcaster returns 503; SSE end-to-end via httptest.NewServer — subscribe, create event after Subscribe lands, verify one frame with id:/event:/data: shape and the task title in the payload. All handler tests run under -race.

Followup for the remaining Phase 3 tasks:
- The reconnect path on the client side: EventSource auto-reconnects and sends Last-Event-ID header; I'll plumb that into sinceID extraction so the frontend subscribes without explicit ?since.
- label filter in the SSE live loop currently does a per-event job.GetLabelsForTaskIDs — fine for low event rates, but O(events) queries. Worth a per-subscription label cache if this becomes hot.

Documented /events as a stable API surface in README.md.

Core code path (JSON replay + SSE stream) already shipped with xn1Kf. This task was the doc half: new 'Web dashboard' section near the end of README covering job serve usage, the URL map, and a /events API reference. API docs include the parameter table (since, limit, actor, task, label, type — AND-composed, all optional), the event wire shape, the detail-field forward-compatibility note, and two example curl invocations (SSE backfill + live-tail; JSON one-shot).

Also tightened the contributors section: the reference to internal/server/ (stub I deleted in the Phase 2 commit) is replaced with a real description of the internal/web/ subpackage tree.

Shipped assets/js/live.js — <live-region src="/events?…"> WebComponent that owns the dashboard's SSE connection.

Responsibilities:
- Opens EventSource; registers listeners for the known event_type vocabulary (created, claimed, released, done, reopened, canceled, noted, blocked, unblocked, labeled, unlabeled, moved, edited, heartbeat) so server frames with event: <name> get picked up. Falls through to 'message' for any server frame that omits event:.
- Dispatches two custom events on the element: 'event' (detail = parsed server event) and 'connection' (detail = connecting|connected|reconnecting|offline). Views wire their own DOM updates to 'event' — this module stays ignorant of Log/Home/Actors shape.
- Persists the last seen event id to localStorage under jobs.live.lastEventId and appends ?since=<id> on reconnect, so the dashboard resumes across full page reloads — complements EventSource's built-in Last-Event-ID for intra-page reconnects.
- Renders the footer heartbeat ([data-heartbeat]) from a 1s tick: 'connected' → 'last event Ns ago', 'reconnecting…', etc. Also sets data-state on the element so CSS can color-shift if desired.

Mount: layout.html.tmpl now includes <live-region src="/events"></live-region> + <script src={{asset js/live.js}}> right after chrome.js, so every page gets the live stream without per-page wiring.

Tests: templates render exposes live-region markup and the fingerprinted js/live.js URL (fence against an unhashed reference slipping in).

Caveat: this is vanilla JS that I haven't exercised in a browser. The server-side wiring is covered by the existing /events + broadcaster tests, but the client-side registration, reconnect, and heartbeat label updates need a human eye on the dashboard with the dev tools console open. Worth opening /log, editing a task from the CLI, and watching the heartbeat timestamp tick.

Shipped log live-tail. Layout exposes {{block "live-region-src"}}/events{{end}} so pages can scope the SSE subscription; Log page overrides with .EventsURL built from the page's current filter state. Server-side SSE filter already matches the same params, so the live stream only delivers events that satisfy the current filter — client filtering isn't needed.

New assets/js/log-live.js:
- Self-guarded (looks for .c-log; no-ops on pages without the log list).
- Listens for 'event' on <live-region>.
- Builds a .c-log-row with the same markup as the server template (c-log-row--<type>, time, actor avatar + link, verb, id pill, note extracted from detail via the same done→note / noted→text / canceled→note rule, c-row-link overlay).

New internal/web/handlers/log.go.eventsURL builds the filter-scoped /events URL; exposed on LogPageData.EventsURL for the template override.

Tests: TestLog_LiveRegionSrc_ReflectsFilters pins the dependency — no filters → /events, actor=alice → /events?actor=alice. Covers the full SSR + filter-threading chain.

Split the heartbeat + connection-state rendering in live.js:
  [data-heartbeat]   → 'last event Ns ago' when connected, 'reconnecting…' / 'offline' / 'connecting…' otherwise. The 'is work still happening?' signal.
  [data-connection]  → 'Connected' / 'Reconnecting' / 'Offline' / 'Connecting'. The 'is the stream alive?' signal.
  Both carry dataset.state so CSS can color-shift per state if desired.
  When the server is slow (connected but quiet), heartbeat shows an aging timestamp while connection still reads 'Connected' — exactly the disagreement a viewer wants to see.

Added navigator.onLine listeners (online / offline window events) to distinguish 'your laptop's wifi dropped' from 'server briefly unreachable'. EventSource errors normally surface either as 'reconnecting' indiscriminately; the browser-level offline signal lets us show 'offline' explicitly. Listeners are torn down in disconnectedCallback so the element is safe to remove and re-add.

1s tick keeps the 'last event Ns ago' string fresh between arrivals.

Phase 3 test sweep. Full suite now runs clean under -race.

Broadcaster:
- Added TestBroadcaster_Fanout_ManySubscribersManyEvents: 20 subscribers × 50 events; verifies no subscriber sees zero events and logs any shortfalls (buffer drops are a tolerated outcome, silent starvation is not). Covers the concurrent fanout path that single-subscriber tests can't exercise.
- Existing tests cover: subscribe delivers new events, lastID seed prevents pre-boot flood, multi-subscriber fanout, idempotent cancel, slow-subscriber backpressure, context cancel shuts loop down.

SSE handler (new events_sse_test.go):
- BackfillReplaysSinceID: seeds 3 events, subscribes with ?since=0, verifies all 3 frames arrive.
- BackfillThenLive_NoDuplicates: opens stream after one seed event, fires a live event post-subscribe, asserts no id appears twice across the backfill/live handoff (this is the dedup fence — Subscription.LastID is the contract that prevents duplicates).
- ReconnectWithLastEventID: resumes via ?since=<middle-id>, asserts only events with id > middle come through. Models the EventSource reconnect path (server accepts ?since= or Last-Event-ID header equivalent).
- FilterScopesLiveStream: subscribes with ?actor=alice, creates events for alice + bob, verifies only alice frames arrive — covers the filter pipe through the live channel.

Helpers: readSSE parses frames from an io.Reader into an id/event/data struct so tests can assert on structured fields rather than scraping raw strings. openSSE opens a keep-alive request with a cancelable context so tests can close cleanly.

data.description:
Three cosmetic refinements to the plan view shipped on top of p4-ssr:
- colors.js skips progress-bar injection on rows with status done or canceled (redundant with the pill).
- colors.js skips injection when the subtree has nothing done and the row isn't active — a dormant todo with 0/N done adds noise. isActive checks the rollup class, so a todo parent with a claimed grandchild still shows the bar.
- CSS collapse rule broadens to hide everything inside .c-plan-row__title except the title-line, so the 'N of M tasks done' text (.c-plan-row__progress-text) folds away when the row is collapsed.
Also: PlanNode.Collapsible now covers 'has description or children', so leaf tasks with descriptions are collapsible too and done leaves fold up their description by default. Prototype/js/colors.js kept in sync.
data.title: Progress-bar display rules and collapse hiding

data.note: See description. Shipped in a single cosmetic commit on top of p4-ssr. Verified via the full test suite (the handler-side Collapsible change has dedicated tests; the JS and CSS hide rules are manual-verify only — no browser-test harness in this project).

Every c-plan-row now carries id="task-<short>". Blocker pills switch from /tasks/<short> to #task-<short>, keeping the reader on the plan document. Blocker pills also render title="<blocker title>" so hovering reveals what the blocker is without navigation — useful when the blocker currently sits in a collapsed subtree. :target CSS reuses the existing .c-plan-row--selected treatment (raised background + 3px primary stripe on the left). Three new handler tests guard the anchor href, row id, and title attribute; two pre-existing rollup tests updated to use a new assertRowHasClass helper that tolerates attribute reshuffles. Expand-ancestors-on-hashchange behavior lands with E2ffo's collapse module.

Implements plan-collapse.js. Click .c-plan-row__disclosure flips data-collapsed on the row and updates aria-expanded / aria-label on the button. Per-task state persists to localStorage under jobs.plan.collapse as {shortID: true|false}; absence means 'follow SSR default'. ?expand=<short>,<short> on the URL force-expands those rows on load and persists them, so shareable links land on the intended branch. hashchange handler walks ancestors of the #task-<short> target and force-expands each, so blocker-pill clicks (from kTfXu) reveal the target even when it sits in a collapsed done-subtree. Graceful degradation: storage failures (privacy mode / quota) are swallowed; the page still works, the override just doesn't survive reload. prototype/js/plan-collapse.js mirrors the production module and prototype/plan.html loads it. Manual-verify only — no browser test harness. Full Go suite still green.

Implements ?label=<name> on /plan. Handler parses the query param, loads the unfiltered forest first (so the labels strip stays stable across switches), gathers the labels of currently-open tasks (done parents kept for context but their historical labels excluded from the strip — otherwise it ballooned to 80+ pills against the real DB), then applies the filter in memory using the already-batched labels map. Strip renders each label as a pill link to /plan?label=<name>; active label gets c-label-pill--active; clear link appears only when a filter is active. Empty match shows the existing c-plan-empty placeholder. Filter semantics match job.filterByLabel: keeps matching tasks + ancestor chain for context; unlabeled descendants of matches are filtered out. Four new handler tests guard the filter behavior, the chip rendering, the empty state, and the no-filter case. UX note: real DB shows ~61 distinct labels on open tasks — strip is functional but heavy; cap-by-frequency or dropdown is a future polish.

data.description:
Refines the labels filter shipped in PwNlo:
- Strip drops to top-5 labels by open-task frequency, plus any selected labels not in the top-5 (so a selection never orphans).
- Multi-select via comma-separated ?label=foo,bar (URL form). Filter logic is OR — tasks tagged with any selected label, plus ancestor chain.
- Leftmost 'All' pill clears the filter and is active when no labels are selected. Replaces the inline 'clear' text link.
- Inline label pills on task rows become clickable <a> links; click adds the label to the selection (no-op if already selected). Strip pills toggle in/out.
- Selected pills flip from ringed to filled (label-color background, white text). New CSS rule for .c-label-pill--active.
No JS needed — every pill href is server-pre-computed.

data.description:
Two related Log-view ergonomics issues observed at ~893 events:
- Page just overflows into normal page-scroll, so the filter bar scrolls away. Needs either a sticky filter bar or a constrained scroll container so filters stay reachable.
- SSR currently renders ALL events for the task tree in one shot. Want pagination — likely server-side cursor (?before=<event_id>&limit=N) with infinite-scroll or load-more, mirroring the SSE replay shape (?since=, ?limit= already supported by p3-replay).
data.title: Log view: scroll and pagination

data.note: Implements multi-select labels with All pill. Strip is top-5 labels by open-task frequency, plus any selected labels not in the top-5 (so a selection never orphans). Comma-separated ?label=foo,bar URL form (each label QueryEscape'd individually so commas stay literal). OR-semantic filter — task kept if it carries any selected label or any descendant does. All pill leftmost, points at /plan, --active when no selection. Strip pills toggle in/out of selection (sorted alphabetically for canonical URLs). Inline label pills on task rows are now <a> links; click adds the label to current selection (no-op if already in). New CSS: c-label-pill--active flips to filled (label-color background, white text) and c-label-pill--all uses neutral primary tint with caps-lockup font. Adopts the existing c-filter-bar / c-filter-bar__group / c-filter-bar__label structure from the Log view for visual consistency. Also fixes a regression: paintProgress in colors.js was painting progress bars + text on leaf rows that became Collapsible due to having a description (no children) — now requires an actual c-plan-subtree sibling, with notes-group correctly skipped. Eight new handler tests cover all the semantics.

Adds OpenTaskLabelFreqs to the job package — one SQL query, returns label name → open-task count. Log handler now caps the Label chip strip to top 10 by that frequency, with the active label always included even if it would fall below the cap (so an active filter never orphans). Two new handler tests guard the cap and the active-label-included rule. The Plan view's pickStripLabels does the same thing in-memory; that one stays forest-walk-based since Plan already has the forest in scope, but both views agree on the underlying definition of 'currently in active circulation.'

Two pieces shipped together: (1) /log scroll: .c-log becomes the scroll container itself via flex: 1 + min-height: 0 + overflow: auto, so the filter bar above stays put while only the rows scroll within their card. No JS, no max-height — leans on the existing .main flex column and 100vh .page grid. (2) Pagination: LogFilters gains Before (event-id cursor) and Limit (default 200). loadLogEvents pages after sort+filter, returns hasMore. Footer 'load older →' anchor in .c-log-more (position: sticky; bottom: 0) carries href=/log?before=<oldestID> with all other filters preserved. Each page is independent — browser back works, URLs are shareable. Sort comparator now tiebreaks on event id desc so events sharing a Unix second are still deterministically newest-first (was an ordering bug masked at low event volumes). Three new handler tests cover the cap, the cursor pagination, and the no-more-link case. SQL push-down for the limit/before is a future optimization; for now we still load all events and page in memory — fine at the current 893 events.

Implements ?show=active|archived|all on /plan. Default is active: roots whose subtree carries any open work; archived hides them. archived shows roots whose entire subtree is done/canceled; all shows both. Three Active/Archived/All tabs are now real links — each preserves the current ?label= selection so changing archive mode doesn't drop the user's label filter. Label pills (strip + inline) preserve ?show= symmetrically. Strip composition is now view-aware: in archived/all, labels of done tasks count toward the top-N (otherwise the strip is empty in archived view). New planURL helper is the single source of URL truth for both label and show params; canonical sort + per-segment escape avoids double-encoding commas. Six new handler tests cover all three modes, tab markup, and parameter preservation across switches.

Implements Plan view live updates via SSE. New plan-live.js subscribes to live-region's 'event' custom event and, on each incoming event, debounces (750ms) then refetches the current /plan URL, parses out the c-section[aria-label='Plan'] (and the c-filter-bar — label frequencies and the top-N composition shift as tasks open and close), and swaps both into the DOM. After the swap it re-runs the idempotent JS the layout would normally trigger at DOMContentLoaded: JobsColors.paint + paintProgress, and a new JobsPlanCollapse.applyStored that re-applies localStorage to the fresh DOM. Self-guarded — module is a no-op if the page has no plan section. plan-collapse.js gains a window.JobsPlanCollapse export so plan-live can re-hydrate. The fragment-swap design ships in ~30 lines vs ~300 for surgical row-mutation; v1 trade-off acknowledging that the plan tree is structurally too varied (insert under any parent's subtree, claim flips status pill plus rollup of every ancestor, note adds a row inside a collapsible details group, block adds a sub-row) to mutate inline cleanly. Network cost is small at this scale; future polish could push to surgical updates if needed. prototype/js/plan-live.js mirrors production.

Implements arrow-first keyboard navigation for /plan in plan-keyboard.js. Roving tabindex pattern: at any moment exactly one .c-plan-row is in tab order; arrows move the cursor row-by-row. Bindings: ArrowDown/j next visible row, ArrowUp/k prev, ArrowLeft collapse-or-parent, ArrowRight expand-or-first-child, Space/Enter toggle, Home/End jump to first/last. Visible-row computation via offsetParent !== null (collapsed subtrees use display: none). Self-guarded — bails if the page has no plan section, if focus is in an input/textarea/contenteditable, or if a modifier key is held (so browser shortcuts and filter typing aren't trampled). Collapse changes write to the same jobs.plan.collapse localStorage key plan-collapse owns, so reload picks up the same state regardless of which surface (click, hashchange, keyboard) drove the change. Vim aliases included for muscle memory but arrows are the documented primary — Dvorak users get a first-class experience. Focus ring uses the global :focus-visible rule (primary color outline + soft glow). prototype/js/plan-keyboard.js mirrors production.

Adds two end-to-end test passes for the plan view: (1) TestPlan_FilterComposition is the broad table-driven check that ?label= and ?show= compose correctly. Nine cases name the visible roots each combination should produce; the test asserts every other root is absent. Catches regressions where a future filter short-circuits the wrong branch in the chain. ?at= time-travel composition lands with p8 and adds rows to this table. (2) TestPlan_RecursiveRenderingStructure exercises depth-3 nesting and confirms the recursive plan-node template produces matching nested c-plan-subtree wrappers, indentation-correct ids, depth-aware heading classes (root → t-heading-lg, depth-1 → t-heading-md, deeper → default), and per-row disclosure presence: root has one (description), child has one (children), bare grand-leaf doesn't. Skipped a true golden-file framework — the rendered output carries volatile bits (relative timestamps, random short ids, event ids) that would need a sanitization layer to compare reliably. Existing 30+ assertion-based tests already cover the per-feature behavior; the structural test gives equivalent regression coverage without the brittleness.

Shipped internal/web/signals package: Compute() returns Activity (60-bucket per-minute histogram split by done/claim/create/block), NewlyBlocked (count + recent edges in last 10m, threshold 5), LongestClaim (longest-running active claim, threshold = 30m TTL), OldestTodo (oldest available unblocked task, threshold 7d). Each alarm signal carries a 0..1 Progress value for the ambient underline. Aligned with prototype (activity histogram over the earlier 'idle actors' phrasing, per user confirm). 15 tests covering empty DBs, windowing, bucketing, event-type split, item cap, threshold saturation, and exclusion rules.

Shipped Home-view signal cards. Handler computes signals, formats into view structs (durations via render.ClaimDuration, ages via render.RelativeTime, progress % ints), passes to home.html.tmpl which renders four c-signal-card articles matching the prototype: activity histogram (60 bars scaled against busiest minute + legend totals), newly blocked (count + context line + --progress), longest claim (duration + actor + task link + --progress), oldest todo (age + task link + --progress). Empty states render em-dash + muted text. Added render.ClaimDuration helper for minute+second precision. 9 handler integration tests + 11 ClaimDuration cases + updated templates/server tests for new data shape. Visual check via curl: 4 cards, 4 underlines, real activity histogram rendering with --h percentages.

Shipped Active claims panel + live-ticker JS. Handler loadActiveClaims query joins tasks with their most-recent 'claimed' event to get true claim-start (heartbeat-proof), ordered oldest-first. HomePageData.ActiveClaims wired into home.html.tmpl as a c-panel with one c-panel-row per in-flight claim (actor avatar link, id pill, title, idle meta, stretched row link). Empty state shows 'No active claims' with '0 in flight' meta. Client: home-live.js ticks [data-claim-idle] cells every 1s from [data-claimed-at] (mirrors Go render.ClaimDuration formatting exactly); on any live-region event, debounced 750ms fetch of / and replaces the signals grid + claims panel in place (plan-live.js pattern). Wired into layout.html.tmpl. Tests: 4 new handler cases (empty state, row per claim with task details excluded for done tasks, oldest-first ordering, data-claimed-at presence). Visual check via curl shows panel rendering with live claim and fingerprinted home-live.js script.

Shipped Recent completions panel. loadRecentCompletions handler query joins done/canceled events with their tasks, LIMIT RecentCompletionsLimit (10) ordered newest-first, then reverses in-memory to render oldest→newest (natural timeline order matching prototype). Deleted tasks excluded via inner join on deleted_at IS NULL. Template wraps Active claims + Recent completions in a c-grid-cols-4 container (two cells filled for now, remaining cells for BgpKq blocked strip + future Available panel). home-live.js already handles the full-page refetch via 'event' on live-region — extended it to also swap the [data-home-recent] region. Tests: 4 new handler cases (empty state, done+canceled both render / noted excluded, oldest→newest order, LIMIT trims oldest keeping the 10 newest). Visual check via curl: 10 real completions rendering with actor + id pill + title + '1h 5m'-style age; 'last 10' meta in header.

Shipped Blocked strip panel. loadBlockedStrip single query JOINs blocks→tasks(blocked)+tasks(blocker), filters: blocked task must not be done/canceled/deleted, blocker must not be done/deleted (canceled blockers have their edges deleted outright in cancel.go). Flattened rows grouped by blocked_id in Go preserving insertion order from ORDER BY t.created_at. BlockedStripLimit=20 caps distinct blocked tasks (not edges). Template renders c-panel-row--stacked variant: id pill + stacked (title + 'waiting on X, Y, Z' meta with comma-joined blocker id-pills linking to their tasks). home-live.js swaps [data-home-blocked] on refetch. Tests: 5 cases — empty state, 2 tasks with shared/distinct blockers, done blocker resolves the block, done blocked task excluded, multiple blockers render as multiple links. Visual check: real dashboard shows 14 waiting tasks with multi-blocker rows rendering comma-separated correctly.

data.note:
Landed BuildSubway end-to-end in internal/web/signals/subway.go.

Public entry: BuildSubway(ctx, db, now) — DB shim around buildSubway(w *graphWorld) which is the testable pure core. Uses existing pickFocals from graph.go (same package, no port needed — handoff note's 'reuse as-is' applies). Composes collectLines (L=2) + computeFork + applyWindow (N=2), then assembles:
- Nodes: fork ancestors → for each line, anchor → visible stops. Deduped by ShortID. State maps claimed→Active, done/canceled→Done, else Todo. URL = /tasks/{shortID}.
- Edges: Branch (open) or BranchClosed (anchor.openBlockers > 0) from fork divergence to each line anchor; Flow within each line (anchor → first stop, then between consecutive Stop items, skipping over elision items); Blocker for explicit blocks between two rendered non-anchor nodes (skipping pairs already covered by BranchClosed and skipping done/canceled blockers).

Implemented LayoutSubway in internal/web/render/subway_layout.go. All 9 of Ya7ea's red snapshot tests now pass.

Algorithm:
- Rows: one row per line, top-to-bottom in seed order. With a fork, the LCA chain sits inline with line index (n-1)/2 — top for 2 lines, middle for 3 lines, low-middle for 4+ (per design doc 'typically the middle line for three lines, the top for two').

data.note:
Fixed both blocker-edge bugs in internal/web/signals/subway.go.

(1) Flow-with-Blocker dedupe: when a Blocker edge covers a (from, to) pair, the Flow edge for the same pair is now suppressed. Implementation: blocker emission moved before the flow loop; a blockerCovers map is built first; the flow loop skips any pair already covered. Without this dedupe the Flow's arrowhead reads as if the dashed amber blocker line itself has an arrow.

(2) Nearest-blocker only: each rendered blocker now emits at most one Blocker edge, to its nearest rendered blocked stop (smallest preorder position). Subsequent blocks by the same blocker are transitive — drawing them separately would visually imply that intermediate stops carry the constraint (the 'Live updates blocks Tests' false reading from the screenshot).

Iteration order is deterministic: candidates accumulate in node-render order, blocker keys are stored in first-seen order, blocked tasks per blocker are sorted by preorder position.

Two regression tests added in subway_test.go (red->green confirmed):
- TestBuildSubway_BlockerEdge_SuppressesAdjacentFlow
- TestBuildSubway_BlockerEdge_OnlyNearestBlocked

Existing edge-case tests still pass — the previous BlockerEdge_BetweenStops case (D blocks F, non-adjacent) and DoneBlocker case behave identically under the new logic.

Browser-checked: home view returns HTTP 200, my current single-claim state renders correctly. The original actors-view bug isn't reproducible from this focal scope, but the structural tests cover both failure modes.

Decision: L=1, N=2 for the production home view. The original spec defaulted to L=2/N=2 'worth tuning against real screenshots.' Once we shipped the rendered subway against real data, the wider preview made rows feel cluttered (Tests appearing 4 stops past the focal because lookahead-touched stops anchor their own ±N windows). L=1 gives a tighter 'next 1 leaf forward' preview while keeping ±2 sibling windows around any visible node. The design doc's six reference scenarios are still authored against L=2 — tests that exercise those shapes pass 2 explicitly via buildSubwayWith; production code uses subwayLookahead=1.

Decision: dashed amber (the existing c-graph-edge--blocker / c-graph-edge--closed treatment) covers both sequential-phase blocks and explicit blocks between rendered stops. No distinct glyph needed — the dashed style alone reads correctly in practice.

Decision: no phase labels above lines. The line anchor node already carries the phase title as a label below the disc, so a header would duplicate. The only marginal case is a single-row mid-stream view where the cluster root has dropped out — interesting idea but not worth the redundancy and vertical-space cost in the common case.

Decision: hide done branches entirely (current spec behavior). Vertical space is at a premium on the home view; a 'Phase 1 ✓' historical indicator at the fork would burn a row-equivalent of space for context that's already implicit in 'what's happening now' framing.

Decision: defer truncation. Allow the canvas to grow vertically for now; with L=1 in production the row count stays small in practice. Revisit if we hit 6+ simultaneous rows in the wild and the page feels unwieldy.

(was `list`). `info` and `list` continue to work as aliases but
stop printing the "prefer the canonical form" note.

Why: matches `git show`, `kubectl describe`, and the rest of
the verb-shaped CLI vocabulary (claim, done, tail). Help text
carries the convention; aliases stay quiet.

Drops these trailing notes:
  - "note: `job show` is an alias for `job info`; prefer the canonical form."
  - "note: `job ls` is an alias for `job list`; prefer the canonical form."
data.title: Make `show` and `ls` canonical; silence the alias warnings

data.description:
`tree <id>` produces the same output as `ls <id>`. Shell-fluent
users reach for `tree` when they want hierarchy; `ls` already
returns the full subtree, so this is a name-only alias for now.

If indented rendering becomes important later, `tree` can
diverge into its own renderer; for today the alias removes
one rejected-command friction without splitting implementation.
data.title: Add `tree` as an alias of `ls`

data.description:
When the node has children, render them inline under a
`Children:` header, in the same shape as `ls` output:
`- [ ] \`shortID\` Title (claim/blocker/labels)`.

Cap:
  - ≤ 10 children: render every child as one line.
  - > 10 children: render `Children: N (use 'job ls <id>' to see all)`.

Example:
  Children:
    - [x] `x81Op` GET /actors — column layout SSR (labels: actors, web)
    - [x] `hgSC7` GET /actors/<name> — single-actor view (labels: actors, web)
    - [ ] `B645R` Live updates (claimed by claude, 28m left)
    - [ ] `oPR2R` Tests (blocked on hgSC7, x81Op)

Why: closes the loop where `show` sends users to `ls` to
discover the same information they came to `show` for.
data.title: `show <id>` lists children inline as a markdown checklist

data.description:
Keep the existing scriptable signal as the first line
("Claimed: X 'Title' (expires in 30m)"), then follow with the
full `show` output. Same flow for `claim-next` and
`done --claim-next`.

Why: claiming is the moment the user wants the briefing.
Folds the universal `claim X && show X` pattern into a single
call. Scripts grepping for "Claimed:" keep working.
data.title: `claim <id>` prints the `show` briefing after the one-liner

data.description:
Add a behavior note to `ls --help`:

  When given a parent, `ls` returns the full subtree under
  that parent (not just direct children). Combine with
  --label, --mine, --claimed-by, --grep to filter.

Why: the current help is silent on recursion depth, leaving
users to infer it from the filter-shaped flags.
data.title: `ls --help`: document subtree-recursion behavior

data.description:
Add a one-line tip to `done --help`:

  Tip: pass --claim-next to atomically close this task and
  claim the next available leaf, collapsing the work loop
  into one call.

Why: the flag exists today but is invisible to anyone who
hasn't read the full --help. Surfacing it turns it into a
reflex.
data.title: `done --help`: surface the `--claim-next` close-and-advance flag

data.description:
Add a tip to `claim --help`:

  Tip: see `claim-next` for "find and claim the next available
  leaf in one step" — and `done --claim-next` for the
  close-and-advance loop.

Why: same surfacing problem as `done`. The two-step
`done X && claim Y` flow is what users discover by default;
the single-call versions should be one help page away.
data.title: `claim --help`: point at `claim-next` and `done --claim-next`

Each view handler accepts ?at and renders the state of
the world at that event. Implemented as a filter on
event replay up to and including that event id.


[2026-04-26 08:05] Scope narrowed (2026-04-26 Opus session, agreed with ben).

Original scope had this task implementing ?at on every server-side view via a state reducer. After auditing real event payloads (every state-affecting event carries sufficient detail; auto-cascades are materialized as their own events; edited carries old_title/new_title, moved carries old/new sort_order), we committed to JS-side reduction for stateful views.

This task now covers ONLY: /log, /actors, and /actors/{name} accept ?at=<event_id> as an upper-bound event filter — events with id > at are excluded from the rendered list (event id == at is included). These are event-window views, not state snapshots, so the implementation is a SQL clause, not a reducer.

Time-travel for /, /plan (and friends) is handled entirely client-side by the JS reducer in LCT5C. Home/Plan handlers are NOT touched here.

Edge cases:
- ?at >= max(event.id): render as live, no banner.
- ?at malformed or non-numeric: 400.
- ?at <= 0 or below earliest event: render empty (no events match).

The history banner is JS-only — rendered by the scrubber UI when it sets ?at. Cold-load ?at= URLs render as live first and then JS folds back on hydration; the brief flash is accepted in trade for not threading a synthetic 'now' through every render helper.

Implemented ?at upper-bound event filter on /log and /actors only.

Server-side scope (final, after two narrowing rounds with ben):
- /log: At/AtInvalid added to LogFilters; handler returns 400 on AtInvalid; loadLogEvents pre-clamps the event slice to id <= At before per-event filtering, so the 'showing N of M events' counter is also at-scoped.
- /actors: handler reads ?at via parseAtParam (shared helper); 400 on invalid; loadActorColumns now takes atUpperBound and applies WHERE e.id <= ? on the event walk; IsClaim/ClaimCount derived from a per-task currentClaimer map updated through the walk (claimed sets, released/done/canceled/claim_expired/reopened clear) instead of reading the live tasks.claimed_by column.

Out of scope (deferred to JS reducer in LCT5C / never):
- /, /plan, /labels/{name}, /tasks/{id}, /tasks/{id}/peek, /actors/{name} — all live-only on the server. Time-travel for stateful views is JS-side (confirmed with ben: /actors/{name} and /tasks/{id} stay live-only).
- The history banner is also JS-only — rendered client-side when the scrubber sets ?at.

[2026-04-26 08:05] Caching hint for the replay buffer (from 2026-04-26 Opus session).

The reducer is a forward-fold of event deltas; events carry old_* fields (old_title, old_desc, old_sort_order, was_status, was_claimed_by, etc.) so reverse-fold is also exact. That makes a doubly-linked frame cache the natural structure:

- Keep the head frame (snapshot of live state at page load).
- Snapshot every N events as we replay (start with N=50; tune later).
- For any target ?at, replay forward or backward from the nearest snapshot.

Tick-by-tick scrubbing then replays a handful of events; arbitrary jumps cost <= N/2 events. Avoids the naive 'replay from genesis every tick' pattern that would chew up CPU on long-running databases.

Initial frame at scrubber load = the live SSR DOM state captured into the reducer's data model on hydration.

[2026-04-26 08:22] Caching strategy revised after auditing event payloads.

Original plan was a doubly-linked cache exploiting old_*/was_* fields for exact reverse-fold. That's not actually feasible:
- done events do not carry was_status, so we cannot distinguish a previously-claimed task from a previously-available one when rewinding.
- claim --force does not carry was_claimed_by on the new claimed event, so we cannot restore the overridden prior claimer.
- released and claim_expired payloads also lack the prior expires_at value.

So the cache is forward-only:
- Frame cache holds (eventId -> Frame) snapshots.
- Public API: frameAt(target). Looks up nearest cached snapshot <= target, then replays forward to target. Snapshots are taken every N events during replay (N=10 in v1; tune later).
- Head frame (current live state) is captured at hydration from a server-provided JSON island and pinned in cache.
- Genesis snapshot (empty world) is also pinned; first-time replays start from there if no closer snapshot exists.

Backward navigation: 'go back one tick' costs at most N events of forward replay from the nearest snapshot. With N=10, tick scrubbing is bounded. For arbitrary jumps the cost scales with how far we are from any cached snapshot, but as the user scrubs through a region snapshots accumulate, so revisits are cheap.

This avoids any schema change to the events table and keeps the reducer one-directional (simpler to reason about and test).

[2026-04-26 08:32] Reverse-fold is back on the table after commit 915916d added prior-state breadcrumbs (was_status, was_claimed_by, was_expires_at) to done/claimed/released/cancel/claim_expired events. Strategy revised:

Doubly-linked frame cache:
- Snapshot every N events (start with N=50; tune later).
- Forward navigation: replay forward from the nearest snapshot <= target.
- Backward navigation: prefer reverse-fold from the nearest snapshot >= target. Cheap when the target is close to a cached frame.
- For pre-breadcrumb events (events written before commit 915916d), reverse-fold detects the missing field and falls back to forward replay from the nearest earlier snapshot. Best-effort; correctness preserved.

Per-event reverse fold table (key fields):
- created -> remove task
- claimed -> if was_claimed_by present, restore prior holder; else remove claim
- released -> restore claim using was_claimed_by/was_expires_at
- done -> restore status from was_status; restore claim if was_status==claimed
- canceled -> same shape as done
- claim_expired -> restore claim using was_claimed_by/was_expires_at
- reopened -> set status back to from_status (already in payload)
- blocked -> remove edge
- unblocked -> add edge back
- labeled -> remove the names this event added (names minus existing)
- noted -> restore description (would need old_desc; current schema only has description_after — accept lossy reverse, fall back to forward replay)
- edited -> use old_title/old_desc
- moved -> use old_sort_order

data.note:
Delivered as three commits across two halves plus a schema prefix.

Commits:
- 915916d: Records prior-state breadcrumbs on done/claimed/released/cancel events. Prefix commit; enables exact reverse-fold without a forward-only fallback.
- 8657bf8: Adds replay reducer + frame cache primitives. initialFrame, applyEvent, reverseEvent (with breadcrumb-aware reverse), FrameCache with sorted-id insertion + nearest-at-or-before/after queries + shouldSnapshot cadence.
- d259a13: Wires the primitives into a ReplayBuffer orchestrator. Bidirectional replay from the nearest snapshot, lazy event fetching with concurrent-call coalescing, fall-back to forward replay when a reverse step hits a non-reversible event (noted, or pre-915916d events).

Tests:
- 35 + 4 = 39 JS tests under node --test in internal/web/jstest/. Forward fold per event type, forward-then-reverse identity round-trips, breadcrumb-fallback behavior, FrameCache invariants, ReplayBuffer head/replay/memoization/range.
- 9 Go tests in internal/job/event_breadcrumbs_test.go covering every breadcrumb-bearing event site.

Tooling:
- Makefile gains test-js target; scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit runs node --test when both Node and the jstest dir exist.
- internal/web/assets/js/replay.mjs is an ES module (browsers serve .mjs as text/javascript via Go's mime registry; Node treats .mjs as ESM unconditionally — no package.json plumbing).

Deferred (per agreement with ben on 2026-04-26): the JSON island that hydrates a head frame in production. Owned by FxhFR — that task is the first consumer of the head frame and the natural place to ship the vertical slice (JSON island -> bootstrap -> ReplayBuffer -> scrubber pill -> cursor -> frame).

Delivered the scrubber pill UI as six commits:

- 2d8a328: Server-side JSON island. Layout emits <script id="initial-frame"> on every layout-rendering page, carrying every non-deleted task / active block / active claim in the shape replay.mjs's initialFrame() consumes. HTML-safe encoded against </script> injection. Six handlers updated through a shared newChrome helper.
- a72be04: Bootstrap module. Reads the island, normalizes the wire shape (detail-as-string -> object, RFC3339 created_at -> unix seconds), constructs a ReplayBuffer, exposes it at window.JobsScrubber.
- edf335c: Pill toggle skeleton. Footer renders the strip skeleton hidden; layout renders the history banner above main, hidden. Click [data-scrubber-toggle] / [data-scrubber-return] / Escape to toggle. Pill label swaps Live <-> Scrubbing.
- 2266acb: Pure cursor math. xToEventId / eventIdToX (binary search by event timestamp), computeDensityBars (60 buckets across 24h, normalized to 100), formatAge / formatHistoryBannerText.
- fd4418a: DOM wiring. Drag handlers (Pointer Events with setPointerCapture so drags survive pointer-leaves-track). This project follows strict red/green per CLAUDE.md. Write the build-module tests first under `internal/web/jstest/home-scrub-build.test.mjs`, confirm red, then implement. Same for the render module. - After the swap, run `window.JobsColors.paint(document)` so the actor avatars re-tint.
- Self-guard the driver: query for the home-specific marker (probably `main` content with a home-distinctive class or data attribute — check home.html.tmpl) and bail if absent so the module can ride the shared layout without per-page wiring.
- Keep the driver swap targeted (specific elements), not the whole `<main>`, so unrelated chrome (header, peek-sheet, scrubber pill) survives the swap. Look at how plan-scrub.mjs and actors-scrub.mjs identify their swap targets.

Single commit at the end with a 'This commit Rebuilds the Home view from frame on scrubber-frame events' subject (present-tense verb completing 'This commit…'). Body: what each module does, why client-side reduction (R0Ro4 narrowing made / and /plan client-side because they need synthetic-now to be exact). Include test counts in the body.

- Don't add server-side ?at to /home — explicitly out of scope per R0Ro4.
- Don't write golden-file tests; substring assertions match the project style (see Kqxr0 closing note for the rationale).

data.description:
Bundle of UI fixes on the time-travel scrubber identified on 2026-04-26. See project/2026-04-26-scrubber-ui-feedback.md for findings.

Ship in any order; #1 (visibility) and #3 (cursor dot) are one-line fixes worth doing first because they make manual testing of the rest sane.
data.title: Scrubber UI fixes — visibility, controls, navigation

data.description:
`.c-history-banner` and `.c-scrubber-strip` both set `display: flex`, which overrides the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }` because the class selector has higher specificity. Result: both elements show in live mode despite the `hidden` attribute.

Fix: add a global utility rule `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` in base.css. Protects every future component too.

Regression test: a JSDOM unit test that loads layout + components.css and asserts `.c-history-banner[hidden]` computes `display: none`.
data.title: Fix: history banner & strip ignore the `hidden` attribute

data.description:
components.css:1366 — `.c-scrubber-strip__cursor::after` uses `bottom: -4px`. Flip to `top: -4px` (and remove the `bottom` property) so the grip sits at the top of the cursor line.

Manual verify: drag the cursor; the dot should be flush with the top of the strip's track area.
data.title: Move cursor dot from the bottom of the time cursor to the top

data.description:
Today the footer pill reads "Live" with a green dot. It should read "Time Travel" with a back-arrow icon when in live mode; clicking it reveals the strip + cursor with a CSS transition (slide up from the bottom). When in scrubbing mode, the pill becomes "Return to live" with the pulsing green dot (i.e. the current "Live" pill styling).

Remove the in-strip "Return to live" button (footer.html.tmpl:10-13) — the pill carries that state now.

Strip stays in the layout always; the enter/exit transition is `transform: translateY(...)` + `opacity`, ~180ms, matching `--motion-duration-base`. Toggle `aria-hidden`/`inert` (or the `hidden` attribute) in lockstep with the transition so screen readers see the strip only while scrubbing.

Wiring: scrubber-pill.mjs already toggles `page--scrubbing` on `.page` and sets `[data-scrubber-pill-label]`. Extend it to swap a back-arrow ↔ green-dot icon and update the button label between "Time travel" and "Return to live".
data.title: Rename Live pill to Time Travel; gate the strip behind its toggle

data.description: Once #scrubber-hidden-bug lands, the existing enterScrubbing/exitScrubbing logic should already produce the right behavior. Add a JSDOM test that toggles each and asserts the banner's `hidden` attribute flips correctly.
data.title: History banner appears only while scrubbing

data.description:
footer.html.tmpl:8 advertises "Drag the cursor or ←/→ to step." but no handler exists. Add to scrubber-pill.mjs:

On keydown when `isScrubbing(doc)`:
  - ArrowLeft  → seek to events[currentIndex - 1]
  - ArrowRight → seek to events[currentIndex + 1]
  - Stop propagation so plan-keyboard.js doesn't also act on the same key while the Plan view is scrubbing.

The current cursor's eventId is derivable from the banner state or the URL `?at=`. Cache the index in module state next to `inFlightX`.

Tests: extend the scrubber-pill tests with synthesized KeyboardEvents and assert the cursor advances/retreats.
data.title: Wire ←/→ arrow keys to step the cursor by one event

data.description:
Today the strip is a fixed 24h window. Add a pan offset so users can shift the visible range earlier or later.

UX:
  - Hold Space or Alt/Option → cursor turns to a grab hand on the track.
  - Drag → translates the window by N ms; the cursor stays where it was in event-space (not screen-space).
  - Release → window stays panned until reset.

Implementation: add `panOffsetMs` to scrubber state. `xToEventId` / `eventIdToX` / `computeDensityBars` take an optional `windowStartMs` (default `nowMs - windowMs`); panning shifts that start. Math module stays pure.

Out-of-scope for this child: kinetic / inertial scrolling. Linear pan only.

Tests in scrubber-cursor.test for the new `windowStartMs` plumbing; manual verify pointer interaction.
data.title: Pan: hold Space (or Alt/Option) and drag to move the visible window

data.description:
Add a `windowMs` zoom level (currently constant `ONE_DAY_MS` in scrubber-cursor.mjs).

UX:
  - Scrollwheel over the track → multiply `windowMs` by 0.9 (zoom in) / 1.1 (zoom out) per wheel tick, centered on the cursor (or on the mouse pointer when not on the cursor).
  - Alt/Option + ←/→ → same effect via keyboard, fixed steps (e.g. ×0.5 / ×2).
  - Clamp to `[60_000ms, 30 * ONE_DAY_MS]` so the zoom can't collapse to nothing or run infinitely wide.

Rebuild density bars and the time-axis labels on each zoom change. The axis currently hard-codes 24h/18h/12h/6h/now in the template — switch to JS-driven labels derived from `windowMs`.

Tests for the zoom math (clamping, center-anchored zoom preserving the cursor's event-id) in scrubber-cursor.test.
data.title: Zoom: scrollwheel over track (and Alt+←/→) to change window length

data.description: scrubber-pill.mjs:250-252 already calls `exitScrubbing` on Escape. If there's no JSDOM test covering this branch, add one. Otherwise close as already-done.
data.title: Verify Esc cancels scrubbing (already wired); add a test if missing

data.note: Added [hidden] { display: none \!important; } to base.css to make the HTML hidden attribute authoritative against class-level display rules. Regression test in assets_test.go reads base.css from the embedded FS and pins the rule. Full Go + JS suites pass.
Flipped .c-scrubber-strip__cursor::after from bottom:-4px to top:-4px so the cursor grip sits at the top. Regression test pins the anchor in components.css.

Pill is now the sole toggle: 'Time travel' (back-arrow) in live mode, 'Return to live' (pulsing green dot) when scrubbing. Strip stays in DOM with aria-hidden + inert; CSS animates max-height + opacity for the slide-up. Removed the in-strip return button. Added pillLabelFor() helper + tests; CSS regression tests pin both states.

Verified end-to-end: enterScrubbing→toggleVisibility(true) sets aria-hidden=false on strip and unhides banner; exitScrubbing→toggleVisibility(false) reverses both. Three new tests in scrubber-pill.test.mjs cover both directions plus a no-chrome safe-fallback. Banner now appears only while scrubbing.

Wired ←/→ to step the cursor by one event while scrubbing. Tracks currentEventId in module state (set by applyCursor + on enterScrubbing default-to-now path; cleared on exit). Pure stepEventId helper handles edge clamping and unknown-id fallback; 6 new tests cover both directions, both edges, empty events, and the race case. preventDefault + stopPropagation so plan-keyboard's arrow nav stays out of the way.

Pan: hold Space or Alt while drag-pointing the track to translate the visible window. scrubber-cursor.mjs gained an optional windowStartMs param on xToEventId/eventIdToX/computeDensityBars (defaults preserve trailing-24h behavior) plus a pure panWindowStartMs(currentStart, deltaPx, trackWidth, windowMs) helper. scrubber-pill tracks windowStartMs in module state, resets on enterScrubbing, re-renders density bars + cursor on every pan tick. Cursor turns to grab/grabbing while modifier is held. 8 new cursor tests cover the windowStartMs override and pan math.

Zoom: scrollwheel over the track narrows/widens the visible window (×0.9 / ×1.1 per tick), anchored on the pointer. Alt+ArrowRight shrinks ×0.5; Alt+ArrowLeft grows ×2; both anchor on the cursor's current event. windowMs clamps to [60s, 30 days] via the new pure zoomWindow() helper. Time-axis labels are now JS-driven via formatAxisLabels() and re-render alongside density bars on every viewport change. 7 new unit tests cover zoom math, clamp boundaries, degenerate factors, and axis-label semantics.

Refactored the keydown handler around a pure classifyKeydown() helper that returns the action descriptor for each key+modifier combo. The Esc→exit branch is now covered by 6 new tests alongside the rest of the key contract: Escape exits, Space (key or Spacebar/code) latches pan, plain ←/→ step, Alt+←/→ zoom, and crucially — every key is inert when not scrubbing so the search bar / global shortcuts aren't hijacked.

data.description: Iteration on the home dashboard mini-graph (subway model). Behavior change to elision rendering, plus several rendering bugs. See conversation 2026-04-27.
data.title: Mini-graph rendering polish

data.description: Today's algorithm unions a ±N window around every anchor (focal + lookahead leaf), which makes the focal's line render up to 6-7 stops when focal & lookahead are adjacent. Refinement: when adding a lookahead-derived anchor, drop it if it already falls within an existing focal's ±N window on the same parent; keep it as a separate anchor otherwise (preserves the rare disjoint-window case for far lookaheads). Cross-line behavior unchanged. TDD: red tests for ?at=1216, 1316, 1321 plus a synthetic mid-line two-focals case.
data.title: Tighten window union: lookahead anchors only outside focal's ±N on same parent

data.description: Replace the current full-slot '…' rendering with: (1) backward and mid-line elisions = three small SVG circles drawn ourselves (no font dependency) sitting in the gap between two visible nodes, no column slot consumed; (2) trailing/forward elision = a small terminal pill carrying the count of hidden trailing siblings, occupying its own slot. Likely splits LineItemElision into LineItemElision + LineItemMore{N} in signals; layout & template follow.
data.title: Render elision as in-gap dots; add (+N) terminal pill for forward elision

data.description: Today the SVG uses width=100% height={CanvasH}, which non-uniformly squishes wide graphs. Switch to viewBox + intrinsic width=CanvasW, then let CSS scale it down with max-width:100%; height:auto. Reproduces at ?at=1316 (graph extends beyond container).
data.title: SVG intrinsic sizing + CSS shrink-to-fit

data.description: At cursor 1288 two root labels overlap at the left of the graph and one edge renders with from.cx > to.cx (legitimate path in buildSubwayEdgeView, but only ever reached when a node lands left of its predecessor). Hypothesis: column collision between a fork ancestor and a line anchor in LayoutSubway. Reproduce against the historical replay frame, then write a regression test before fixing.
data.title: Fix overlap & backward edge at frame 1288

data.description: At cursor 1321 the genuine 'Next' leaf is mdYup (Empty-state polish) but the graph anchors on Phase 10 with Accessibility Sweep visible at the trailing end. Either pickFocals is not returning mdYup at this frame, or it is and the lookahead chain is widening the window past Empty-state polish (which the sibling task on lookahead union should fix). Verify which after that task lands; if the focal pick itself is wrong, it's its own bug.
data.title: Fix focal-picking / window drift at frame 1321

data.note: lineSeed split into focalAnchors + lookaheadAnchors; applyWindow now anchors a ±N window for every focal but only for lookahead anchors whose index isn't already covered. Adjacent-lookahead caps at ±N around the focal (fixes ?at=1216-style widening); far lookahead still opens a disjoint window.

Split LineItem into Stop/Elision/More with MoreCount. applyWindow emits LineItemMore for trailing hidden siblings instead of a trailing elision. Layout: in-gap elision sits at the midpoint of surrounding item centers (no slot consumed); More pill takes a slot at the line end with synthetic short ID via signals.MoreShortID for edge resolution. Template: elision renders as 3 SVG circles inside the SVG canvas (no font dependency); More pill is a smaller HTML disc with the count. Verified live on /home: '+1' pill renders for the current claim's line.

Wraps the graph in a container-query-driven c-graph-frame; CanvasW/H stamped as --canvas-w/--canvas-h custom properties. Inner c-graph-canvas keeps its intrinsic CanvasW × CanvasH pixel size so SVG paths and HTML-positioned nodes/labels stay aligned at any scale; the frame uses aspect-ratio + transform: scale(min(1, 100cqw / canvas-w)) so it shrinks (never upscales) when the parent is narrower than CanvasW. SVG itself now sized intrinsically (width=CanvasW height=CanvasH) instead of width=100% height=CanvasH, killing the non-uniform squish at ?at=1316.

Root cause: LayoutSubway's line loop wrote cols[line.AnchorShortID] but never wrote rows[line.AnchorShortID]. When the second line's anchor was already a stop on the first line (line 1's parent is a child of the LCA, which IS line 0's anchor) or shared a short ID with a fork ancestor, the row from the earlier pass stuck and the anchor piled on top of line 0's. Buildsubway-edge-view then drew a zero-length, visually-backward edge from the overlapping disc to its first stop. Fix: write rows[line.AnchorShortID] = lineRow alongside cols. Two regression tests pin: (1) the second anchor renders one row stride below the first; (2) no two nodes share a (Left, Top) coordinate.

Confirmed duplicate of Tx8rV — pickFocals correctly returns globalNext (mdYup) at frame 1321 when no claims exist. The user-visible 'wider than ±2' window was the lookahead-union widening Tx8rV already fixed: lookahead from mdYup walks to the next sibling, which falls inside mdYup's ±2 window and now drops, so the line correctly centers on the focal with a (+1) trailing pill. Regression test mirrors the frame's reported shape end-to-end (BuildSubway → Line.Items): five children with one preceding done sibling and globalNext at idx 1 produces [c00, c01, c02, c03, more(1)]. Test green on first run because Tx8rV already drove the underlying behavior; kept as a frame-level pin against future re-regression.

data.description: Build scripts/replay-snapshot/ that loads .jobs.db, replays events 1..N to reconstruct a graphWorld, runs BuildSubway + LayoutSubway, and prints (a) the focal(s) chosen, (b) the topological Subway model, and (c) the rendered SubwayView. Goal: diagnose 'why does ?at=N look wrong' by reproducing the exact server-side state without needing a browser. Reusable for future graph-rendering investigations.

data.description: When a line's anchor IS the LCA (Phase 9 = LCA + line 0 anchor) and another line branches off it (oDKYC's line), the edge from LCA to child-line anchor today renders as a same-column flow edge — drawn by the band-aid as a vertical arrow, which is wrong since arrows-down read as 'blocked path' in this design language. Proper fix: treat such edges as Branch edges (or whatever the fork machinery emits) so they render as the same gentle curve used everywhere else fork branches diverge. Likely lives in BuildSubway's edge generation: when a Flow edge would connect the LCA's row to a child-line anchor at the same col but different row, emit a Branch instead. Revert the same-column vertical-line band-aid in buildSubwayEdgeView once this lands.
data.title: Route LCA→child-line edges through the fork branch, not as direct flow

data.note: Built scripts/replay-snapshot/main.go: forward-replays the events table from event 1 up to --at=N to reconstruct a SubwayInput, then runs BuildSubwayFromInput + LayoutSubway and prints the model. Caveat: pre-2026-04-23 'job import' wrote sort_order=0 in every 'created' event and the backfill SQL repaired the tasks table directly. Forward-only replay would scramble preorder; the tool stamps current tasks.sort_order at create time to mirror what the JS scrubber renders (which rewinds from the live head). Used to reproduce ?at=1287/1288 — confirms the user's image #9 is what BuildSubway emits, with focal=k9fFC (Dynamic favicon, the only available Phase 9 leaf), not 666VP. Output also surfaces a real bug: a Branch qkWEQ → qkWEQ self-edge when the LCA is also line 0's anchor — separate task Ve8v8 already covers the proper fix.

data.description: Replace the index-level dedup with a parent-boundary rule: a lookahead anchor whose parent is the focal's parent OR a descendant of it gets absorbed into the focal's line (no new row), since the lookahead is just diving into a sibling's subtree. Lookahead anchors that exit upward (cousin or further) keep their own line, and the existing fork-chain machinery extends ancestors left-to-right back to the LCA. Reproduces ?at=1288: focal k9fFC, lookahead lands on tpC4u (child of oDKYC, a sibling of k9fFC under qkWEQ) — under the new rule no oDKYC line, just qkWEQ's ±N window.
data.title: Lookahead earns a new line only when it exits the focal's parent's subtree

data.note: Replaced applyWindow's index-level dedup with collectLines's parent-boundary rule. addLookahead now drops anchors whose parent is, or is a descendant of, any focal's parent. Lookaheads that descend into a sibling's subtree are absorbed; only lookaheads that exit upward across a parent boundary (cousin or further) seed a new peek-line. Verified against frame 1288 via the replay helper: image #9's two-line topology collapses to a single qkWEQ line with focal k9fFC ±2, leading elision for XeTlP, no oDKYC peek-line, no LCA-self-edge. Updated all six existing collectLines scenario tests + the OpenBlockerClosesBranch input test to match the new rule (parent-claim focals at the same level no longer fan out into separate lines).

data.new_desc: Multi-step implementation gated by the design note. Two render modes — single-focal preorder window, multi-focal tree map — dispatched per-cluster on whether the focal-path subgraph is a single chain or branches. Invariants: focals are leaves only; each tree node renders at most once; row's leftmost is always rendered (curve target / structural anchor); branch curves originate at leftmost-of-row. Same-parent-siblings carve-out: focal siblings share a row, with ≤2 non-focal siblings inline / ≥3 collapsed to mid-line elision. Backward broken-line elision sits between leftmost and -N-th content stop, never left of leftmost. Forward terminating elision (no (+N) pill). Empty cluster renders "No open tasks" placeholder. Sequencing: (1) single-focal preorder mode, (2) multi-focal tree-map mode + per-row parent edges, (3) layout pivot to depth-aligned columns + centering, (4) cleanup (vertical-line band-aid, (+N) pill remnants), (5) pickFocals leaf-only filter.

data.description:
`job move` is currently sibling-only. Add cross-parent reparenting
so long-running plans can be restructured without cancel/create
cascades that destroy IDs and pollute the event log.

Proposed grammar:
  job move <id> under <new-parent>          # reparent to end
  job move <id> under <new-parent> before|after <sibling>
  job move <id> before|after <sibling>      # current shape, unchanged

Implementation: one new event type (`reparented`) with prior
parent_id stored in detail for invertibility. Update replay/scrubber
to handle the new event.

Why it matters: Phase 10 polish pass surfaced this organically.
The workaround was 22 events (cancel 10 children, watch auto-close,
recreate). That breaks ID stability and contradicts "events are the
source of truth."
data.title: Extend move with cross-parent reparenting

data.description:
`job split <id>` takes an existing leaf, opens N children under it
from an inline list of titles, and re-blocks the parent on them.
Equivalent to `job add` x N + `job block` today, but condensing it
makes "I should track this as smaller steps" the path of least
resistance.

Proposed grammar:
  job split <id> "Child A" "Child B" "Child C"

The parent is automatically blocked on the new children. The parent
remains claimed by the current actor.

Why it matters: Mid-session, an agent considered breaking a large
child into sub-children but skipped it because the ritual was too
heavy. The work stayed mental instead of tracked.
data.title: Add split command for inline task subdivision

data.description:
Add an optional `criteria:` array to the import schema and to
`job add`/`job edit`. Each entry has a short label and a state
(`pending` / `passed` / `skipped` / `failed`).

`job show` renders criteria as a checklist. `job done` can optionally
accept `--criterion key=passed` to update state inline, but **never
blocks on pending criteria** — the auto-close cascade remains
untouched. A soft warning may be printed if criteria are left
pending, but the close proceeds regardless.

Why it matters: Verification gates currently carry their acceptance
criteria as free-text paragraphs. A structured checklist is more
likely to be filled in by agents, more scannable for the next reader,
and enables future audit queries (e.g. "which gates had deferred
performance checks?"). This is lighter than making exit tasks
independent, which would lose the semantic parent/child relationship.

Rationale for no enforcement: we are in BUILD mode; ship the field
as an invitation to structure and observe whether agents voluntarily
fill it in. If trust gets abused, we can add a `--force` gate later.
data.title: Add structured acceptance criteria to tasks

data.description:
Four related papercuts where agents make the same wrong guesses
every session because the CLI surface is inconsistent.

data.description:
`job note <id> "text"` should work without `-m`. Today it fails
with `unexpected argument`. Keep `-m` and stdin (`-`) as
alternatives so existing scripts don't break.

Why: `job add <parent> <title>` takes its body positionally.
The inconsistency means agents guess wrong every session.
data.title: Accept positional message text on job note
Accept --parent as alias on job add

data.description:
`job done <id> -m "..."` works; `job release <id> -m "..."`
fails with `unknown shorthand flag: 'm'`. Lifecycle verbs `done`
and `release` should share a flag surface. Append the note before
releasing the claim.

data.description:
Agents instinctively reach for `job unclaim` when they want to
drop a claim. The "Did you mean: claim?" suggestion is backwards.
Add `unclaim` as a top-level alias and mention it near `claim` in
help text.

data.description:

causing duplication in `show` output (description already

   agent working a leaf can see what it unblocks downstream.
   Today only the gate side shows the relationship.

Four related changes to how `ls`, `tree`, and `list` behave and

a one-liner: "Showing actionable tasks only. Use --all to include
blocked / done / canceled tasks." This orients first-time users without
changing the default filter behavior.

`--open` as a convenience. Absorbs the wrong guess agents make

summary lines — those are the actually-useful parts.

data.description:
`job claim-next` already exists as a standalone command. Fold it
into `job claim --next` for a single cohesive surface. `job
claim --next` claims the same leaf `job status` surfaces as Next.
Optionally accept a parent arg (`job claim --next <parent>`) to
scope the pick to a subtree.

In BUILD mode with zero users, drop the standalone `claim-next`
command rather than maintaining both. Update help text and any
internal references.
data.title: Consolidate `claim-next` into `claim --next`

data.description:
`job claim <id>` echoes a `Next:` line pointing at the globally
next available task. Drop it when the claimed task *is* the
next task the planner would have suggested; keep it after
`done` / `cancel` where it genuinely guides flow.
data.title: Suppress Next hint after job claim when redundant

data.description:
Parents with children should not be claimable. A claim means
"I'm actively working on this" but a parent is a container that
auto-closes when its children finish. These concepts fight each
other and produce expired claims on phases spanning hours or days.

`claim`, `next`, `status`, and `claim --next` should all filter
out parents with children from their claimable task lists. A
parent with no children is a leaf-in-waiting and can still be
claimed normally.
data.title: Make parents with children unclaimable

data.description:
When `job claim` is run against a non-leaf, the error currently
says "claim a leaf instead, or run 'next <id> all' to see them."
Inline a one-line summary of the available leaves so the user can
claim correctly on the next command rather than the one after.
Cap the inline list to keep the error compact.
data.title: List open leaves in claim <parent> error message

and `--since <duration>` so an agent can ask "what did I just
close in the last 5 minutes?" without scrolling through the
entire history.

data.description:
Two related dashboard cleanups discovered while dogfooding:

1) The dashboard has no awareness of acceptance criteria. The data exists in the DB (migration 0003) but neither the task detail page, the peek sheet, nor the Log tab render it. The `criteria_added` and `criterion_state` events also fall through the dashboard's verb maps and emit raw snake_case ("criteria_added by alice") in History rows; they're absent from the Log filter chip bar entirely. The CLI's FormatEventDescription already has nice handling — there's a smell that web and CLI maintain two independent verb tables, but that consolidation is out of scope here.

2) History rows inline the full note text after the verb, which duplicates the note body that lives elsewhere on the page. The task page exposes only the *completion* note above History, so progress notes from `noted` events live ONLY inside History rows today — meaning we can't just strip them without first surfacing them in their own section. The peek sheet additionally mis-labels its single completion-note block as "Notes" (plural, generic), conflating it with progress notes that aren't actually rendered.

Render shape for criteria: a checklist between (Completion note / Progress notes) and History, four states — pending (empty box), passed (check), skipped (em-dash), failed (×). Match the CLI's `criterionGlyph` vocabulary so the two surfaces tell the same story.

data.description:
Today, `job done <id>` succeeds even when the task has unmarked
pending criteria — the system emits an informational note ("X
closed with N pending criteria") but does not block. The first
agent run through a criteria-bearing task on 2026-04-29 closed
one task (GjJX6) with 6 unmarked criteria due to autopilot from
prior criteria-less closes. Strict-by-default catches that slip
at the moment it matters.

Behavior: if the task has criteria and any are still in the
pending state, refuse the close and print the list of pending
criteria back to the caller. Allow override via an explicit
flag whose verbosity is the point.

Override flag: standardize on `--force-close-with-pending`. The
`--force-*` prefix is the established Unix idiom for "I know
what I'm doing"; the verbosity is what makes it self-documenting
in shell history.
data.title: Make criteria-strict the default close behavior

The refusal's leading line uses a stable, greppable prefix (e.g. `cannot close: N pending criteria`) so retry automation can pattern-match it
The pending-count in the refusal header agrees with the listed criteria (regression test against off-by-one)
An explicit override flag (`--force-close-with-pending`) bypasses the check
The override path records the waiver on the done event so a reviewer can see what was deferred
`--cascade` closes still work without per-criterion flags (children own the criteria)
`job cancel` is unaffected (canceled work's criteria are moot)
Tasks without criteria are unaffected — no new friction for the common case
`job done --all-passed` shorthand marks every pending criterion as passed in one call

data.description:
The most frequent close shape is "every criterion passed."
Today that requires one `--criterion` flag per row, which
for an 8-criterion task is 8 long quoted strings. A bulk
shorthand keeps the discipline (you still typed it) without
the typing tax.

The close ack must surface what the bulk flag touched
(e.g. `Marked 6 criteria passed before closing`) so the
self-audit value of the per-row form is preserved. A bulk
flag that silently mutates N rows would erode exactly the
discipline strict-default is trying to add.

data.description:
Today criteria are referenced by verbatim label string, which
makes `--criterion "long quoted label with parens (and × glyphs)=passed"
the dominant close-flow ergonomic. More importantly, the
`criterion_state` event records `label` as the key, so a label
edit silently orphans the historical timeline (the JS
reverse-fold landed in aez2c does `findIndex(c => c.label === detail.label)`
and that match breaks). Giving each criterion a stable short ID
— same shape as task short IDs, e.g. `x7e` — fixes both the
ergonomic and the correctness issues, and unlocks cross-surface
references (commit messages, cross-task blockedBy, stable DOM
ids for SSE partial updates).

Generation lives in `insertCriteria`, the single row-insert
path all criterion-creation paths converge through (`job add --criterion`,
`RunAddCriteria`, `job import`). Hashes stay OUT of the import
grammar — the schema is authoring grammar; the hash is server
identity. Tasks already work this way and a future re-import
function would match by title, not by hash.

`job show` displays the short ID next to each criterion so it is discoverable from the briefing
`--criterion <shortID>=passed` is accepted on `job done` and `job edit` alongside the existing label-string form
`criterion_state` events record the short ID alongside (or in place of) the label, so label edits do not orphan the event history
The JS replay buffer's `criterion_state` reverse-fold matches by short ID, not by label
A one-time migration backfills short IDs onto existing task_criteria rows
Pre-migration `criterion_state` events (label-keyed) continue to apply correctly via a fall-back match path
Label edits on a criterion (a future capability) are decoupled from event identity — labels become pure display strings

data.description:
When a task closes with multiple criteria marked in the same
`done` call, the timeline records one `done` event plus N
`criterion_state` events at near-identical timestamps. In the
web History section these render as N+1 separate rows
interleaved with surrounding events from sibling tasks. Visual
clustering — either grouping under the close, or rendering the
criteria as a sub-line of the done row — would let the dashboard
tell the same story the CLI's `job show` does after a close.

Out of scope for the original aez2c plan; surfaced here as a
follow-up because the data is already there and the dashboard
now renders criteria states.

Open question (resolve before locking the implementation
criteria): the right grouping rule. Transaction-grouping is
tight but misses criteria marked seconds before the close call
in a separate transaction. Time-windowing is loose but may
over-cluster. A small spike against real criteria-heavy close
data should pick the rule before this task is broken into
implementation children.
