data.description:
Today, when a multi-focal cluster has ≥2 in-subgraph children at the cluster LCA with no focal-leaf carve-out, internal/web/signals/subway.go:1006-1013 emits the LCA as its own top row (no stops) and pushes every in-subgraph child to a sub-row. The layout pre-seed at internal/web/render/subway_layout.go:161-185 only inlines an LCA that isn't already an anchor or stop, so when the LCA IS the row-0 anchor it ends up rendered alone above the rest of the rows.

Desired model: row 0 is the LCA spine. At every fork on the spine, the first in-subgraph child continues row 0 and the remaining in-subgraph children become sub-rows. Sub-rows recurse by the same rule. Column = tree depth falls out for free (col(branchParent)+1 with branchParent = tree parent).

Reference cases (all confirmed):

  Case A — carve-out at spine tail:
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B . [*]C

  Case B — fork at cluster LCA:
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B . [*]C
    Row 1:          | Phase 2 -> Content -> [*]X . [*]Y . [*]Z   branchParent: Doc Site

  Case C — fork deeper than LCA:
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B
    Row 1:                     | Imagery -> [*]X . [*]Y          branchParent: Phase 1

  Case D — nested forks (sub-row order is preorder):
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B
    Row 1:                     | Imagery -> [*]X . [*]Y          branchParent: Phase 1
    Row 2:          | Phase 2 -> Content -> [*]M . [*]N          branchParent: Doc Site

Cleanest fix is at the data layer (buildOneRow): when the spine reaches a real fork (no focal carve-out, >=2 in-subgraph children), keep walking the spine through the first child and emit the remaining children as sub-rows. The layout-side pre-seed for legacy fixtures can stay as-is or retire alongside.

Visible regression today: with the documentation-site plan imported, the home subway shows 'Documentation site' floating on a ghost row above 'Scaffolding' (row 0) and 'Content' (row 1).
data.title: Subway graph: row 0 should carry the LCA spine, not float the LCA above

criteria.label: buildOneRow walks the spine through the first in-subgraph child at every fork, emitting remaining in-subgraph children as sub-rows
Cluster LCA is never the sole node on its row when the cluster has multiple sub-rows
Subway tests (subway.go + subway_layout.go) cover Cases A-D from the task description
Documentation site root no longer floats above row 0 in the live home view (verified manually with job serve)

The visit walk also got tightened: chain nodes descend into direct children only, and off-chain children don't recurse into their own subtrees (so e.g. an unrelated J→K,L branch stays out of the row).

`job done <id> -m "..."` and `job release <id> -m "..."` both

<id> -m "..."` errors with `unknown shorthand flag: 'm'`. The
natural use case is a starting note ("what I'm about to try")
symmetric with release's parting note. Add -m to `claim`; have
it append a `noted` event before recording the claim so the
context lands at the start of the timeline rather than the end.

data.title: Accept -m on `job claim` (parity with `done` and `release`)

data.description:
`status` is deliberately human-only, but `--format=json` fails
with the generic `unknown flag: --format` — no hint about what
to reach for instead. Two acceptable resolutions:

A. Accept `--format=json` and emit a JSON shape that mirrors
   the human output: { identity, counts: {open, claimed, done,
   canceled}, last_activity_unix, roots: [...rollup rows],
   next: {id, title}, stale: [...] }. Preferred — script-driving
   agents would use it.

B. Reject with `status is human-only; use 'ls', 'show', or
   'next' for JSON output.` Cheap to ship, fixes the
   discoverability problem if (A) is out of scope.

Pick one; the current state is the worst of both.
data.title: Make `job status --format=json` either work or fail with a directive message

data.description:
Today's failure modes both produce misleading or silent results:

1. `job add "Child A" jTzON` (title-then-parent, transposed) errors
   with `task "Child A" not found` — accurate but misdirecting; the
   user goes looking for a missing task instead of recognizing the
   arg order.
2. `job add jTzON` (parent only, title forgotten) silently creates a
   root task literally titled `jTzON` — no error at all, and the
   slip only surfaces later when the stray root task appears in
   `job status`.

Keep the positional order strict (`add [parent] <title>`) — auto-
detecting which arg is which based on "looks like a short id" is
DWIM that fails on short titles that happen to collide with the
short-id shape. Instead, branch the error on what's actually wrong:

- Two args, leading arg doesn't resolve as a short id → `no such
  parent "Child A"; positional order is 'add <parent> <title>', or
  use --parent to disambiguate.`
- One arg, and that arg DOES resolve as an existing task's short
  id → `"jTzON" is an existing task — did you mean 'add jTzON
  <title>'? (To create a root task literally named "jTzON", pass
  --parent="" to disambiguate.)` Refuse the create until the user
  confirms intent.

The common case — one arg that doesn't resolve as a short id — stays
frictionless: a root task is created with that title.
data.title: Direct the user toward the right fix when `job add` positional args look wrong

criteria.label: Two-arg call with an unresolved leading positional errors with a hint naming the correct order and `--parent` as the disambiguator
Single-arg call where the arg matches an existing short id refuses the create and prompts the user to either supply a title or pass `--parent=""` for the literal-title intent
Single-arg call with a non-short-id string still creates a root task with that title — no new friction for the common case
Two-arg call with a valid leading parent short id still creates the child as before — no behavior change on the happy path
Each new error message has a stable, greppable leading clause so retry automation can branch on it

data.note: Adds the note parameter to RunClaim and wires the -m flag through cmd/job/claim.go, mirroring release -m and done -m. The noted event lands in the same tx as the claimed event and precedes it in the timeline so an agent's starting context anchors the lifecycle rather than trails it. resolveMessage gives -m the same @path / stdin shorthand as the other verbs. Test coverage: atomicity, ordering, empty-note no-op, failed-claim rollback, CLI -m / -m @path / -m -. All callers updated for the new signature; full test suite green; docs updated (reference/_index.md and concepts/leaves-and-claims.md).

Adds --format=json to status with a documented JSON shape. Forest scope: {identity, counts, last_activity_unix, roots, next, stale, decisions}; subtree scope drops the preamble and returns {target, children, next, stale, decisions}. stale and roots are always arrays (possibly empty) so script consumers can iterate without a nil check; next is null when no claimable leaf exists. Unknown --format values are rejected with a directive naming the valid options (md|json). data.note:
Built RunOrient domain model in internal/job/orient.go (8 tests in orient_test.go, all green; full suite green; gofmt/go vet clean).

PUBLIC API for the renderer (mBaVj):
  RunOrient(db, targetShortID, scopeShortID, actor string) (*OrientView, error)
  - targetShortID="" -> next available leaf (RunNext); else positional id.
  - scopeShortID="" -> whole root tree; else subtree rooted at scope. Target/scope orthogonal.

TYPES (all in orient.go, ready to render):
  OrientView{ Header OrientHeader; Tree *OrientNode }
  OrientHeader{ Target,Title,Root,Status string; BlockedBy []string; Blocks []OrientRef{ID,Title};
                Criteria CriteriaTally{Passed,Total}; OwnNotes []NoteEntry; WeighNotes []string }
  OrientNode{ Task *Task; Target bool; Blocks []string; Criteria []Criterion; Notes []NoteEntry; Children []*OrientNode }

CONVENTIONS the YAML renderer should match the design schema with:
  - Per-node field order is identity->spec->history: id,status,(closed if done),desc,labels,blocks,criteria, NOTES LAST.
  - Header.Root is the target's TRUE root even under --scope (scope only bounds Tree).
  - Notes are pre-filtered to substance via substantiveNotes(): noted events + completion note; churn excluded. NoteEntry has {Actor,Text,CreatedAt}. Completion note is appended last, attributed to the done event's actor/timestamp (both may be zero/empty - render defensively).
  - Criteria are []Criterion{ShortID,Label,State}; render as {text: Label, state: State}. State enum: pending/passed/skipped/failed.
  - target node flagged via OrientNode.Target -> emit 'target: true'.
  - 'closed' date: derive from Task.Status=='done' + Task.UpdatedAt (no dedicated closed field on Task).
  - OwnNotes/WeighNotes/Blocks/BlockedBy are nil slices when empty (render as []).

data.description:
Today `done --claim-next` picks the next available leaf REPO-WIDE
(cmd/job/done.go passes "" as the scope to RunClaimNextFiltered). In a
focused session that means closing a leaf can hand you an unrelated
out-of-scope task in another root (observed: closing a resilience-batch
leaf claimed a phase-3 NOTE in a different tree).

Decision (with user): scope ONLY `done --claim-next`, anchored on the
root ancestor of the just-closed task (clean, unambiguous anchor).
Leave standalone `claim --next` global — its positional parent already
scopes, and a no-arg claim has no closed task to anchor on.

Implementation: add an exported job-package helper that resolves the
closed task's top ancestor (reuse findTopAncestor in tasks.go) and
calls the existing RunClaimNextFiltered with that root short id; the
recursive-CTE scope in queryAvailableLeafFrontier already restricts to
the whole subtree. Add `--under <id>` (explicit scope override) and
`--any` (restore global), both meaningful only with --claim-next.
Precedence: --under > --any > default(root-of-closed).

data.text:
Design decisions before implementing:
- Table found_in(task_id PK -> tasks.id ON DELETE CASCADE, source_id NOT NULL -> tasks.id ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at). ON DELETE CASCADE on source_id is a deliberate departure from the brief's plain REFERENCES: PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON (internal/job/database.go:80) and cancel --purge hard-deletes task rows, so a plain reference would make purging a source fail with an FK error. Purge is total erasure, not a status change, so the provenance edge going with it is correct.
- The four cases the brief names (done, cancel, cascade-cancel, soft-delete) are all status/flag changes and touch no rows; nothing in cancel.go or the auto-close path reads or writes found_in.
- show renders 'Found in:' / 'Surfaced:' in house column style (matching 'Blocked by:' / 'Blocks:') rather than the brief's lowercase 'found in:' - consistency with the surrounding briefing wins.
- add --found-in validates the source before RunAdd and sets the edge after, rather than changing RunAdd's signature (which would ripple into import, web and testhelpers). Not one transaction; the realistic failure (bad source id) is caught up front.

Implemented -F/--file across all seven verbs via one shared helper in cmd/job/commands.go (registerFileFlag + bodyFlagSpec/resolveBodyFlag + resolveMessageAs with a typed bodySource for error attribution). cancel's --reason/-m now routes through the resolver too. 28 new cmd-level tests in cmd/job/file_flag_test.go; full go suite green, no existing test changed. Docs next.

Implemented: sentinel error internal/job/errors.go (ErrNoAvailableTasks + errNoAvailableTasks wrapper, Unwrap-only so err.Error() text is byte-identical for next/claim). claims.go's two RunNextFiltered error returns now wrap via newErrNoAvailableTasks() (message text unchanged). New RunOrientNoTasks (internal/job/orient.go) + RenderOrientNoTasksYAML (internal/job/orient_yaml.go) render target:null + message, with tasks: showing the focused root's tree (when focus scoped the miss) or every root in the forest (no focus). cmd/job/orient.go catches errors.Is(err, job.ErrNoAvailableTasks) and renders that instead of returning the error, so orient exits 0. Added 3 new cmd-level tests to cmd/job/orient_test.go (TestOrient_EmptyRepo_ExitsZeroWithGuidance, TestOrient_FocusedRootExhausted_ExitsZeroWithGuidance, TestNextAndClaimNext_EmptyRepo_StillExitNonZero) -- all red before implementation, all green after. None of cmd/job/commands_test.go, cmd/job/next_all_test.go, internal/job/claim_next_scope_test.go needed changes -- none of them actually exercise orient (verified by grep + targeted test runs); they still pass unchanged. internal/job/focus_orient_test.go's TestRunOrient_NoArg_FocusedRootExhausted_FailsLoudly also stays green unchanged, by design: RunOrient/RunOrientOpts (domain layer) still return the error, only cmd/job/orient.go (CLI layer) catches it. Docs: DOCS.md had NO orient section at all (pre-existing gap, contradicts brief's premise) -- added one row to the Viewing-tasks table. docs/content/docs/reference/observation.md's ## orient section updated (5th bullet on exit-0 behavior + reworded focus bullet). gofmt/vet/go test ./... all clean. Reverted unrelated go-fix rewrites in internal/job/cancel.go, internal/job/done_strict_test.go, internal/web/handlers/errors.go that appeared when I ran go fix ./... -- out of scope, not part of this diff.

Docs done: DOCS.md rows for all seven verbs, docs/content/docs/reference/{_index,execution,planning}.md, concepts/leaves-and-claims.md, and the root help's short-flag table. Full go suite + 335 JS tests green. Verified against a freshly built binary, not just the test harness.

add/edit -F implemented in the same pass as XtgBr, sharing resolveBodyFlag. Deliberate divergence from the five -m verbs: --desc stays STRICTLY LITERAL on add/edit (bodyFlagSpec.InlineLiteral), so -F is the only file form there and a description beginning with '@' is stored as typed. --desc "" still clears on edit (the pointer is driven by 'provided', not by a non-empty value), and -F alone now satisfies the at-least-one-flag gate. data.text:
Tree kind implemented (worktree .claude/worktrees/kind, not committed).

Schema: PLACEHOLDER internal/migrations/900_task_kind.sql — ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'task' CHECK (kind IN ('task','issue')). Verified in sqlite that both CHECK and NOT NULL bite. Renumber at integration.

Model: internal/job/kind.go — typed TreeKind enum (KindTask/KindIssue), ParseTreeKind, RunSetKind recording a kind_changed event with {from,to}. Task.Kind added to the struct and to all 15 task SELECTs + closed_tail's hand-rolled scan.

Design decisions:
1. `job move <issue-root> under <parent>` ERRORS rather than resetting kind to 'task'. Resetting silently discards the operator's classification and puts nothing in the audit log; the fix is one explicit `job kind <id> task`, which does land an event. Consistent with "conversion loses nothing".
2. `ls` marks issue roots as `(issue-tree)` inside the existing parens group (with claims/blockers/labels) rather than a bare `[issues]` tag after the title — it composes with labels and matches how format.go already renders state. `show` prints `Kind: issue` on issue roots only; task is the default and printing it everywhere is noise.
3. The filter seam is the anchor of queryAvailableTasks: the kind predicate is applied only when parentID == nil. An explicit id/scope or a focus (which sets scope=focus.ShortID) therefore overrides the default for free — no special-casing.
4. `--issues` is forest-wide and ignores focus, mirroring the existing rule that `next all` ignores focus for the explicit "show me everything" form. Without it, `--issues` under a task focus would return task leaves.
5. `job status`'s global `Next:` hint also excludes issue-trees (summary.go), because it answers the same question as `next` — leaving it would have made status recommend a leaf `claim --next` refuses. The per-root rollup still lists every root.
6. JSON: `"kind": "issue"` emitted only on issue roots (omitempty), so no existing payload changes.

Not built (per brief): found-in edge, -F flags, orient exit-0, severity/triage/reporter.

- Web dashboard: verified it renders fine with an issue root (/, /plan, /log all 200), but shows no issue-tree marker and does not segregate issue trees. Left alone per brief.
- `job import` has no `kind:` key in the grammar; imported roots default to 'task'.
- `job status`'s per-root rollup rows do not mark issue roots.
- go fix applied three pre-existing modernizations unrelated to this change (internal/job/cancel.go, internal/job/done_strict_test.go, internal/web/handlers/errors.go) — the pre-commit hook would have applied them anyway.

Implemented `ls --issues` and issue-root demotion.

- internal/job/list_issues.go (new): `IssueOpenCount` (unfiltered open-task
  count across all issue roots, root included), `ScopeListResult` (splits an
  already-computed ListResult to one tree kind — top-level Open nodes
  directly, ClosedTail via a new unexported `rootKindByTaskID` ancestor
  lookup, recapping to the caller's requested cap so "N of M" stays accurate
  per kind).
- internal/job/format.go: added `RenderIssueRootList` (renders `ls --issues`
  rows without the now-redundant `issue-tree` tag) and
  `listStateParensOpts`/`renderMarkdownListTagged` backing it.
  `RenderMarkdownList`/`listStateParens` signatures are unchanged — no
  existing caller/test touched.
- cmd/job/list.go: new `--issues` flag. Kind-splitting only applies to the
  unscoped forest (`parentShortID == ""`); an explicit id is unaffected
  either way. Markdown always splits (default excludes issue roots,
  `--issues` shows only them); `--format=json` never demotes by default
  (every root + `kind`, per spec) but `--issues` narrows it too, for
  symmetry with every other filter. The `Issues: N open · job ls --issues`
  trailer prints on every default-mode markdown return path (including the
  "nothing actionable"/no-match branches) whenever any issue root exists,
  and never otherwise. `--all`'s closed-tail footer is scoped by kind in
  both modes (fetched uncapped, filtered, recapped — see
  TestLsAllClosedFooterScopedByKindInBothModes).
- cmd/job/kind_test.go: `TestListMarksIssueRootsCLI` asserted the old
  behavior (default `ls` tags an issue root inline) — replaced with
  `TestListOmitsIssueRootsByDefaultCLI` asserting the new one (omitted +
  trailer). No other existing test needed changes; internal/job/kind_test.go
  still tests `RenderMarkdownList` (the tag-preserving path) directly and
  stays green untouched.
- DOCS.md (ls row only), docs/content/docs/reference/observation.md (`ls`
  section), docs/content/docs/concepts/tree-kinds.md ("Where the marking
  shows up" bullet) updated.

New tests: internal/job/list_issues_test.go (9 cases: IssueOpenCount x4,
ScopeListResult x4, RenderIssueRootList x1), cmd/job/list_issues_test.go
(9 cases covering all 6 job-show criteria plus --issues composing with
--mine/-l and the closed-footer split). TDD: cmd/job/list_issues_test.go was
written and run red (unknown flag: --issues / wrong assertions) before

its tests rather than strictly test-first — the design (mirroring the
existing taskKindRoots/defaultKindScope pattern in claims.go) needed fixing

issue-tree's sole child cascade-closes the root, per the parent-auto-close

sweeps stale claims first (as status does) so an expired lock never becomes the source; several
claims print a hint naming the ids. Creation goes through RunAddKind with KindTask, i.e. add's
transaction, and both the root and the found-in source resolve before any write.

Two brief facts were wrong: `add` prints no parent line and no Found in: acknowledgement. The
verb prints `add`'s actual advisory lines (Released:/child count) and borrows the `found-in`
verb's wording, `Found in: <new> was found in <src>`.

Fixed: `cascadeAutoCloseAncestors` (internal/job/tasks.go) now stops the leaf-frontier
auto-close cascade at an issue-tree root instead of closing it. Added a guard
right after the `open > 0` check: `if p.ParentID == nil && p.Kind.IsIssue() { return result, nil }`.
This is shared by both `done` and `cancel` cascades, and by construction it also
means `releaseFocusOnRootClose` never fires for the root (that call sits further
down, unreached once we return early) — verified with a new test. An explicit
`job done <root>` / `job cancel <root>` is untouched (different code path).

New tests (red-then-green, in internal/job):
- issue_root_cascade_test.go (new file): skip-on-done, not-listed-in-AutoClosedAncestors,
  intermediate-parent-still-closes, skip-on-cancel, explicit-done-still-closes (this
  last one was already green — it exercises a path this fix doesn't touch, kept as
  a guard).
- focus_autorelease_test.go: TestCascadeCloseIssueRoot_DoesNotReleaseFocus (new).

Two pre-existing tests encoded the bug itself and had to change (TDD rule: explain
why an existing test changes):
- internal/job/focus_kind_test.go: TestCloseIssueRoot_ReleasesTheIssueFocusOnly ->

  last leaf cascade-closed the issue root and released everyone's issue focus —
  that was the bug. Now asserts focus and root both survive.
- internal/job/status_issues_test.go: TestBuildIssuesStatus_NextNilWhenNoneClaimable
  -> renamed TestBuildIssuesStatus_NextIsRootWhenItsChildrenAllClosed. With the root
  no longer closing, it's the only open node left (no open children, unclaimed), so
  `next --issues` correctly hands it out as the frontier ("the next open issue" per
  docs) instead of nil. This surfaced only because the old cascade bug made this
  state unreachable before. Did not touch claims.go/RunNextFiltered itself — the
  existing leaf-selection query already does the right thing once the root's state
  is correct; this is a consequence, not a second bug.

Docs: one sentence added to DOCS.md's Tree kinds intro paragraph and to
docs/content/docs/concepts/tree-kinds.md's "Why the distinction exists" section,
each stating the cascade never closes an issue-tree root and that explicit
`job done <root>` is unchanged.

Verification: `go fix ./...` (clean, no changes beyond mine), `gofmt -l .` (clean),
`go vet ./...` (clean), `go mod tidy` (no changes), `go test ./...` all green.
`make build` succeeded; reproduced the original bug on a scratch db pre-fix
mentally matches the brief's repro, and post-fix: `add "Bugs" --kind issue`,
`add <root> "flaky test"`, `done <bug>` -> `show <root>` now reports
`Status: available` (not done); `done <root>` explicitly still closes it
(`Status: done`).

Files touched: internal/job/tasks.go, internal/job/issue_root_cascade_test.go (new),
internal/job/focus_autorelease_test.go, internal/job/focus_kind_test.go,
internal/job/status_issues_test.go, DOCS.md, docs/content/docs/concepts/tree-kinds.md.

The brief's DO-NOT-BUILD list didn't anticipate that fixing the cascade would flip
two existing tests from green (on buggy behavior) to red, one of which
(status_issues_test.go) exposed that RunNextFiltered/BuildIssuesStatus (in
claims.go / status_issues.go, neither of which was on the excluded list) now hands
out the issue root itself as "next" once its children are all closed. That's the
correct behavior per the docs' own "the next open issue" framing, not a second bug
— but it's a judgment call the brief didn't flag, and another agent touching
list.go/next semantics in parallel should know this dependency exists. Also minor:
the brief says "confirm ... the root-close focus auto-release does not fire for it
— add a test," which I did, but note the mechanism is "never reached" rather than
"reached but does nothing" — worth being precise about since a future refactor of
the cascade could reintroduce the bug if someone moves the release call earlier
without re-adding the issue-root guard first.

Done in worktree .claude/worktrees/loglive (not committed).

Root cause was two drifts, not one:
1. log-live.js re-implemented the row markup by hand — no metadata cell, raw event_type as the verb.
2. live.js subscribed to a stale list of SSE event *names*. Every /events frame carries `event: <type>`, and a named SSE frame never reaches a `message` listener, so found_in_set, kind_changed, criteria_added, criterion_state, claim_expired, focus_set/released, reparented and purged never reached ANY live module — the rows never arrived at all.

Fix (option (a) from the brief):
- New internal/web/assets/js/log-row.mjs: pure verbFor / metadataFor / isSystemEvent / renderLogRow + KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES, mirroring the server.
- log.html.tmpl's row extracted into a {{define "log-row"}} block; handlers.buildLogEventRow extracted from loadLogEvents so a row can be built from one event.
- log-live.js -> log-live.mjs, rendering from the shared module (importmap entry added).
- live.js KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES widened to the full emitted vocabulary.

Tests: internal/web/handlers/log_row_parity_test.go renders each of 25 fixtures through the Go template AND through log-row.mjs via node, and diffs the normalised markup (verified it fails on a deliberate one-word change). Plus two drift guards: KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES in log-row.mjs == handlers.knownEventTypes, and live.js subscribes to every event type scraped from the recordEvent call sites in internal/job. internal/web/jstest/log-row.test.mjs (25 tests) walks the same list.

Browser evidence: sleepy session on /log against a scratch db, fired found-in / kind / note / block / edit --criterion / --set-criterion / label; dumped the 17 live rows and the 17 rows from a fresh SSR load and diffed — 0 mismatches.

Docs: DESIGN.md log-row spec now describes the metadata column and the two-renderer contract; http-api.md notes the named-frame subscription requirement. Two gotchas appended.

Follow-up NOT done (different row variant, out of scope): actors-live.js has its own renderLogRow for /actors/<name> with the same class of drift (raw event_type verb, a c-log-row__note the SSR never emits). The actor_single template's row has no metadata cell, so unifying it is a design call.

data.text:
`GitignoreHint` is now a function over the entry table, not a hand-typed constant.

Shape change: `gitignoreEntry` went from {name, comment} to {comment, patterns []string} so the two WAL sidecars can share one comment ("SQLite WAL sidecars — always local"), as the doc's "The hint" block requires. `.jobs.db` carries "Jobs event store — local by default; delete this line to share it".

One renderer serves both callers: `gitignoreBlock(entries)` emits "# comment" on its own line above its patterns. `GitignoreHint()` renders the full table (trailing newline trimmed, so callers can Fprintln it); `WriteGitignoreEntries` renders only the *missing* groups under its existing "# job" header, via a new `missingGitignoreEntries(existing)` partition helper that keeps the group structure — so a comment still prints above whichever of its patterns are absent.

Tests (red first — the constant-to-function change was a compile failure across the package): no hint line is both a pattern and a comment (reuses the existing trailingComment regexp); every hint line is unindented and each pattern appears as a bare line; the hint equals the documented block byte-for-byte; the writer's block on a fresh dir equals the hint after stripping the "# job" header.

One existing test changed: the idempotency test asserted `len(alreadyPresent) == len(jobGitignoreEntries)`, which was 3 when entries were per-pattern and is 2 now that they are grouped. It compares against `len(gitignorePatterns())` — the flattened pattern list — which is what it always meant.

Discrepancy with the design doc worth recording: the doc sketches `GitignoreHint(missing []string)`, but leaf 6rYaf specifies the hint always shows all three patterns. Implemented as a no-arg `GitignoreHint()`; a `missing` parameter would have had no caller.

- docs/content/docs/getting-started/initialize.md — rewritten: `job init --as <name>` required, `--strict` alternative, the init-refusal error text, the new copy-pasteable gitignore hint block, and a `job gitignore` section replacing `--gitignore`.
- docs/content/docs/getting-started/first-plan.md — prerequisite line now shows `job init --as alice`.
- docs/content/docs/getting-started/_index.md — card subtitle updated (`job init --as <name>`, strict mode, `job gitignore`).

- docs/content/docs/reference/setup.md — `init` example block drops `--default-identity`/`--gitignore`, adds the refusal error text; new `## gitignore` section documents the verb; reworded one comment that used "default-identity" as a plain compound noun (it doesn't reference the removed flag, but it matched the literal verification grep).
- docs/content/docs/reference/_index.md — Setup card subtitle now lists `gitignore`.
- DOCS.md — Get-started quick-start now shows `job init --as alice`; identity section example block and prose rewritten (no `$USER` fallback, no `--default-identity` line); command table splits the old single `init` row into `init --as`, `init --strict`, and a new `job gitignore` row.
- README.md — quick-setup paragraph and example now use `job init --as <name>` / `job init --as claude`, with guidance to name the assistant, not the account.
- scripts/verify-getting-started.sh — step 1 drops `--default-identity`/`--gitignore` from `init`; inserted a new step 2 that calls `job gitignore` directly (renumbered steps 2-8 to 3-9). NOT run — the binary doesn't have the new behavior yet (per the brief); the integrator runs it after rebuild.
- project/gotchas.md — added a `rule:`-prefixed entry: project/agents/jobs.md line 29 is now slightly stale (init always required recording a name; a reader could still infer the old `$USER` default) but the whole file sits inside a generated `<!-- agents:begin jobs@6661dd -->` region, so I did not edit it directly per the "don't edit inside generated regions" rule — flagged for the shared-rule review instead.

Verification: `grep -rn 'default-identity\|init --gitignore\|records \$USER' docs DOCS.md README.md project/agents scripts` returns nothing (exit 1, no matches) in the worktree.

Also added a `job gitignore` step to verify-getting-started.sh (brief said "if it exercises --gitignore, switch to job gitignore" — it did exercise it via init, so I split it into its own step rather than dropping the coverage).

Did not run scripts/verify-getting-started.sh, per instruction — the binary doesn't have the new behavior yet.

`job gitignore` is a top-level verb in the new cmd/job/gitignore.go, registered next to `init` in commands.go; `init --gitignore` is gone and is now a cobra unknown-flag error.

The verb resolves its directory as `filepath.Dir(job.ResolveDBPathForInit(dbPath))` — the same resolution `init` uses to pick where to create the database, so `job --db /path/to/x.db gitignore` writes /path/to/.gitignore. It opens no database, records no event, and needs no --as: the directory is the whole input, so it works before `init` as happily as after. Output is `Wrote N entries to .gitignore: a, b` on a write and `.gitignore already includes …` (humanJoin) when everything is present.

The old `init --gitignore` tests moved to cmd/job/gitignore_test.go against the verb (create, append to an existing file, idempotent, partial-present, and the real-`git` `check-ignore` test that catches the trailing-comment trap), plus two new ones: it works in a directory with no .jobs.db and creates none, and `init --gitignore` errors. `gitignore` was also added to the verb list in TestHelp_MentionsCurrentVerbs — verified red by commenting out the AddCommand line before restoring it, since a help-listing assertion is otherwise green from the moment the verb exists.

One wording correction against the design doc: it prints `already includes .jobs.db, .jobs.db-shm and .jobs.db-wal`, but `humanJoin` — which the brief says to reuse, and which every other list the CLI prints goes through — uses an Oxford comma. The test asserts humanJoin's spelling; consistency across the CLI beats a doc example's informal comma.

`job init` now requires an identity. The check is the first statement in RunE — before the "already exists" stat and before CreateDB — so a call that names nobody leaves nothing behind to `--force` over. `--default-identity` and the `$USER` fallback are gone; `--as` (the existing global flag) records the default and the output drops the `(from …)` suffix, since there is only one source left.

Messages: rather than mint a third identity-required string, the two that exist are now named constants in cmd/job/identity.go — `identityRequiredMsg` (the unchanged per-verb wording, used by both `requireAs` in commands.go and `requireAsStrict` in identity.go, which were duplicate literals) and `initIdentityRequiredMsg` for init's longer refusal. commands_test.go pins each as a literal (`wantIdentityRequired`, `wantInitIdentityRequired`) so the wording cannot drift unnoticed.

Help (Long) follows decision 3: what the default identity is for, "use the name of whoever is running the command — a person's handle, or, for an automated assistant, the assistant's own name rather than the account it runs under", the $USER caution, --strict, and a pointer to `job gitignore`. data.note:
Ruling (Ben, 2026-09-01): tasks mint six base62 characters; criterion ids stay three characters and become unique per task rather than per table.

Why six: the width is one byte slice in generateShortID and nothing resolves an id by length, so existing five-character ids are untouched and no migration runs. Six cuts cross-replica collision odds about 60x, and a collision has no safe remap once the id is in notes and commits, so cheap insurance beats a tidy column.

Why criteria stay three: every lookup is already scoped by task and every event that references a criterion carries its task, so global uniqueness buys nothing and, at three characters, is the larger collision hazard. Global addressability, if ever wanted, is task id plus criterion id, which the per-task scope supports.

Details in project/2026-09-01-git-native-event-log.md, decision 1.

Nothing about width remains for this leaf.

internal/eventlog landed on wt/codec (worktree .claude/worktrees/codec). Pure library, stdlib only, no SQLite and no internal/job import.

Files: eventlog.go (package doc + base62 alphabet copy), envelope.go, position.go, clock.go, replica.go, store.go (paths + flock), appender.go, reader.go, plus a _test.go for each. 1831 lines total, largest file 318.

API the store leaf (gjMDD) can build on:
- Envelope{V,Rep,Seq,TS,Actor,Type,Task,Data json.RawMessage}; Marshal/Unmarshal, one line each.
- Position{TS,Rep,Seq}, Compare/Less, Sort([]Envelope), String() "<ts>-<rep>-<seq>", ParsePosition.
- Clock: NewClock / NewClockWith(func() time.Time), Now, Observe, Load, Save. Save's value is what local.json persists as last_seen.
- NewReplicaID / ValidReplicaID / ReplicaIDLength.
- StoreDir(cachePath), LogDir(storeDir), LogPath(storeDir, rep), LockPath(cachePath) = cachePath+".lock"; AcquireLock(cachePath) / (*Lock).Release.
- OpenAppender(storeDir, cachePath, rep); Append (takes the lock) and AppendLocked (caller already holds it — the append-plus-apply path must use this one or it deadlocks).
- Files(storeDir) []File{Rep,Path,Size} — Size is the watermark byte offset. ReadFile(path), ReadAll(storeDir). Errors are *ParseError{Path,Line,Err} and *SeqGapError{Path,Line,Expected,Got}.

Three decisions worth knowing:
1. The appender re-scans the file for the last seq under the lock on EVERY batch, not once at open. Caching it at open would repeat a seq the moment a second appender or a second process wrote.
2. Appending onto a file that does not end in a newline is refused as a *ParseError, rather than silently repairing a half-written tail.
3. The position string is a cursor, not a sort key: plain decimal is not lexicographically ordered, so compare positions by parsing them. Tested that sorting parsed positions matches Position.Compare.

Verification: go fix / gofmt / go vet / go mod tidy clean; go test -count=1 ./... green; go test -race ./internal/eventlog green; go build ./... clean. Red was confirmed twice — once against panicking stubs, and once by mutating four behaviours (clock max, position tiebreak, seq-gap check, appender seq source), which failed exactly the 16 tests that cover them.

data.text:
`job merge <other.jobs.db> [--dry-run] [--format=md|json]` implemented on wt/merge.

Library: internal/job/merge_snapshot.go (both files read into short-id-keyed maps + the common-prefix relatedness check), merge_plan.go (every write decided, no DB touched — dry run is the same path minus apply), merge.go (apply in one transaction, staging, RunMerge), merge_report.go (report types + Markdown/JSON). CLI: cmd/job/merge.go, registered in commands.go and in the root help's Setup group. Docs: DOCS.md database table row; docs/content/docs/reference/setup.md gets a `merge` section (and the page intro + reference card now name it).

Design calls worth recording:

- The other file is staged to a temp copy before it is opened, because OpenDB runs migrations and could otherwise write to it. That makes "the other file is never written" literally true rather than true-in-practice.
- Merge records no event of its own and needs no --as: copying history is not making it, and an event would break "a second merge changes nothing".
- Events union as a *multiset* (counts per tuple), not a set. A set union would silently drop a tuple either side legitimately holds twice.
- A dropped claim is only reported when the merge actually writes that task's row, so a re-run reports nothing rather than repeating a drop it did not perform.
- Claims are treated as leases, not row fields: a live claim survives even when its side loses the row. Expired claims are never adopted onto a row that lacked one (they do ride along when their own row wins, which matches what lazy expiry would leave).
- users are unioned by name (identity registry); config is deliberately NOT merged — default identity and strict mode belong to the checkout.
- Union semantics cannot express deletion: a label removed or a blocker cleared on one side returns if the other still holds it. Documented in the reference page. Note `RunDone` deletes block edges where the closed task is the blocker (tasks.go:843), so closing a blocker on one side and merging can resurrect the edge.
- A criteria short-id collision across two *different* tasks is detected and inserted with a NULL short id, which the next OpenDB backfills.

Suite: `go test ./... -p 1` green; go fix / gofmt / go vet / go mod tidy / go build clean.

Typed every recordEvent/recordOrphanEvent payload in internal/job as a Go struct, one per event type, in one new file internal/job/event_payloads.go. Added a named EventType string type with 23 constants (one per event type in the vocabulary) and changed recordEvent/recordOrphanEvent in database.go to take EventType (detail stays `any`).

Audited every call site by hand first: every existing payload that references a task or criterion was ALREADY a short id string (never an integer row id) — the codebase already did the right thing there, so this leaf was purely the map->struct/string->EventType mechanical refactor, no semantic value changes. No JSON key was renamed.

New files:
- internal/job/event_payloads.go — EventType + 23 constants + 23 payload structs (CreatedPayload, LabeledPayload, UnlabeledPayload, ReleasedPayload, CanceledPayload, DonePayload, BlockedPayload, UnblockedPayload, PurgedPayload, ClaimExpiredPayload, NotedPayload, ClaimedPayload, CriterionEntry + CriteriaAddedPayload, CriterionStatePayload, FocusSetPayload, FocusReleasedPayload, HeartbeatPayload, FoundInSetPayload, FoundInClearedPayload, KindChangedPayload, ReopenedPayload, EditedPayload, MovedPayload, ReparentedPayload).
- internal/job/event_payloads_test.go — TestEventPayloadsMarshalWithShortIDs (marshals one populated sample of every payload type, walks the decoded JSON recursively, fails if any field named "id" or ending "_id" holds a JSON number) and TestEveryEventTypeHasAPayloadSample (cross-checks the sample table against every EventType constant).

Key design point: three event types ("done", "canceled", and the auto-close-ancestor cascade that emits either) share a struct across genuinely different call-site shapes. Where a field is unconditionally present at one call site but must be entirely absent at another (only the `cascade` bool), I used `*bool` so json omitempty can tell "false" from "not applicable" — a plain bool would have either always emitted `cascade:false` or always dropped it. All other optional fields use plain omitempty since every reader (format.go, replay.mjs) already tolerates missing-vs-null (confirmed by reading every reader before touching a field).

Updated internal/web/handlers/log_row_parity_test.go's scraper: eventConstRe now matches `EventXxx EventType = "value"` (was matching lowercase `eventXxx = "value"`) — required because the new constants live in one const block with a type annotation, not the old one-per-file bare consts. Did not touch the assertion logic, per the brief.

Removed the old ad-hoc consts (eventFocusSet/eventFocusReleased in focus.go, eventKindChanged in kind.go) in favor of the new EventType constants; updated their non-recordEvent readers too (SQL query params, string comparisons in focus.go, the switch in format.go, kind_test.go).

(twice, converged — rewrote boolPtr to use `new()` per Go 1.24 and added a `//go:fix inline` pragma, harmless), gofmt -l (clean after one file), go vet ./... (clean), go mod tidy (no go.mod/go.sum changes).

No reader depends on key order (verified — all readers do map/property access, not raw string comparison). Also, where a field is optional at some call sites of an event type (e.g. done/canceled's `cascade_closed`), omitempty now omits the key entirely instead of the old map-based `"cascade_closed":null`; confirmed every reader treats missing and null identically. Done on branch wt/local (worktree .claude/worktrees/local); not committed.

What landed
- internal/job/local.go + local_test.go: LocalState{rep,last_seen,identity,strict,focus{actor:{kind:root}}} in .jobs/local.json (eventlog.StoreDir beside the cache). Load (missing = zero state, malformed = error naming the path), atomic Save (temp+fsync+rename), UpdateLocalState under eventlog.AcquireLock for every read-modify-write. rep/last_seen are reserved and unused — the store leaf fills them.
- How the cache path reaches the code: CachePathOf(db) asks SQLite (`PRAGMA database_list`) which file the connection was opened from. Chose that over threading a path parameter: threading would have changed GetFocus/GetFocusKind/ResolveIdentity plus RunNextFiltered, RunOrientNoTasks, ResolveIssueRoot, BuildSummary, RunStatus, RunClaim/RunDone/RunCancel and ~180 test call sites — including tasks.go, which agent-sortkeys is rewriting. The pragma keeps --db and local.json impossible to disagree, and every existing test kept its signature. Note: SQLite reports the symlink-resolved absolute path.
- Identity: config.go now reads/writes local.json; GetConfig/SetConfig deleted; the config table stays in the schema and is asserted to have zero rows. New InitIdentity(db, name, strict) used by `job init`: --force previously reset strict/focus by deleting the DB, and now has to clear them explicitly (regression test in cmd/job/identity_test.go).
- Focus: focus.go rewritten onto local.json. flipFocusOnClaim moved after RunClaim's commit (a failed focus write prints a warning; the claim stands) — a file lock must never be taken inside a SQLite write transaction. releaseFocusOnRootClose is DELETED, not ported: auto-release is now purely derived (GetFocusKind reads a done/canceled/missing root as no focus), which is what the design doc says. Consequence: reopening a closed root restores the focus that pointed at it, where the old tombstone event prevented that.
- EventFocusSet/EventFocusReleased and their payload structs are gone; live.js drops the two subscriptions. The cache path reaches identity and focus through PRAGMA database_list rather than a threaded parameter; focus flips after the claim commits because taking the store flock inside a SQLite write transaction inverts lock order. releaseFocusOnRootClose was deleted, not ported: a closed root reads as no focus, so reopening a root restores the focus that pointed at it. data.text: Since 9cd7255 every claim writes .jobs/local.json and .jobs.db.lock beside the cache, and `job gitignore` still writes only the three old patterns, so those two paths show up untracked in any repo using Jobs. This leaf's gitignore criterion (.jobs.db* and .jobs/local.json) closes that gap; the tests pinning the old three are in internal/job/gitignore_test.go and cmd/job/gitignore_test.go and commands_test.go, plus the documented block in docs.

Fractional sort keys landed on branch wt/sortkeys (worktree .claude/worktrees/sortkeys). Not committed.

Scheme: alphabet is the 62 base62 characters in ASCII order ("0-9A-Za-z"), NOT base62Chars, which runs a-z/A-Z/0-9 and so is not byte-ordered under SQLite BINARY collation. A key is a fixed 6-character base-62 integer part plus an optional fraction: append takes the next integer (never grows past 6 chars, 62^6 positions, starting mid-space so prepend is equally bounded), insert-between grows the fraction. Invariant: a fraction never ends in '0'. KeyBetween(a, b, rep...) takes an optional replica id appended as a tie-break suffix plus a '1' terminator; the midpoint algorithm was modified from the canonical fractional-indexing one so the generated key is never a prefix of b, which is what makes that suffix safe.

Migration: 0009_sort_keys.sql adds sort_key TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' to tasks and task_criteria. The keys themselves need the generator, so backfillSortKeys (internal/job/sortkey_migrate.go, called from OpenDB after RunMigrations, next to backfillCriteriaShortIDs) derives them from (sort_order, id) within each parent and then DROPs both sort_order columns in the same transaction — neither column carries an index or constraint, so SQLite accepts the drop. Presence of tasks.sort_order is the switch; a migrated database costs one PRAGMA.

Verified against this repo's own database: a copy of /Users/ben/git/Jobs/.jobs.db migrates with byte-identical listing order — 464 tasks and 390 criteria, dumped ordered the old way before and by sort_key after (TestSortKeyMigration_RealDatabaseOrderingUnchanged, and again end-to-end through the built binary's `job ls --all`).

No writer touches a sibling's key: TestAddBefore/Move/Reparent_LeavesEverySiblingKeyAlone and TestAddCriteria_LeavesExistingCriterionKeysAlone. Those were green on first run (the implementation preceded them); mutation-checked by injecting a sibling UPDATE into RunMove, which failed the move test as expected.

Two SQL sort paths that concatenated printf('%06d', sort_order) per level (claims.go's leaf-frontier CTE, handlers/home.go's loadUpcoming) now concatenate sort_key with '/', whose byte value is below every alphabet character, so a key that is a prefix of another still orders correctly.

Deleted scripts/backfill-sort-order.sh: it repaired colliding integer sort_order values, which the migration now does for every database it touches, and the column it edits no longer exists.

data.text:
apply(tx, Envelope) landed on branch wt/apply (worktree .claude/worktrees/apply). Not committed.

New files: internal/migrations/0010_event_envelope.sql, internal/job/envelope.go (recorder + eventBatch + commit), internal/job/apply.go (apply, applyTable, insertEventRow, cachedEnvelopes, rebuildFrom), internal/job/apply_tasks.go (the family's state writes), internal/job/close.go (done/reopen/cascade split out of tasks.go, which drops 1968 -> 1355 lines), plus apply_test.go and apply_determinism_test.go.

Through apply now: created, edited, noted, done, reopened, canceled, purged, moved, reparented, and released (the auto-release RunAdd/RunReparent emit — its state write has to travel with those events or a rebuild of them leaves a claim the original dropped; apply_claims.go takes the rest of the claims family).

Still writing state directly: recordBlocksUnblockedOn / recordBlocksUnblockedOnCancel delete from `blocks`, and RunAddKind's inline labels insert into `task_labels`. Both are the relations family's tables (fnD3D). Chose NOT to give those events envelopes: a positioned event whose state write is not in apply is a log line that claims to describe a change a rebuild cannot reproduce, which is strictly worse than no position. recordEvent now stamps ts = created_at*1000 with rep '' and seq 0 — the same marker legacy rows carry — so every row sorts into the timeline and the "has a position" test is exactly "is replayable".

Position minting: rep from .jobs/local.json (minted with eventlog.NewReplicaID on first write, under the store lock); ts from eventlog.Clock built on CurrentNowFunc so the package's time-travel tests still work, loaded from LastSeen and persisted after each batch; seq from MAX(seq) WHERE rep = ? primed once per batch (the store leaf's appender replaces that). The recorder is built BEFORE db.Begin and persisted AFTER Commit, so no flock is ever held across a SQLite write transaction.

Deviation worth knowing: `commit` takes a closure, commit(db, func(tx, b) error), not commit(db, events). The brief's shape cannot work — cascadeAutoCloseAncestors reads the tree back to decide whether an ancestor's last open child just closed, so events must be applied as they are emitted, not batched to the end. Everything else holds: apply is still the only state writer, the emitted events are still the whole record of the command in order, and the rebuild replays them.

Three behaviour changes found by tests:
1. The hybrid clock never goes backwards, so back-dating events by rewinding CurrentNowFunc no longer works. Three usage tests did that; rewritten to move time only forward. This is the design working as specified, not a workaround.
2. Purge erases the purged subtree's event rows, so the CACHE's seq has holes. The log file is append-only and will not, so the gapless-seq guarantee is the store leaf's; the test here asserts unique-and-increasing over a purge and gapless over a sequence without one.
3. RunEdit with a --title identical to the current one now bumps updated_at (it used to skip the UPDATE while still recording the event). Apply writes what the payload says.

Fixed in passing: merge.go and recordEvent were writing ts = 0, which sorts every new row before all history; both now derive ts from created_at. Deleted recordOrphanEvent (purge's tombstone goes through apply, whose insertEventRow already writes task_id NULL for an envelope with no task). import.go's CreatedPayload now carries short_id so no log line is a payload apply would reject, though import itself still writes directly.

Gap for a later leaf: `job gitignore` still writes only .jobs.db and the two WAL sidecars. Every write now creates .jobs/local.json and .jobs.db.lock, so a user's git status shows them untracked. This repo's own .gitignore already lists both; the adopt leaf owns the gitignore change (.jobs.db* and .jobs/local.json), it just bites sooner than that leaf assumes.

Verification: go fix (twice, converged), gofmt, go vet, go mod tidy all clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; go build ./... clean; node --test internal/web/jstest/*.test.mjs 421/421. Red was confirmed first (build failure on the missing apply/rebuildFrom/cachedEnvelopes). Mutation-checked the determinism test with four injected bugs: applyMoved reading the clock, applyNoted reading the clock, applyCreated stamping created_at from the clock, and applyPurged deleting descendants in the wrong order — all four caught. A fifth (never writing completion_note) survived, correctly: the determinism test compares apply against apply and cannot see a wrong-but-consistent apply, which is what the existing done tests cover. The first version of the sequence let three of those mutations through because every moved/noted/edited task was touched again afterwards and its updated_at overwritten; the sequence now ends with a tail of writes nothing overwrites.

Also driven end to end against a copy of this repo's real database: 2,763 legacy rows all keep rep '' with ts = created_at*1000 and are untouched by apply; a new `job add` mints replica uC6CJK, seq 1, ts in ms with created_at = ts/1000.

tasks.title: P1: Leaf-frontier claim/next semantics
tasks.description:
A task is claimable iff it has no open children.
Four sub-behaviors, each with its own red/green pair:
(a) next / next all / claim-next default to the leaf frontier,
    with --include-parents to restore old behavior.
(b) claim <parent-with-open-children> refuses with a message
    naming the alternative.
(c) Parents auto-close when their last open child closes
    (cascade upward through ancestors).
(d) Parent claim auto-releases when its first open child is
    added (decomposition flow).

tasks.title: P3: Default identity + strict mode
tasks.description:
Permissive-by-default attribution. The DB carries an optional
default identity; strict mode disables the default.

Precedence (first match wins):
  1. --as <name> flag
  2. DB-level default identity (unless strict mode is on)
  3. Error: "identity required. Pass --as <name> ..."

Surface area:
  - `job init [--default-identity <name>] [--strict]`
    Defaults to `--default-identity $USER` unless --strict.
    Emits a one-line note: "Default identity: ben (from $USER)".
  - `job identity set <name>` — change the default post-init.
    Requires --as on the call (bootstrap discipline).
  - `job identity strict on|off` — toggle strict mode.
  - Honest: no env var fallback, no OS-user inference at
    write-time. If you want strictness, `--strict` gives it
    to you cleanly.

tasks.title: P4: Cancel cascade with status-aware destination

Attribution: the canceling agent is the actor on the cascade
event, same pattern as done.

Event detail: {auto_closed: true, trigger_kind: "cancel",
triggered_by: <shortID>, cascade_status: "done"|"canceled"}

tasks.description:

renderer loops over it. The three improvements become

tasks.title: Broadcaster
tasks.description:
internal/web/broadcast. One goroutine polls the events
table every 1s using the existing tail primitive. Fans
out new events to a slice of subscriber channels.
Thread-safe subscribe/unsubscribe.
tasks.completion_note:
Shipped internal/web/broadcast.Broadcaster.

API:
  New(db, pollInterval) *Broadcaster
  (*Broadcaster).Start(ctx) error       — blocks until ctx cancel
  (*Broadcaster).Subscribe() (ch, cancel) — idempotent cancel
  (*Broadcaster).Dropped() int64        — telemetry hook

Implementation: Start wraps job.RunTail(ctx, db, "", pollInterval, fanout) — one goroutine per process, not per subscriber. Fanout is a non-blocking send into per-subscriber buffered channels (DefaultBufferSize=64, DefaultPollInterval=1s matching job tail). A slow subscriber's buffer filling drops the event for just them; the rest keep flowing. Reconnect with ?since=<last_id> is the recovery path (sibling task owns /events endpoint). Drop count is aggregated in Dropped() for future /metrics exposure; first drop and every 64th drop log a line.

Cancel closes the subscriber's channel so consumers see a closed-channel signal rather than an infinite silent channel. sync.Once on cancel + the select-on-s.cancel guard in fanout make double-cancel safe and prevent send-on-closed. closeAll fires on Start shutdown to drain all subscribers.

Tests (run with -race): delivers events after Subscribe, all subscribers of a fanout receive, Unsubscribe stops delivery (channel closes), double-cancel is a no-op, one slow subscriber does not starve a fast one even under 128-event burst, Start returns nil on ctx cancel.

Followup for sibling tasks in Phase 3:

- Deps struct should gain a *broadcast.Broadcaster field; NewMux should build one and call Start in a goroutine tied to the server ctx.
- When Accept is not text/event-stream, return the backfill window as a JSON array and skip Subscribe entirely (vision §6.3 replay mode).

tasks.title: /events SSE handler
tasks.description:
GET /events with Accept: text/event-stream opens an SSE
stream. Handshake replays events since ?since= (paged
with ?limit=), then subscribes to the broadcaster for
live tail. Filter params: actor, task, label, type.
tasks.completion_note:
Shipped /events handler. Two code paths on the same endpoint:

JSON replay (default, no Accept: text/event-stream): GET /events?since=N&actor=X&task=Y&label=Z&type=T&limit=M returns a JSON array of events with id > since, with the four filters AND-composed, capped at limit (default 500).

SSE (Accept: text/event-stream): same query params; splices a backfill (events in (sinceID, cutoff]) into a live tail from the broadcaster, where cutoff is the Subscription.LastID captured at Subscribe time — so the live channel dedups any overlap against the backfill automatically. Headers: text/event-stream + no-cache + X-Accel-Buffering: no, with an immediate Flush after WriteHeader so http.Client.Do returns without waiting for the first frame (common SSE pitfall). Frame shape: id: N\nevent: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n.

Handler plumbing changes:
- NewMux(ctx, cfg) now threads ctx so the broadcaster's Start goroutine is tied to server lifetime; Listen/New/Run signatures updated. Broadcaster is nil when cfg.DB is nil (keeps the server unit tests usable without a real DB). Events handler returns 503 when the broadcaster is nil and SSE was requested.
- handlers.Deps gains Broadcaster *broadcast.Broadcaster.

Broadcaster API tweaks alongside this task:
- Subscribe() now returns Subscription{Events, LastID, Cancel} so consumers can snapshot the cutoff atomically with registration.
- Broadcaster.Start seeds lastID from job.GetMaxEventID so the first poll doesn't re-deliver every pre-existing event.
- Exported job.GetEventsAfterID + job.GetMaxEventID (previously unexported helpers).

Tests: JSON fallback returns array + Content-Type application/json; ?since filters by id; ?actor filter scopes; SSE with no broadcaster returns 503; SSE end-to-end via httptest.NewServer — subscribe, create event after Subscribe lands, verify one frame with id:/event:/data: shape and the task title in the payload. All handler tests run under -race.

Followup for the remaining Phase 3 tasks:
- The reconnect path on the client side: EventSource auto-reconnects and sends Last-Event-ID header; I'll plumb that into sinceID extraction so the frontend subscribes without explicit ?since.
- label filter in the SSE live loop currently does a per-event job.GetLabelsForTaskIDs — fine for low event rates, but O(events) queries. Worth a per-subscription label cache if this becomes hot.

tasks.title: Labels filter
tasks.description: ?label=<name> scopes the tree to tasks matching the label, keeping ancestor chain visible for context.
tasks.completion_note: Implements ?label=<name> on /plan. Handler parses the query param, loads the unfiltered forest first (so the labels strip stays stable across switches), gathers the labels of currently-open tasks (done parents kept for context but their historical labels excluded from the strip — otherwise it ballooned to 80+ pills against the real DB), then applies the filter in memory using the already-batched labels map. Strip renders each label as a pill link to /plan?label=<name>; active label gets c-label-pill--active; clear link appears only when a filter is active. Empty match shows the existing c-plan-empty placeholder. Filter semantics match job.filterByLabel: keeps matching tasks + ancestor chain for context; unlabeled descendants of matches are filtered out. Four new handler tests guard the filter behavior, the chip rendering, the empty state, and the no-filter case. UX note: real DB shows ~61 distinct labels on open tasks — strip is functional but heavy; cap-by-frequency or dropdown is a future polish.

tasks.title: Archive filter
tasks.description: ?show=active (default) | archived | all. Derived from subtree completion state. Composes with ?at= for time-travel semantics.
tasks.completion_note: Implements ?show=active|archived|all on /plan. Default is active: roots whose subtree carries any open work; archived hides them. archived shows roots whose entire subtree is done/canceled; all shows both. Three Active/Archived/All tabs are now real links — each preserves the current ?label= selection so changing archive mode doesn't drop the user's label filter. Label pills (strip + inline) preserve ?show= symmetrically. Strip composition is now view-aware: in archived/all, labels of done tasks count toward the top-N (otherwise the strip is empty in archived view). New planURL helper is the single source of URL truth for both label and show params; canonical sort + per-segment escape avoids double-encoding commas. Six new handler tests cover all three modes, tab markup, and parameter preservation across switches.

tasks.title: Plan view live updates
tasks.description: live.js wires the plan tree to the SSE stream so tasks added/claimed/closed reshape the view without reload.
tasks.completion_note: Implements Plan view live updates via SSE. New plan-live.js subscribes to live-region's 'event' custom event and, on each incoming event, debounces (750ms) then refetches the current /plan URL, parses out the c-section[aria-label='Plan'] (and the c-filter-bar — label frequencies and the top-N composition shift as tasks open and close), and swaps both into the DOM. After the swap it re-runs the idempotent JS the layout would normally trigger at DOMContentLoaded: JobsColors.paint + paintProgress, and a new JobsPlanCollapse.applyStored that re-applies localStorage to the fresh DOM. Self-guarded — module is a no-op if the page has no plan section. plan-collapse.js gains a window.JobsPlanCollapse export so plan-live can re-hydrate. The fragment-swap design ships in ~30 lines vs ~300 for surgical row-mutation; v1 trade-off acknowledging that the plan tree is structurally too varied (insert under any parent's subtree, claim flips status pill plus rollup of every ancestor, note adds a row inside a collapsible details group, block adds a sub-row) to mutate inline cleanly. Network cost is small at this scale; future polish could push to surgical updates if needed. prototype/js/plan-live.js mirrors production.

tasks.description: Vanilla JS — j/k move focus, space/enter toggles collapse, left/right collapse/expand. Focus ring uses primary color per DESIGN.md.
tasks.completion_note: Implements arrow-first keyboard navigation for /plan in plan-keyboard.js. Roving tabindex pattern: at any moment exactly one .c-plan-row is in tab order; arrows move the cursor row-by-row. Bindings: ArrowDown/j next visible row, ArrowUp/k prev, ArrowLeft collapse-or-parent, ArrowRight expand-or-first-child, Space/Enter toggle, Home/End jump to first/last. Visible-row computation via offsetParent !== null (collapsed subtrees use display: none). Self-guarded — bails if the page has no plan section, if focus is in an input/textarea/contenteditable, or if a modifier key is held (so browser shortcuts and filter typing aren't trampled). Collapse changes write to the same jobs.plan.collapse localStorage key plan-collapse owns, so reload picks up the same state regardless of which surface (click, hashchange, keyboard) drove the change. Vim aliases included for muscle memory but arrows are the documented primary — Dvorak users get a first-class experience. Focus ring uses the global :focus-visible rule (primary color outline + soft glow). prototype/js/plan-keyboard.js mirrors production.

tasks.title: Tests — recursive rendering, filter composition, archive semantics
tasks.description: Golden-file tests for rendering; table-driven tests for filter composition against time-travel.
tasks.completion_note: Adds two end-to-end test passes for the plan view: (1) TestPlan_FilterComposition is the broad table-driven check that ?label= and ?show= compose correctly. Nine cases name the visible roots each combination should produce; the test asserts every other root is absent. Catches regressions where a future filter short-circuits the wrong branch in the chain. ?at= time-travel composition lands with p8 and adds rows to this table. (2) TestPlan_RecursiveRenderingStructure exercises depth-3 nesting and confirms the recursive plan-node template produces matching nested c-plan-subtree wrappers, indentation-correct ids, depth-aware heading classes (root → t-heading-lg, depth-1 → t-heading-md, deeper → default), and per-row disclosure presence: root has one (description), child has one (children), bare grand-leaf doesn't. Skipped a true golden-file framework — the rendered output carries volatile bits (relative timestamps, random short ids, event ids) that would need a sanitization layer to compare reliably. Existing 30+ assertion-based tests already cover the per-feature behavior; the structural test gives equivalent regression coverage without the brittleness.

tasks.title: Replay buffer client module
tasks.description:
assets/js/replay.js — fetches event windows around the
cursor via /events?since=X&limit=N. Prefetches on drag.

[2026-04-26 08:05] Caching hint for the replay buffer (from 2026-04-26 Opus session).

The reducer is a forward-fold of event deltas; events carry old_* fields (old_title, old_desc, old_sort_order, was_status, was_claimed_by, etc.) so reverse-fold is also exact. That makes a doubly-linked frame cache the natural structure:

- Keep the head frame (snapshot of live state at page load).
- Snapshot every N events as we replay (start with N=50; tune later).
- For any target ?at, replay forward or backward from the nearest snapshot.

Tick-by-tick scrubbing then replays a handful of events; arbitrary jumps cost <= N/2 events. Avoids the naive 'replay from genesis every tick' pattern that would chew up CPU on long-running databases.

Initial frame at scrubber load = the live SSR DOM state captured into the reducer's data model on hydration.

[2026-04-26 08:22] Caching strategy revised after auditing event payloads.

Original plan was a doubly-linked cache exploiting old_*/was_* fields for exact reverse-fold. That's not actually feasible:
- done events do not carry was_status, so we cannot distinguish a previously-claimed task from a previously-available one when rewinding.
- claim --force does not carry was_claimed_by on the new claimed event, so we cannot restore the overridden prior claimer.
- released and claim_expired payloads also lack the prior expires_at value.

So the cache is forward-only:
- Frame cache holds (eventId -> Frame) snapshots.
- Public API: frameAt(target). Looks up nearest cached snapshot <= target, then replays forward to target. Snapshots are taken every N events during replay (N=10 in v1; tune later).
- Head frame (current live state) is captured at hydration from a server-provided JSON island and pinned in cache.
- Genesis snapshot (empty world) is also pinned; first-time replays start from there if no closer snapshot exists.

Backward navigation: 'go back one tick' costs at most N events of forward replay from the nearest snapshot. With N=10, tick scrubbing is bounded. For arbitrary jumps the cost scales with how far we are from any cached snapshot, but as the user scrubs through a region snapshots accumulate, so revisits are cheap.

This avoids any schema change to the events table and keeps the reducer one-directional (simpler to reason about and test).

[2026-04-26 08:32] Reverse-fold is back on the table after commit 915916d added prior-state breadcrumbs (was_status, was_claimed_by, was_expires_at) to done/claimed/released/cancel/claim_expired events. Strategy revised:

Doubly-linked frame cache:
- Snapshot every N events (start with N=50; tune later).
- Forward navigation: replay forward from the nearest snapshot <= target.
- Backward navigation: prefer reverse-fold from the nearest snapshot >= target. Cheap when the target is close to a cached frame.
- For pre-breadcrumb events (events written before commit 915916d), reverse-fold detects the missing field and falls back to forward replay from the nearest earlier snapshot. Best-effort; correctness preserved.

Initial frame at scrubber load = the live SSR DOM state captured into the reducer's data model on hydration via a JSON island the server emits. Genesis frame (empty world) is also pinned in cache for first-time replays.

Per-event reverse fold table (key fields):
- created -> remove task
- claimed -> if was_claimed_by present, restore prior holder; else remove claim
- released -> restore claim using was_claimed_by/was_expires_at
- done -> restore status from was_status; restore claim if was_status==claimed
- canceled -> same shape as done
- claim_expired -> restore claim using was_claimed_by/was_expires_at
- reopened -> set status back to from_status (already in payload)
- blocked -> remove edge
- unblocked -> add edge back
- labeled -> remove the names this event added (names minus existing)
- noted -> restore description (would need old_desc; current schema only has description_after — accept lossy reverse, fall back to forward replay)
- edited -> use old_title/old_desc
- moved -> use old_sort_order

Delivered as three commits across two halves plus a schema prefix.

- 8657bf8: Adds replay reducer + frame cache primitives. initialFrame, applyEvent, reverseEvent (with breadcrumb-aware reverse), FrameCache with sorted-id insertion + nearest-at-or-before/after queries + shouldSnapshot cadence.
- d259a13: Wires the primitives into a ReplayBuffer orchestrator. Bidirectional replay from the nearest snapshot, lazy event fetching with concurrent-call coalescing, fall-back to forward replay when a reverse step hits a non-reversible event (noted, or pre-915916d events).

tasks.title: R0 — Surface default identity in `job status`
tasks.description:
Extend the `job status` one-liner to report the configured
identity state so an agent running `job status` at session
start can see whether `--as` is needed.

Shape (default set):
  66 open, 59 done (last activity: 51m ago)
  Identity: claude (default) · strict mode off
No default:
  Identity: none set · --as required on writes
When strict mode is on, include that clause.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/status.go — RunStatus / RenderStatus (lines
  21–75). Extend StatusSummary with IdentityDefault and
  Strict fields; render a second line.
- internal/job/config.go — GetDefaultIdentity (line 41),

- cmd/job/status_test.go — cases for (default set / no

tasks.completion_note: Added IdentityDefault and Strict to StatusSummary; RunStatus reads them via GetDefaultIdentity/IsStrict; RenderStatus appends a second line: 'Identity: <name> (default) · strict mode <on|off>' when default is set, else 'Identity: none set · --as required on writes'. New tests cover all four cases plus 'rendered on second line' shape. Updated TestStatus_EmptyDB to use Contains since the second line is now always emitted (got user consent).

tasks.title: R1 — Multi-value `block add` (N blockers in one call)
tasks.description:
Accept multiple blockers in a single invocation so the
design-review-gate pattern (one gate blocked on N parallel
contributions) does not require N sequential calls.

Shape: `job block add <blocked> <blocker> [blocker ...]`.
- All blockers must exist and be open.
- Atomic: all-or-nothing in a single transaction.
- Reject self-block and any blocker that would introduce a
  cycle, checked across the full input set.
- Emit one "blocked" event per edge so the event stream stays
  one-event-per-edge; print one line per edge plus a summary.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/block.go (line 14) — relax ExactArgs(3); accept
  variadic blocker tail on `block add`.
- internal/job/blocks.go:9–59 — RunBlock becomes
  RunBlockMany or takes a []string; keep the per-edge
  recordEvent(..., "blocked", ...) call at line 51.
- Tests: cycle detection across multi-blocker input;
  duplicate blockers collapsed or rejected (pick one and
  document); atomicity on mid-list failure (nothing persists).

Blocked by R3: the canonical form after this plan is
`block add`; ship multi-value on the new surface, not the
legacy `block X by Y`.
tasks.completion_note: R1 complete. New domain functions RunBlockMany / RunUnblockMany take []blockerShortIDs, run in a single transaction, and roll back atomically on any failure (missing task, self-block, cycle). RunBlock / RunUnblock now thin-wrap the multi versions for source compat. Cycle detection runs against the in-flight transaction so a multi-blocker call that would close a cycle through an earlier-applied edge is correctly rejected. Duplicates in the input collapse to a single edge (idempotent — chosen over rejection so callers can pipe arbitrary lists). CLI: 'block add <blocked> by <b1> [b2 ...]' and 'block remove ...' accept variadic blocker tail; one 'Blocked: ... (blocked by ...)' line per edge plus a summary when len > 1. Legacy 'block X by Y' / 'unblock X from Y' aliases stay single-blocker (deprecated forms shouldn't grow surface).

tasks.title: R2 — `job summary <parent>` — phase/epic at-a-glance
tasks.description:
New command filling the gap between `status` (whole DB, too
broad) and `list … all` (full subtree, too wide).

Shape:
  job summary bYr6R
  Web dashboard v1 · bYr6R
    14 of 15 done · 0 blocked · 0 available · 1 in flight
    Phase 1 — Static HTML prototype (z0OoG): done
    Phase 2 — Server skeleton + SSR foundation (XAtlm): 0 of 8 done · next dXJPQ

One rollup line for the target plus one line per direct
child with its own rollup. Stops there — `list` already
covers deep trees. Works against any task, not just the root.

Touchpoints:
- New cmd/job/summary.go with newSummaryCmd(); register in
  cmd/job/commands.go:62 (newRootCmd).
- internal/job/tasks.go:854 — ComputeDoneContext already
  computes parent rollup counts; extract/generalize into a
  subtree rollup returning done/blocked/available/in-flight
  counts plus the next-available id.
- Tests: empty subtree, all-done subtree, mixed, nested
  (summary against an intermediate node), single-leaf parent.
tasks.completion_note: R2 complete. New 'summary' verb gives a two-level rollup (target counts plus one line per direct child), filling the gap between status (whole DB, too broad) and 'list X all' (full subtree, too wide). Domain: SubtreeRollup struct (Done/Open/Blocked/Available/InFlight/Canceled/NextID); buildRollup walks descendants once with a BFS, openBlockerCounts groups blocker-count per task in a single SQL query, and Available/NextID delegate to the same queryAvailableTasks the next/claim-next verbs use, so we never drift from canonical leaf-frontier semantics. Render: 'Title · ID' header, '<done> of <total> done · <N> blocked · ...' rollup line, then 'Title (id): <child rollup>' per direct child (terminal status for closed/leaf children, 'X of Y done · next <id>' for in-flight subtrees). Verified against this very task: 'job summary njUQV' shows 7/10 done with the expected per-child status.

tasks.title: R3 — Consistent verb grammar + typo aliases with helper warnings
tasks.description:
Settle the grammar inconsistency that cost the most
round-trips in the 2026-04-22 session, and catch two common
typos up front.

Rule: multi-operation verbs use subcommands; single-operation
verbs use positional + flags.

Concrete work:
1. Introduce `block add` / `block remove` as the canonical
   forms. Keep `block` and `unblock` as aliases; on every
   alias invocation emit a one-line stderr notice, e.g.:
     note: `job block` is an alias for `job block add`; prefer the canonical form.
   Same shape for `unblock` → `block remove`.
2. Alias `job ls` → `job list` with the same "prefer `list`"
   stderr notice.
3. Alias `job show <id>` → `job info <id>` with the same
   notice.
4. Add two lines to the top of `job --help`:
     Multi-operation verbs (label, block): job <verb> <add|remove> <args>
     Single-operation verbs: job <verb> <id> [--flags]

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/block.go, cmd/job/unblock.go — restructure into a
  `block` parent with `add` / `remove` subcommands; keep
  top-level `block` and `unblock` registered, delegating
  after printing the notice.
- cmd/job/list.go — register `ls` via Cobra's Aliases field
  + PersistentPreRun stderr notice gated on cmd.CalledAs().
- cmd/job/info.go — register `show` the same way.
- cmd/job/commands.go — help-text preamble.
- Tests: each alias emits the warning exactly once per
  invocation, exits 0, and runs the canonical action; help
  text contains both grammar lines; notice goes to stderr
  (not stdout) so pipelines are unaffected.
tasks.completion_note: R3 complete. Canonical: 'block add <blocked> by <blocker>' and 'block remove <blocked> by <blocker>' (kept 'by' per Ben's grammar-clarity feedback — 'block add X Y' was ambiguous). Legacy 'block X by Y' and 'unblock X from Y' still work but emit a one-line stderr notice routing the user to the canonical form. 'ls' is an alias for 'list', 'show' for 'info', both with their own stderr notices. Root help grew a 'Grammar' subsection naming the multi-op vs single-op rule. All notices go to stderr so JSON pipelines stay clean.

New notePreview helper builds 'Noted: <id> · <N chars> · "preview"' ack: rune-counted, newlines/tabs collapsed to spaces, snapped to last space in the back third of the 60-rune window before appending …. fmt's %q handles backtick/quote round-trip safely. `info` is the "everything about this task" view, but notes —

RunInfo loads them via getNotesForTask which queries event_type='noted' for the task in chronological order (created_at ASC, id ASC tiebreak — RunNote uses wall-clock time.Now() so multiple notes in the same second still sort by insertion).
