tasks.title: R6 — Stop hard-wrapping prose in `job info`
tasks.description:
`info` today hard-wraps description (and, post-R5, notes) at
80 columns, breaking words on wider terminals and embedding
newlines that make piping lossy. Modern CLI convention (git,
gh, kubectl, cargo) is to emit raw prose and let the
terminal reflow.

Shape: drop the hard-wrap on prose fields (description, note
bodies). Emit each paragraph as a single logical line; keep
real author-supplied newlines (bullet lists inside a note).
Tables and column-aligned output — child lists, label rows —
keep their current formatting; this rule applies to prose
only.

If a future pager/printer workflow wants the wrapped shape,
gate it behind an opt-in `--wrap <n>` flag rather than
making it the default.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/format.go:155–199 — RenderInfoMarkdown; locate
  the wrap helper and restrict its scope (or remove it for
  prose fields).
- Tests: long-paragraph description survives intact on both
  narrow and wide pseudo-terminals; embedded newlines
  preserved; tabular rows still column-aligned.

Independent of R5; if both ship, this rule covers the new
Notes section too.
tasks.completion_note: R6 complete. Root cause: hard-wrap was in source text (YAML imports preserve author-supplied newlines); renderer dutifully emitted them. Fix unwraps at render time. New unwrapProse helper: collapses single \n inside a paragraph to space, preserves blank-line paragraph breaks, keeps bullet (- / *) and numbered (1.) list lines on their own line. Applied to Description and note bodies in RenderInfoMarkdown. Tabular fields (Children counts, Labels row) untouched. Verified job info njUQV now renders the description on one logical line.

tasks.title: R7 — Drop `note:` body from `list` parentheticals
tasks.description:
Done tasks currently render as
  (note: <500–1200 chars>, labels: X, Y)
burying the label scan target behind a wall of note text.
Notes belong in `info` (see R5); `list` should be
structural.

Shape: remove the `note: <body>` clause from the
parenthetical. Keep every other component — `labels: …`,
`blocked on …`, `(canceled)`, `(reason: …)` for canceled

tasks.title: Short-flag conventions — audit and align
tasks.description:
Audit short flags across the CLI and add the ones an agent/human would reflexively guess — but avoid letters with strong established meanings elsewhere.

Leading case: cancel --reason needs a short form (guessed on 2026-04-22 while drafting project/2026-04-22-opus-feedback.md; wasted a round-trip). Recommend -m (matches note -m '<text>', so 'short flag for free-text body' becomes a cross-command convention). Explicitly AVOID -r on cancel: -r overwhelmingly means 'recursive' in CLI muscle memory (rm, cp, grep, chmod), and cancel already cascades to subtasks, so -r would read as 'recursively cancel' or 'skip the cascade' rather than 'attach a reason.'

Approach:
1. Establish the convention: -m = free-text body (reason, note text, etc.). Avoid letters with strong prior meaning (-r recursive, -f force, -v verbose/version, -h help) unless the command's semantics actually match.
2. Enumerate every command's long flags and list the short forms Cobra would accept without clashing.
3. For each, decide whether the short form is obvious enough to be worth adding. Bias toward adding when the mapping is unambiguous (--desc -> -d if not taken, --label -> -l if not taken, --title -> -t).
4. Add the selected short flags alongside existing long forms (non-breaking).
5. Document the convention in --help or README so future additions stay consistent.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/cancel.go — add -m for --reason as the leading case.
- cmd/job/{add,note,claim,release,edit,label,block,...}.go — per-command audit.
- README commands table — short-form column, or inline in each command's flag list.

Tests: each new short flag parses to the same behavior as its long form; no regressions on existing short flags (e.g. -m on note); cancel -m routes text to --reason exactly as cancel --reason would.

Reasoning: -r is heavily loaded with 'recursive' in CLI muscle memory (rm, cp, grep, chmod), and cancel already cascades to subtasks, so -r would read as 'recursively cancel' or 'skip the cascade' rather than 'attach a reason.' Picking -m instead propagates the existing 'note -m' convention — short flag for free-text body — across commands that take free text.

findNextSibling (internal/job/tasks.go:1029) — candidates are sorted by sort_order (via getChildren ORDER BY sort_order), and the first unblocked wins. So when closing A unblocks a chain B→C→D alongside an always-unblocked-but-later sibling E, findNextSibling returns B, not E.

tasks.title: P7 — Auto-extend claim TTL on writes to the claimed task
tasks.description:
The bigger design move from the heartbeat retrospective.
When an agent writes to a task they currently hold
(`note`, `edit`, `label add`, `label remove`), the write
itself is an "I'm still working on this" signal — extend
the claim TTL by DefaultClaimTTLSeconds (P1's 30m).

Rules:
- Only extend; never shorten. If the existing
  claim_expires_at is further in the future than now+TTL,
  leave it alone.
- Only extend if the writing actor IS the current
  claim_holder. A `note` from a different actor must not
  silently override another agent's lock.
- Don't add a new event type. The existing `noted` /
  `edited` / `labeled` events already record the activity;
  the TTL bump is a side effect, not a notable event.

Decide before implementation: keep `job heartbeat` as a
low-level escape hatch for "I'm working but not writing"
(recommendation), or remove it entirely once auto-extend
covers the common case. If kept, demote it from the
quickstart and orchestration sections of README.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/tasks.go — RunNote, RunEdit (auto-extend
  block at the start of the transaction).
- internal/job/labels.go — RunLabelAdd, RunLabelRemove
  (same).
- New helper: maybeExtendClaim(tx, taskID, actor) used by
  all four call sites.
- Tests: extend on note as holder; no-op on note as
  non-holder; no-op when current expiry > now+TTL; combined
  with the P1 TTL bump.

tasks.title: Extract shared subtree-rollup renderer
tasks.description:

roots) and subtree scope (one parent). Behavior-preserving

RunSummary becomes a thin wrapper: resolve shortID to *Task, delegate. tasks.title: Tighten the rollup line
tasks.description:
Three refinements to the shared renderer's headline and
per-child block:

(1) Suppress zero-count status tokens. Render only non-zero
    states. "10 of 10 done · 0 blocked · 0 available · 0 in
    flight" collapses to "10 of 10 done".

(2) When the scope is fully complete (every descendant in
    done or canceled), append a closure timestamp to the
    rollup: "closed 2026-04-22 18:47". Source: latest
    done/canceled event within scope.

(3) In the per-child block, drop the trailing ": <status>"
    when the child's status matches the scope's dominant
    status (done when the scope is mostly-done; otherwise
    available). Surface only exceptions — claimed,
    canceled, blocked — so the eye lands on what deviates.
tasks.completion_note: Three refinements to the shared rollup renderer: (1) zero-count tokens suppressed — the scoreboard line now only renders non-zero states, so a fully-done scope reads 'N of N done' instead of 'N of N done · 0 blocked · 0 available · 0 in flight'. (2) Closure timestamp appended when the scope is fully complete: 'closed YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' sourced from the latest done/canceled event in the subtree via a new subtreeClosureTime helper. Only fires when Open == 0 and at least one descendant closed. (3) Per-child exception rule: leaf children whose status is 'done' or 'available' (the scope's natural background state) drop their trailing ': status' — the headline counts already cover them. Claimed, canceled, and blocked children retain their status to surface genuine exceptions. Added IsBlocked bool to SubtreeRollup so an 'available' task with an open blocker renders ': blocked'. 5 new tests, all red→green. Existing summary tests preserved.

tasks.completion_note: Added 'summary' as a cobra Alias on the status command with a PreRun that emits a stderr notice when CalledAs() == 'summary'. Matches the existing info/show and list/ls deprecation pattern exactly. Deleted cmd/job/summary.go since the old RunSummary→BuildRollup→RenderSummary path is already what status <id> takes after u5. Removed the newSummaryCmd() AddCommand. Stdout parity with status is automatic (same underlying codepath); test confirms. The JxyAc umbrella's unification arc is complete — status is the canonical verb, summary is a deprecated alias, and both forest-scope and subtree-scope paths share the BuildRollup engine.

tasks.title: Fix sort_order assignment in job import (+ backfill script)
tasks.description: job add sets sort_order correctly (0, 1, 2, ...) per sibling scope. job import does not — every imported task gets sort_order = 0, so all siblings collide. findNextSibling uses 's.SortOrder > closed.SortOrder' and returns no candidates when all siblings share 0, which breaks Next: hints on imported umbrellas. Fix: in internal/job/import.go's insert path, assign sequential sort_order at each level. Regression test: import a plan with N siblings, assert sort_orders are distinct and ascending. Backfill: one-shot script in scripts/ that renumbers per parent_id using id as tiebreak — not a schema migration since this only affects pre-existing local dbs.
tasks.completion_note: Fixed import.go's hardcoded sort_order=0 by threading sortOrder through the recursive insert function. Children start at 0 (no pre-existing siblings); imported roots start at nextSortOrderForParent(tx, parentDBID), which reads MAX(sort_order)+1 of existing siblings under the import's anchor so we don't collide when importing under an existing parent. Added three regression tests. Also shipped scripts/backfill-sort-order.sh — idempotent renumbering via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY parent_id ORDER BY id), scoped to colliding parent scopes only so job-move-adjusted scopes are preserved. Ran against live .jobs.db: 28 colliding scopes, 162 rows renumbered, 0 remaining. Full suite green.

tasks.title: Rewrite done-ack Next: as a hierarchical ancestor walk
tasks.description: Current ComputeDoneContext has three shape-specific fields (NextSibling, NextAfterParent, NextFallback) cobbled together. Replace with a single hierarchical walk: forward siblings of closed, then earlier siblings of closed, then walk up to parent and repeat (forward then earlier at each level). Only hit the global frontier when the closed task's entire root tree has no remaining claimable leaves. Keeps the agent within the closed task's subtree as long as there is work there — 'close D under C; next goes to E' rather than jumping to another umbrella. See conversation 2026-04-23 for full algorithm.
tasks.completion_note: Replaced NextSibling / NextAfterParent / NextFallback trio with a single Next *Task field on DoneContext, computed by new findNextClaimableLeafHierarchical helper in internal/job/tasks.go. Algorithm: starting at closed's parent, at each ancestor level scan forward siblings (sort_order strictly greater than came-from) then earlier siblings; descend into any parent-with-open-children to surface the first claimable leaf. Walk up until claimable work found or we exhaust closed's root tree; final pass treats the root-level forest as virtual siblings. Keeps SkippedBlocked / SkippedBlockedBy for the forward-sibling-blocked hint (only fires at the immediate parent level). Renderer simplified to one Next: branch. Two new red tests covered the distinct failures of the old path: close-highest-sibling-when-earlier-root-has-lower-sort_path, and walk-up-earlier-sibling-beats-decoy-root. Live probe of the user's example tree confirms close D returns Next: E. Full suite green.

tasks.title: CLI papercuts from the 2026-04-23 session

tasks.title: F1 — `job add` accepts `-l, --label <name>` (repeatable)
tasks.description:
Adding a task with labels currently requires two calls:
`job add ...` then `job label add <id> a b c`. Thread labels
into RunAdd's transaction so the created + labeled events
land atomically and the common case is one call.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/add.go — StringSliceVarP on --label/-l
- internal/job/tasks.go — RunAdd signature gains []string
  labels; insertLabels called inside the existing tx; the
  "labeled" event recorded alongside "created"
- Tests: add with one label, add with multiple labels, add

tasks.completion_note: Added -l/--label (StringArrayVarP, repeatable) to job add. RunAdd signature gains []string labels param; normalizeLabelNames + insertLabels called inside the existing tx; labeled event recorded atomically with created. Used StringArrayVarP (not StringSliceVarP) so comma-in-label validation actually fires.

tasks.title: F2 — Surface real YAML parse errors on import
tasks.description:
When a plan has a single fenced YAML block but the YAML
fails to parse (e.g., unquoted colon in a title
`title: Surface Next: in status output`), the current error
is the probe-loop's generic
`no YAML tasks: block found in <file>`. The real
`yaml.Unmarshal` error (mapping values not allowed, line N
col M) is swallowed.

Fix: in extractTasksYAML's probe loop, capture the most
recent yaml.Unmarshal error encountered in a candidate
fence. If no block yielded a usable tasks key AND at least
one candidate errored during Unmarshal, surface that error
(with its line/col) instead of the generic message.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/import.go — extractTasksYAML probe loop
  tracks lastErr; RunImport uses it when no block matched
- Tests: plan with one yaml fence and a bad-colon title
  asserts the error text names the parse failure (line
  number or "mapping values are not allowed")
tasks.completion_note: extractTasksYAML now returns (string, bool, error); probe loop captures lastErr from yaml.Unmarshal. RunImport surfaces that error when no block matched, instead of the generic 'no YAML tasks: block found' message.

tasks.title: F3 — `job list --grep <pattern>` for task search
tasks.description:
Agents fall back to `job list | grep` when searching by
title fragment, losing parent context and tree structure.
Add --grep <pattern> to list — case-insensitive substring
match by default — that composes with existing filters
(--label, --mine, --claimed-by) and respects --format=json.

Decide before implementation: substring-only, or allow
regex via a separate --grep-regex? Lean substring; it's
what every agent would try first.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/list.go — --grep StringVar, plumbed through
- internal/job/tasks.go — list query adds LIKE filter on
  title (or post-filter, depending on perf on larger dbs)
- Tests: substring match, case-insensitive, no match,
  composes with --label, respects --format=json shape
tasks.completion_note: Added --grep <pattern> to job list: case-insensitive substring match on title, post-filter, composes with --label/--mine/--claimed-by. filterByGrep recurses so a parent node is kept if any descendant matches. No output (not the empty-list message) when --grep returns nothing.

tasks.title: F4 — Preview `blockedBy` edges in `import --dry-run`
tasks.description:
Current dry-run lists imported tasks but omits the block
graph. Any plan with serialized chains can't be reviewed
end-to-end without the real import. Cycle detection runs
regardless, but the edges themselves are invisible.

Shape:
  <new-1>  A
  <new-2>  B (blocked on <new-1>)
  <new-3>  C (blocked on <new-2>)
For edges resolving to existing DB tasks, render the real
short-ID in place of the <new-N> placeholder.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/import.go — dry-run branch threads each
  parsed task's resolved blockedBy (local refs + existing
  DB short IDs) into the ImportedTask result
- cmd/job/import.go — md renderer extends each row with
  the parenthetical when the list is non-empty
- Tests: dry-run of a plan with blockedBy edges surfaces
  them; dry-run with a blockedBy to an existing task
  renders the real ID, not a placeholder
tasks.completion_note: Added BlockedBy []string to ImportedTask (json: blocked_by, omitempty). Dry-run branch resolves each parsedTask's blockedByResolved: local blockers get <new-N> placeholders, existing DB tasks get their real short ID. MD renderer appends '(blocked on X, Y)' parenthetical when non-empty.

tasks.title: F5 — Align `-m` verb ack shapes (design)
tasks.description:
`note` puts the body preview on the verb line
(`Noted: <id> · N chars · "preview"`) while `done` and
`cancel` put title on the verb line and preview on a
sub-line (`Done: <id> "Title"\n  note: N chars · "preview"`).
Both shapes make sense per-verb but a programmatic reader
needs two regexes.

This is a design conversation, not a mechanical fix. Stop
and ask before implementing. Options:
(a) Normalize note to the verb-line-plus-sub-line form
    (a dummy sub-line when there's nothing to qualify).
(b) Normalize done/cancel to the single-line form for the
    cases where there's no title context worth preserving.
(c) Leave as-is; document the two shapes in AGENTS.md.
tasks.completion_note: Implemented option (a): note ack now two-line form matching done/cancel. 'Noted: <id> "Title"\n  note: N chars · "preview"'. Fetches task title via GetTaskByShortID before RunNote (avoids signature change). Updated note_echo_test.go: new want strings, extractQuotedPreview now scans the note: sub-line.

tasks.title: F6 — `list --all` flag replaces the `all` positional
tasks.description:
`list [parent] [all]` uses a literal-string positional for
the "include closed" toggle. It composes awkwardly with
the other flags: `list JxyAc all --mine` vs the cleaner
`list JxyAc --all --mine`.

Breaking change. In BUILD mode per CLAUDE.md that's fine,
but it is user-visible. Option: keep the positional
undocumented for one release as a graceful migration.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/list.go — BoolVar --all, drop (or undocument) the
  positional
- internal/job/tasks.go — showAll bool is already plumbed;
  only the cmd layer changes
- Tests: existing `list <parent> all` call sites migrate
  to --all; keep one asserting the positional still works
  if we go the soft-migration route
tasks.completion_note: Added --all BoolVar to job list. Positional 'all' still accepted silently for graceful migration. Use: string updated to 'list [parent]'; Long description updated to --all. Composes with parent scoping, --label, --mine, --claimed-by.

tasks.title: CLI improvements from 2026-04-23 Sonnet session

Five agent-facing ergonomics fixes drawn from the R1–R5

Each child stands alone and can be landed in any order.
Tests are bundled with each change; the docs task at the

tasks.title: R1 — `status <id>` inlines task list when scoped
tasks.description:
When `status` is given an `<id>` argument, append the task
list for that subtree below the rollup summary — identical
to what `list <id>` would produce, without requiring a
second call. No filtering; for grep/label filtering the user
still calls `list` explicitly.

Shape:
  job status NpWZj
  NpWZj — CLI papercuts from 2026-04-23 session
    4 of 6 done · 0 blocked · 2 available
    Next: F5_id · Stale: none

  Tasks:
    - [x] F1_id  Add --label flag to `job add`
    - [ ] F5_id  Two-line note ack on success
    ...

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/status.go — when args[0] is set, call
  RunListFiltered for the subtree and append output below
  the summary block.
- internal/job/status.go — no changes needed; summary
  already scopes correctly.
- Tests: status <id> on a flat subtree shows both rollup
  and tree; status with no args is unchanged; status on a
  deep tree shows all levels (same depth default as list).
tasks.completion_note: Implemented in cmd/job/status.go — calls RunListFiltered for the subtree and renders with RenderMarkdownList below the rollup when args[0] is set. Three tests added: flat subtree, no-args unchanged, deep tree.

tasks.title: R2 — `reopen` auto-claims; add `--no-claim` escape hatch
tasks.description:
Reopening a task is almost always followed immediately by
claiming it. Make this atomic by default; add --no-claim
for the rare case where someone else will work the task.

Shape:
  job reopen F5_id
  Reopened: F5_id "Two-line note ack"
    claimed by alice (until 2026-04-23 15:42)

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/reopen.go — after RunReopen succeeds, call
  RunClaim unless --no-claim is set. Append the claim
  confirmation line to output.
- cmd/job/reopen.go — add BoolVar for --no-claim flag.
- internal/job/tasks.go — no internal change required;
  the command layer calls both in sequence.
- Tests: reopen auto-claims by default; --no-claim skips
  the claim step and omits the claim output line; reopening
  an already-open task still fails (unchanged); output
  format includes the claim line when claimed.
tasks.completion_note: reopen now auto-claims by default; --no-claim flag skips it. cascade suppresses auto-claim. Output includes task title. Updated two existing status-check tests to expect 'claimed' instead of 'available'.

tasks.title: R3 — Batch `job info <id> [id ...]`
tasks.description:
Accept multiple IDs so context on several related tasks
can be fetched in one call.

Shape: variadic args, rendered sequentially separated by
a blank line. --format json returns a JSON array.

Fail behavior: first invalid ID returns an error and stops
(fail-fast). This can be relaxed to "all-errors" later if
needed, but fail-fast is simpler to implement and easier
to reason about.

Touchpoints:
- cmd/job/info.go — change ExactArgs(1) to MinimumNArgs(1);
  loop over args; blank-line separator between tasks.
- cmd/job/info.go — --format json wraps results in a JSON

- internal/job/tasks.go — RunInfo is unchanged; the loop

- Tests: single ID (unchanged behavior); two IDs returns

tasks.completion_note: info cmd changed to MinimumNArgs(1), loops over args, blank-line separator, JSON wraps in array. Updated two existing JSON tests to unmarshal array.

tasks.title: R4 — Surface `decision`-labeled tasks in `job status`
tasks.description:
Tasks labeled `decision` represent questions that must be
answered before work can proceed. Today they are invisible
in status output — indistinguishable from normal open tasks.
Surfacing them in the status preamble (alongside Next: and
Stale:) gives agents and humans a reliable signal that a
human decision is pending.

Shape — new line in status preamble when any open task
carries the `decision` label:
  Next:     F5_id "Two-line note ack"
  Stale:    none
  Decision: D3_id "Choose auth strategy"

Multiple decision tasks: list all on separate lines.
Scoped status (status <id>): include only decision tasks
within that subtree.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/status.go — RunStatus: after computing
  Next and Stale, query for open tasks with label=decision
  scoped to the current subtree (or whole DB for unscoped).
  Populate a new DecisionTasks []TaskRef field on
  StatusSummary.
- internal/job/format.go — render Decision: lines in the
  preamble block. Empty slice → omit the section.
- Tests: decision-labeled open task surfaces; closed
  decision task does not; non-decision open task does not;
  scoped status only shows in-subtree decisions; multiple
  decision tasks each get a line.
tasks.completion_note: Added DecisionTasks []*Task to Summary struct; queryDecisionTasks in summary.go queries task_labels scoped to subtree or global; RenderSummary prints Decision: lines after Next:.

tasks.title: R5 — Replace RunListFiltered positional params with ListFilter struct
tasks.description:
RunListFiltered now has 7 positional parameters. Each new
filter feature costs a signature change and ~20 caller
updates. A filter struct caps that cost permanently.

Shape:
  type ListFilter struct {
      ParentID       string
      Depth          int
      ShowAll        bool
      ClaimedByActor string
      Label          string
      GrepPattern    string
  }
  func RunListFiltered(db *sql.DB, f ListFilter) ([]*TaskNode, error)

Breaking change to the internal API — acceptable in build
mode with zero external users.

Touchpoints:
- internal/job/tasks.go — replace the 7-arg signature;
  update the implementation (no behavioral change).
- All callers (~20 sites across 5 files):
  cmd/job/list.go, cmd/job/labels_test.go,
  cmd/job/short_flags_test.go, cmd/job/database_test.go,
  cmd/job/format_listparens_test.go — replace positional
  args with struct literals.
- Tests: full suite should pass without behavioral change.
  The test for the refactor is a green suite, not a new
  test case.
tasks.completion_note: Introduced ListFilter struct; replaced 7-arg signature; updated ~20 call sites across cmd/job and internal/job test files.

tasks.title: Docs sweep for R1–R5

tasks.title: BeiT0 review follow-ups
tasks.description: Three gaps surfaced during code review of the BeiT0 CLI improvements session.

tasks.title: Add TestReopen_Cascade_NoAutoClaim test

tasks.completion_note: Moved Decision: rendering from RenderSummary to the cmd layer (after Stale:), added TestStatus_CLI_Decision_OrderedAfterStale regression test

tasks.title: Add TestStatus_CLI_Decision_Claimed_StillSurfaces test
tasks.description: A claimed (not done/canceled) decision task should still surface as a Decision: line. The query is correct but the intent is untested — lock it in.

tasks.title: Blocked-by pills become in-page anchors
tasks.description: Row ids switch to id="task-<short>" and blocker pills link to #task-<short> instead of /tasks/<short>. Add a :target CSS highlight. The collapse-JS hooks hashchange to auto-expand ancestors of the anchor target so jumping into a collapsed done-subtree reveals the blocker. Also add title="<task title>" on blocker pills as a hover fallback.
tasks.completion_note: Every c-plan-row now carries id="task-<short>". Blocker pills switch from /tasks/<short> to #task-<short>, keeping the reader on the plan document. Blocker pills also render title="<blocker title>" so hovering reveals what the blocker is without navigation — useful when the blocker currently sits in a collapsed subtree. :target CSS reuses the existing .c-plan-row--selected treatment (raised background + 3px primary stripe on the left). Three new handler tests guard the anchor href, row id, and title attribute; two pre-existing rollup tests updated to use a new assertRowHasClass helper that tolerates attribute reshuffles. Expand-ancestors-on-hashchange behavior lands with E2ffo's collapse module.

tasks.title: Parent rows roll up to active when a descendant is claimed
tasks.description: A branch row whose own status is still-open (not done/canceled) renders as active when any descendant's display status is active. Done/canceled parents keep their own status — a closed branch stays closed even if a reopened descendant picks up life again. Emerged from p4-ssr review: with nothing claimed the tree looked monochrome todo, masking where work was happening. Implemented in buildPlanNodes, guarded by two tests.
tasks.completion_note: Shipped alongside p4-ssr. buildPlanNodes now bubbles 'active' from any active descendant onto an open parent; done/canceled parents are left alone. Two new tests: TestPlan_ParentRollsUpToActiveWhenDescendantIsClaimed (3-level chain, claim on grandchild → parent+child render active) and TestPlan_RollupDoesNotOverrideDoneParent (done parent with reopened+claimed child stays done).

tasks.title: Progress-bar display rules and collapse hiding
tasks.description:
Three cosmetic refinements to the plan view shipped on top of p4-ssr:
- colors.js skips progress-bar injection on rows with status done or canceled (redundant with the pill).
- colors.js skips injection when the subtree has nothing done and the row isn't active — a dormant todo with 0/N done adds noise. isActive checks the rollup class, so a todo parent with a claimed grandchild still shows the bar.
- CSS collapse rule broadens to hide everything inside .c-plan-row__title except the title-line, so the 'N of M tasks done' text (.c-plan-row__progress-text) folds away when the row is collapsed.
Also: PlanNode.Collapsible now covers 'has description or children', so leaf tasks with descriptions are collapsible too and done leaves fold up their description by default. Prototype/js/colors.js kept in sync.
tasks.completion_note: See description. Shipped in a single cosmetic commit on top of p4-ssr. Verified via the full test suite (the handler-side Collapsible change has dedicated tests; the JS and CSS hide rules are manual-verify only — no browser-test harness in this project).

tasks.title: Multi-select labels filter with All pill and inline-pill clicks
tasks.description:
Refines the labels filter shipped in PwNlo:
- Strip drops to top-5 labels by open-task frequency, plus any selected labels not in the top-5 (so a selection never orphans).
- Multi-select via comma-separated ?label=foo,bar (URL form). Filter logic is OR — tasks tagged with any selected label, plus ancestor chain.
- Leftmost 'All' pill clears the filter and is active when no labels are selected. Replaces the inline 'clear' text link.
- Inline label pills on task rows become clickable <a> links; click adds the label to the selection (no-op if already selected). Strip pills toggle in/out.
- Selected pills flip from ringed to filled (label-color background, white text). New CSS rule for .c-label-pill--active.
No JS needed — every pill href is server-pre-computed.
tasks.completion_note: Implements multi-select labels with All pill. Strip is top-5 labels by open-task frequency, plus any selected labels not in the top-5 (so a selection never orphans). Comma-separated ?label=foo,bar URL form (each label QueryEscape'd individually so commas stay literal). OR-semantic filter — task kept if it carries any selected label or any descendant does. All pill leftmost, points at /plan, --active when no selection. Strip pills toggle in/out of selection (sorted alphabetically for canonical URLs). Inline label pills on task rows are now <a> links; click adds the label to current selection (no-op if already in). New CSS: c-label-pill--active flips to filled (label-color background, white text) and c-label-pill--all uses neutral primary tint with caps-lockup font. Adopts the existing c-filter-bar / c-filter-bar__group / c-filter-bar__label structure from the Log view for visual consistency. Also fixes a regression: paintProgress in colors.js was painting progress bars + text on leaf rows that became Collapsible due to having a description (no children) — now requires an actual c-plan-subtree sibling, with notes-group correctly skipped. Eight new handler tests cover all the semantics.

tasks.title: Cap Log view's label chip strip to top N by frequency
tasks.description: Currently log.go's buildLabelChips emits one chip per label in DistinctLabels — same wall-of-pills problem the plan strip had before lxHYI. Cap to top 10 by open-task frequency, with the same 'always include selected' rule so an active filter never orphans.
tasks.completion_note: Adds OpenTaskLabelFreqs to the job package — one SQL query, returns label name → open-task count. Log handler now caps the Label chip strip to top 10 by that frequency, with the active label always included even if it would fall below the cap (so an active filter never orphans). Two new handler tests guard the cap and the active-label-included rule. The Plan view's pickStripLabels does the same thing in-memory; that one stays forest-walk-based since Plan already has the forest in scope, but both views agree on the underlying definition of 'currently in active circulation.'

tasks.title: Log view: scroll and pagination
tasks.description:
Two related Log-view ergonomics issues observed at ~893 events:
- Page just overflows into normal page-scroll, so the filter bar scrolls away. Needs either a sticky filter bar or a constrained scroll container so filters stay reachable.
- SSR currently renders ALL events for the task tree in one shot. Want pagination — likely server-side cursor (?before=<event_id>&limit=N) with infinite-scroll or load-more, mirroring the SSE replay shape (?since=, ?limit= already supported by p3-replay).
tasks.completion_note: Two pieces shipped together: (1) /log scroll: .c-log becomes the scroll container itself via flex: 1 + min-height: 0 + overflow: auto, so the filter bar above stays put while only the rows scroll within their card. No JS, no max-height — leans on the existing .main flex column and 100vh .page grid. (2) Pagination: LogFilters gains Before (event-id cursor) and Limit (default 200). loadLogEvents pages after sort+filter, returns hasMore. Footer 'load older →' anchor in .c-log-more (position: sticky; bottom: 0) carries href=/log?before=<oldestID> with all other filters preserved. Each page is independent — browser back works, URLs are shareable. Sort comparator now tiebreaks on event id desc so events sharing a Unix second are still deterministically newest-first (was an ordering bug masked at low event volumes). Three new handler tests cover the cap, the cursor pagination, and the no-more-link case. SQL push-down for the limit/before is a future optimization; for now we still load all events and page in memory — fine at the current 893 events.

tasks.title: Graph data model + Next-chain walker
tasks.description:
Pure data layer in internal/web/signals/graph.go. Computes per-lane spine via Next-chain predecessor/successor walk (up to 2 hops each side), cousin-boundary substitution to parent, vertical sibling stacking at focal column with +N spillover, cross-lane node dedup, lane sort by project-order position, +N pill counts on boundary parents, blocker edge collection (including off-graph suppression). No-active fallback to Next:. Red-green TDD per scenarios A-H worked through in design.

[2026-04-24 09:34] Types + walker + Scenario A green. graph.go (in-memory world loader, leftOf/rightOf walker, parent-substitute rule, cousin vs flow edge classification, blocker edges with off-graph suppression, +N count on parent nodes, state derivation). Empty DB + Scenario A (mid-sibling focal: Phase3 -> Step1 -> [Step2] -> Step3 -> Phase4(+6)) both pass. Remaining: Scenarios B-G, vertical sibling stacking, multi-lane dedup test, no-active fallback to Next.
tasks.completion_note: Data layer complete. MiniGraph is purely topological: Lanes (each with 5-slot spine + stacked sibling IDs), deduplicated Nodes pool (metadata only: State/Actor/IsParent/ChildrenNotShown/URL), typed Edges (Flow/Cousin/Blocker). No grid positions, no stroke styles — that all belongs to 7y9Zd. Nine tests cover scenarios A/B/C/E, no-active fallback to Next:, multi-lane with cross-lane dedup on a shared blocker, vertical sibling stacking, and done-blocker edge suppression. Full signals package + cmd/job + handlers suite green; gofmt and go vet clean.

tasks.title: Layout + SVG renderer

[2026-04-25 16:13] Close note (close cmd's note dropped due to a shell-quoting issue):

Implemented LayoutSubway in internal/web/render/subway_layout.go. All 9 of Ya7ea's red snapshot tests now pass.

Algorithm:
- Rows: one row per line, top-to-bottom in seed order. With a fork, the LCA chain sits inline with line index (n-1)/2 - top for 2 lines, middle for 3 lines, low-middle for 4+ (per design doc 'typically the middle line for three lines, the top for two').
- Columns: with a fork, the AncestorChain occupies cols 0..k-1; each line's anchor sits at col k; stops follow at k+1, k+2, .... Without a fork, anchor at col 0, stops at col 1+. Elision items advance the column count without placing a node, so a leading or trailing ellipsis reserves visual space.
- Geometry: same node disc and column stride as LayoutMiniGraph (32px disc, 160px col step, 40px row step) so the two graph variants render at the same visual scale. Edge geometry mirrors the existing builder: straight horizontal segment between disc edges for same-row hops; tangent-matched cubic bezier exiting/entering horizontally for row-shifting hops.
- Element flags: SubwayNodeView.IsLineAnchor and IsForkAncestor mark structural nodes for the template; SubwayEdgeView.IsBranch and IsClosure separate fork ingress edges (and their closure-marker decoration on BranchClosed) from regular Flow.
- Elisions: SubwayElisionView records the (Left, Top) center of each ellipsis glyph for the template - not yet exercised by the 6 reference scenarios but plumbed through for the windowed cases the data layer already produces.

tasks.title: Fix subway blocker edges: suppress redundant Flow + emit only nearest blocker
tasks.description:
Two bugs caught on real-world data review: (1) when a Blocker edge covers a (from,to) pair, the Flow edge between the same pair is also emitted; the Flow's arrowhead reads as if the dashed amber line itself has an arrow. (2) When a blocker open-blocks multiple rendered stops, one fan-out edge is emitted per blocked target — visually implies a chain (e.g. 'Live updates blocks Tests') when in reality a single upstream task blocks all of them transitively. Fix both in buildSubway: dedupe Flow when a Blocker covers the pair; emit at most one Blocker edge per blocker, to the nearest rendered blocked stop in tree order.

[2026-04-25 16:58] Plan: 1) red regression tests in subway_test.go for both bugs (Flow-with-Blocker dedupe, nearest-blocker only); 2) update buildSubway to dedupe Flow against Blocker pairs and limit each blocker to its nearest rendered blocked stop; 3) browser-verify against the actors task line that triggered the visual bug.
tasks.completion_note:
Fixed both blocker-edge bugs in internal/web/signals/subway.go.

(1) Flow-with-Blocker dedupe: when a Blocker edge covers a (from, to) pair, the Flow edge for the same pair is now suppressed. Implementation: blocker emission moved before the flow loop; a blockerCovers map is built first; the flow loop skips any pair already covered. Without this dedupe the Flow's arrowhead reads as if the dashed amber blocker line itself has an arrow.

(2) Nearest-blocker only: each rendered blocker now emits at most one Blocker edge, to its nearest rendered blocked stop (smallest preorder position). Subsequent blocks by the same blocker are transitive — drawing them separately would visually imply that intermediate stops carry the constraint (the 'Live updates blocks Tests' false reading from the screenshot).

Iteration order is deterministic: candidates accumulate in node-render order, blocker keys are stored in first-seen order, blocked tasks per blocker are sorted by preorder position.

Two regression tests added in subway_test.go (red->green confirmed):
- TestBuildSubway_BlockerEdge_SuppressesAdjacentFlow
- TestBuildSubway_BlockerEdge_OnlyNearestBlocked

Existing edge-case tests still pass — the previous BlockerEdge_BetweenStops case (D blocks F, non-adjacent) and DoneBlocker case behave identically under the new logic.

## Context
This is the last per-view scrubber gap. Three siblings shipped this session: 6wgmS (Plan-scrub), Xg742 (Actors-scrub), 9DWh0 (Log-scrub). Phase 8 igwXT is closed; this task lives under bYr6R as a follow-up. Caught smoke-testing — scrubbing on / leaves the Home cards frozen at live state.

## Where to start (in order)
1. Read this note + the task description above.
2. Read MEMORY.md (auto-loaded already) for project context.
3. Run `job status` for the landscape briefing.
4. Read `internal/web/handlers/home.go` (580 lines) and `internal/web/templates/html/pages/home.html.tmpl` (284 lines) — the source you're porting to JS.
5. Read commit 4511a25 (`git show 4511a25` — actors-scrub) as the structural template. The Actors port is the closest parallel: needs both `frame` (current state) and the event walk via `window.JobsScrubber.range(0, cursor.id)` for per-event derivations.

## Shape of the work
Three new modules mirroring the actors-scrub trio:
- `internal/web/assets/js/home-scrub-build.mjs` — pure data layer porting home.go's signal-card aggregations. Takes (events, frame, nowSec) → returns the shape home.html.tmpl consumes.
- `internal/web/assets/js/home-scrub-render.mjs` — pure HTML emitter mirroring home.html.tmpl exactly.
- `internal/web/assets/js/home-scrub.mjs` — driver. Listen for jobs:scrubber-frame, fetch events via `window.JobsScrubber.range(0, event.id)`, build, render, swap. On jobs:scrubber-live, fetch-and-swap window.location.href.

## Already available (don't re-write)
- `scrub-util.mjs` exports `relativeTime(nowSec, thenSec)` and `escapeHTML(s)`. Import from there.
- `replay.mjs` exports the frame shape (frame.tasks Map, frame.blocks Map, frame.claims Map). Each task has notes: Array<{actor, ts, text}> populated during forward replay.

This project follows strict red/green per CLAUDE.md. Write the build-module tests first under `internal/web/jstest/home-scrub-build.test.mjs`, confirm red, then implement. Same for the render module. The driver itself isn't jstested (no DOM in node) — same pattern as plan-scrub, actors-scrub, log-scrub.

## Gotchas seen on the actors port
- `frame` is aggregate state — it doesn't carry per-event history. For anything that aggregates events (recent activity, freshly-blocked timestamps), pull events via `window.JobsScrubber.range(0, cursorId)` and reduce.
- ageText must be computed against the cursor event's created_at (frozen), not Date.now().

- Self-guard the driver: query for the home-specific marker (probably `main` content with a home-distinctive class or data attribute — check home.html.tmpl) and bail if absent so the module can ride the shared layout without per-page wiring.
- Keep the driver swap targeted (specific elements), not the whole `<main>`, so unrelated chrome (header, peek-sheet, scrubber pill) survives the swap. Look at how plan-scrub.mjs and actors-scrub.mjs identify their swap targets.

## Live-test before declaring done
Build and run `/tmp/job serve` (port-walks if 7823 is busy), curl /static/js/home-scrub*.mjs to confirm 200, then leave the dashboard running for the user to drag-test in a browser. Same dance the prior three tasks used.

## Commit
Single commit at the end with a 'This commit Rebuilds the Home view from frame on scrubber-frame events' subject (present-tense verb completing 'This commit…'). Body: what each module does, why client-side reduction (R0Ro4 narrowing made / and /plan client-side because they need synthetic-now to be exact). Include test counts in the body.

## Don't
- Don't refactor scrub-util.mjs or any of the existing scrub modules.
- Don't add server-side ?at to /home — explicitly out of scope per R0Ro4.
- Don't write golden-file tests; substring assertions match the project style (see Kqxr0 closing note for the rationale).

tasks.title: Fix: history banner & strip ignore the `hidden` attribute
tasks.description:
`.c-history-banner` and `.c-scrubber-strip` both set `display: flex`, which overrides the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }` because the class selector has higher specificity. Result: both elements show in live mode despite the `hidden` attribute.

Fix: add a global utility rule `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` in base.css. Protects every future component too.

Regression test: a JSDOM unit test that loads layout + components.css and asserts `.c-history-banner[hidden]` computes `display: none`.

tasks.title: Pan: hold Space (or Alt/Option) and drag to move the visible window
tasks.description:
Today the strip is a fixed 24h window. Add a pan offset so users can shift the visible range earlier or later.

UX:
  - Hold Space or Alt/Option → cursor turns to a grab hand on the track.
  - Drag → translates the window by N ms; the cursor stays where it was in event-space (not screen-space).
  - Release → window stays panned until reset.

Implementation: add `panOffsetMs` to scrubber state. `xToEventId` / `eventIdToX` / `computeDensityBars` take an optional `windowStartMs` (default `nowMs - windowMs`); panning shifts that start. Math module stays pure.

Out-of-scope for this child: kinetic / inertial scrolling. Linear pan only.

Tests in scrubber-cursor.test for the new `windowStartMs` plumbing; manual verify pointer interaction.
tasks.completion_note: Pan: hold Space or Alt while drag-pointing the track to translate the visible window. scrubber-cursor.mjs gained an optional windowStartMs param on xToEventId/eventIdToX/computeDensityBars (defaults preserve trailing-24h behavior) plus a pure panWindowStartMs(currentStart, deltaPx, trackWidth, windowMs) helper. scrubber-pill tracks windowStartMs in module state, resets on enterScrubbing, re-renders density bars + cursor on every pan tick. Cursor turns to grab/grabbing while modifier is held. 8 new cursor tests cover the windowStartMs override and pan math.

tasks.title: Zoom: scrollwheel over track (and Alt+←/→) to change window length
tasks.description:
Add a `windowMs` zoom level (currently constant `ONE_DAY_MS` in scrubber-cursor.mjs).

UX:
  - Scrollwheel over the track → multiply `windowMs` by 0.9 (zoom in) / 1.1 (zoom out) per wheel tick, centered on the cursor (or on the mouse pointer when not on the cursor).
  - Alt/Option + ←/→ → same effect via keyboard, fixed steps (e.g. ×0.5 / ×2).
  - Clamp to `[60_000ms, 30 * ONE_DAY_MS]` so the zoom can't collapse to nothing or run infinitely wide.

Rebuild density bars and the time-axis labels on each zoom change. The axis currently hard-codes 24h/18h/12h/6h/now in the template — switch to JS-driven labels derived from `windowMs`.

Tests for the zoom math (clamping, center-anchored zoom preserving the cursor's event-id) in scrubber-cursor.test.
tasks.completion_note: Zoom: scrollwheel over the track narrows/widens the visible window (×0.9 / ×1.1 per tick), anchored on the pointer. Alt+ArrowRight shrinks ×0.5; Alt+ArrowLeft grows ×2; both anchor on the cursor's current event. windowMs clamps to [60s, 30 days] via the new pure zoomWindow() helper. Time-axis labels are now JS-driven via formatAxisLabels() and re-render alongside density bars on every viewport change. 7 new unit tests cover zoom math, clamp boundaries, degenerate factors, and axis-label semantics.

tasks.description: Today's algorithm unions a ±N window around every anchor (focal + lookahead leaf), which makes the focal's line render up to 6-7 stops when focal & lookahead are adjacent. tasks.title: Render elision as in-gap dots; add (+N) terminal pill for forward elision
tasks.description: Replace the current full-slot '…' rendering with: (1) backward and mid-line elisions = three small SVG circles drawn ourselves (no font dependency) sitting in the gap between two visible nodes, no column slot consumed; (2) trailing/forward elision = a small terminal pill carrying the count of hidden trailing siblings, occupying its own slot. tasks.title: SVG intrinsic sizing + CSS shrink-to-fit
tasks.description: Today the SVG uses width=100% height={CanvasH}, which non-uniformly squishes wide graphs. Switch to viewBox + intrinsic width=CanvasW, then let CSS scale it down with max-width:100%; height:auto. Reproduces at ?at=1316 (graph extends beyond container).
tasks.completion_note: Wraps the graph in a container-query-driven c-graph-frame; CanvasW/H stamped as --canvas-w/--canvas-h custom properties. Inner c-graph-canvas keeps its intrinsic CanvasW × CanvasH pixel size so SVG paths and HTML-positioned nodes/labels stay aligned at any scale; the frame uses aspect-ratio + transform: scale(min(1, 100cqw / canvas-w)) so it shrinks (never upscales) when the parent is narrower than CanvasW. SVG itself now sized intrinsically (width=CanvasW height=CanvasH) instead of width=100% height=CanvasH, killing the non-uniform squish at ?at=1316.

tasks.title: Fix overlap & backward edge at frame 1288
tasks.description: At cursor 1288 two root labels overlap at the left of the graph and one edge renders with from.cx > to.cx (legitimate path in buildSubwayEdgeView, but only ever reached when a node lands left of its predecessor). Hypothesis: column collision between a fork ancestor and a line anchor in LayoutSubway. Reproduce against the historical replay frame, then write a regression test before fixing.
tasks.completion_note: Root cause: LayoutSubway's line loop wrote cols[line.AnchorShortID] but never wrote rows[line.AnchorShortID]. When the second line's anchor was already a stop on the first line (line 1's parent is a child of the LCA, which IS line 0's anchor) or shared a short ID with a fork ancestor, the row from the earlier pass stuck and the anchor piled on top of line 0's. Buildsubway-edge-view then drew a zero-length, visually-backward edge from the overlapping disc to its first stop. Fix: write rows[line.AnchorShortID] = lineRow alongside cols. Two regression tests pin: (1) the second anchor renders one row stride below the first; (2) no two nodes share a (Left, Top) coordinate.

tasks.title: Route LCA→child-line edges through the fork branch, not as direct flow
tasks.description: When a line's anchor IS the LCA (Phase 9 = LCA + line 0 anchor) and another line branches off it (oDKYC's line), the edge from LCA to child-line anchor today renders as a same-column flow edge — drawn by the band-aid as a vertical arrow, which is wrong since arrows-down read as 'blocked path' in this design language. Proper fix: treat such edges as Branch edges (or whatever the fork machinery emits) so they render as the same gentle curve used everywhere else fork branches diverge. Likely lives in BuildSubway's edge generation: when a Flow edge would connect the LCA's row to a child-line anchor at the same col but different row, emit a Branch instead. Revert the same-column vertical-line band-aid in buildSubwayEdgeView once this lands.

tasks.title: Lookahead earns a new line only when it exits the focal's parent's subtree
tasks.description: Replace the index-level dedup with a parent-boundary rule: a lookahead anchor whose parent is the focal's parent OR a descendant of it gets absorbed into the focal's line (no new row), since the lookahead is just diving into a sibling's subtree. Lookahead anchors that exit upward (cousin or further) keep their own line, and the existing fork-chain machinery extends ancestors left-to-right back to the LCA. Reproduces ?at=1288: focal k9fFC, lookahead lands on tpC4u (child of oDKYC, a sibling of k9fFC under qkWEQ) — under the new rule no oDKYC line, just qkWEQ's ±N window.

Lookaheads that descend into a sibling's subtree are absorbed; only lookaheads that exit upward across a parent boundary (cousin or further) seed a new peek-line. Invariants: focals are leaves only; each tree node renders at most once; row's leftmost is always rendered (curve target / structural anchor); branch curves originate at leftmost-of-row. tasks.title: Add split command for inline task subdivision
tasks.description:
`job split <id>` takes an existing leaf, opens N children under it
from an inline list of titles, and re-blocks the parent on them.
Equivalent to `job add` x N + `job block` today, but condensing it
makes "I should track this as smaller steps" the path of least
resistance.

Proposed grammar:
  job split <id> "Child A" "Child B" "Child C"

The parent is automatically blocked on the new children. The parent
remains claimed by the current actor.

Why it matters: Mid-session, an agent considered breaking a large
child into sub-children but skipped it because the ritual was too
heavy. The work stayed mental instead of tracked.

tasks.title: Add structured acceptance criteria to tasks
tasks.description:
Add an optional `criteria:` array to the import schema and to
`job add`/`job edit`. Each entry has a short label and a state
(`pending` / `passed` / `skipped` / `failed`).

`job show` renders criteria as a checklist. `job done` can optionally
accept `--criterion key=passed` to update state inline, but **never
blocks on pending criteria** — the auto-close cascade remains
untouched. A soft warning may be printed if criteria are left
pending, but the close proceeds regardless.

Why it matters: Verification gates currently carry their acceptance
criteria as free-text paragraphs. A structured checklist is more
likely to be filled in by agents, more scannable for the next reader,
and enables future audit queries (e.g. "which gates had deferred
performance checks?"). This is lighter than making exit tasks
independent, which would lose the semantic parent/child relationship.

Rationale for no enforcement: we are in BUILD mode; ship the field
as an invitation to structure and observe whether agents voluntarily
fill it in. If trust gets abused, we can add a `--force` gate later.

tasks.title: Make parents with children unclaimable
tasks.description:
Parents with children should not be claimable. A claim means
"I'm actively working on this" but a parent is a container that
auto-closes when its children finish. These concepts fight each
other and produce expired claims on phases spanning hours or days.

`claim`, `next`, `status`, and `claim --next` should all filter
out parents with children from their claimable task lists. A
parent with no children is a leaf-in-waiting and can still be
claimed normally.

Cap the inline list to keep the error compact.

tasks.title: Wire criteria into the Dashboard, clean up history rendering
tasks.description:
Two related dashboard cleanups discovered while dogfooding:

1) The dashboard has no awareness of acceptance criteria. The data exists in the DB (migration 0003) but neither the task detail page, the peek sheet, nor the Log tab render it. The `criteria_added` and `criterion_state` events also fall through the dashboard's verb maps and emit raw snake_case ("criteria_added by alice") in History rows; they're absent from the Log filter chip bar entirely. The CLI's FormatEventDescription already has nice handling — there's a smell that web and CLI maintain two independent verb tables, but that consolidation is out of scope here.

2) History rows inline the full note text after the verb, which duplicates the note body that lives elsewhere on the page. The task page exposes only the *completion* note above History, so progress notes from `noted` events live ONLY inside History rows today — meaning we can't just strip them without first surfacing them in their own section. The peek sheet additionally mis-labels its single completion-note block as "Notes" (plural, generic), conflating it with progress notes that aren't actually rendered.

Render shape for criteria: a checklist between (Completion note / Progress notes) and History, four states — pending (empty box), passed (check), skipped (em-dash), failed (×). Match the CLI's `criterionGlyph` vocabulary so the two surfaces tell the same story.

tasks.title: Render criteria on the task detail page
tasks.description: Add a "Criteria" section between the Notes/Completion-note block and History on /tasks/<id>. Renders as a checklist where each row shows the four-state glyph, the label, and (for non-pending) a quiet trailing state badge (passed / skipped / failed) so screen readers and color-blind users get the state without relying on the glyph alone. Section is omitted entirely when the task has zero criteria.
tasks.completion_note: Criteria checklist lands between Completion note and History on /tasks/<id>. Per-row template renders [ ] / [x] / [-] / [\!] glyphs, the label, and a quiet trailing badge for non-pending rows; data-criterion-state attr carries the raw state for tests + CSS targeting. Section omitted when zero criteria. Glyph vocabulary mirrors the CLI's criterionGlyph().

tasks.description: Same Criteria section as the task detail page, sized for the peek sheet's narrower column. Same four-state glyphs, same trailing badges, same "omitted when zero criteria" rule. Sits between the completion-note section (once relabeled per the sibling task) and History.

Add the same to the JSON island so client-side replay can reflect criteria_added and criterion_state events without a server round-trip. Extend applyEvent / reverseEvent in the JS replay buffer to handle both event types (criteria_added appends entries; criterion_state mutates a row's state, with the prior state captured for invertibility). Peek handler gets the same data.
tasks.completion_note: Server pipeline + JSON island + JS replay buffer all wired up. Pipeline: TaskPageData carries Criteria; loadTaskPageData calls GetCriteria. JSON island: initial.TaskState gains Criteria []CriterionState (omitempty:no — always [] when none). JS: cloneFrame and initialFrame deep-copy criteria; FORWARD adds criteria_added (append) and criterion_state (mutate-by-label); REVERSE undoes criteria_added by tail-pop and criterion_state via the prior breadcrumb that the server already records. 5 new replay tests cover both forward and reverse identity round-trips.

tasks.title: Map criteria_added and criterion_state to human-readable verbs
tasks.description: The web layer's verb tables (tasks.go's eventVerb and log.go's VerbText assignment) currently fall through to raw event-type strings for criteria_added and criterion_state, leaking snake_case into History and Log rows. Add explicit cases that mirror the CLI's wording: "criteria_added" → "added N criteria, by"; "criterion_state" → "marked \"label\" passed" (substituting the actual label and state). Apply the same vocabulary to both task/peek History and the Log tab.
tasks.completion_note: eventVerb signature now takes (type, detail) so it can fold counts/labels into the phrase. Two helpers — criteriaAddedVerb and criterionStateVerb — render 'added N criteria[/criterion]' and 'marked "label" state' from the event detail JSON. Reused verbatim by log.go for the Log tab; the Log surface drops the trailing 'by' since actor sits before the verb there. Singular/plural noun handled (1 → criterion). Type chip CSS class still carries the raw type for styling hooks (mirrors claim_expired).

tasks.title: Add criteria_added and criterion_state to the Log filter chip bar

Append both, in the position that matches the prototype's intended layout (after edit/note adjacencies — they're authoring-side activity, not state transitions like done/canceled).

tasks.title: Make criteria-strict the default close behavior
tasks.description:
Today, `job done <id>` succeeds even when the task has unmarked
pending criteria — the system emits an informational note ("X
closed with N pending criteria") but does not block. The first
agent run through a criteria-bearing task on 2026-04-29 closed
one task (GjJX6) with 6 unmarked criteria due to autopilot from
prior criteria-less closes. Strict-by-default catches that slip
at the moment it matters.

Behavior: if the task has criteria and any are still in the
pending state, refuse the close and print the list of pending
criteria back to the caller. Allow override via an explicit
flag whose verbosity is the point.

Override flag: standardize on `--force-close-with-pending`. The
`--force-*` prefix is the established Unix idiom for "I know
what I'm doing"; the verbosity is what makes it self-documenting
in shell history.

tasks.title: Add `--all-passed` / `--all=<state>` shorthand to `job done`
tasks.description:
The most frequent close shape is "every criterion passed."
Today that requires one `--criterion` flag per row, which
for an 8-criterion task is 8 long quoted strings. A bulk
shorthand keeps the discipline (you still typed it) without
the typing tax.

The close ack must surface what the bulk flag touched
(e.g. `Marked 6 criteria passed before closing`) so the
self-audit value of the per-row form is preserved. A bulk
flag that silently mutates N rows would erode exactly the
discipline strict-default is trying to add.
tasks.completion_note: Wired --all-passed and --all=<state> in done.go. CLI applies per-row --criterion overrides first, then bulk-marks remaining pending criteria via RunSetCriterion. RunDone records criteria_bulk_state on the done event for History. Audit line reports per-target count: 'Marked N criteria <state> before closing.' Singular/plural noun. Empty when nothing touched.

tasks.title: Surface pending criteria count at `job claim` time
tasks.description:
The claim briefing shows the criteria list but not a header
like "you'll need to mark N criteria to close this." A
single line up top primes the agent (or human) to think
about the close shape from the moment they claim, which
reinforces the discipline strict-default introduces.
tasks.completion_note: Header line surfaces pending count when > 0, references --force-close-with-pending so phrasing matches the strict-close error. Omitted when nothing pending so post-resolution briefing isn't cluttered. 5 tests cover header presence, partial-pending count, override-flag mention, all-resolved omission, and the no-criteria regression.

tasks.title: Give criteria server-generated short IDs
tasks.description:
Today criteria are referenced by verbatim label string, which
makes `--criterion "long quoted label with parens (and × glyphs)=passed"
the dominant close-flow ergonomic. More importantly, the
`criterion_state` event records `label` as the key, so a label
edit silently orphans the historical timeline (the JS
reverse-fold landed in aez2c does `findIndex(c => c.label === detail.label)`
and that match breaks). Giving each criterion a stable short ID
— same shape as task short IDs, e.g. `x7e` — fixes both the
ergonomic and the correctness issues, and unlocks cross-surface
references (commit messages, cross-task blockedBy, stable DOM
ids for SSE partial updates).

Generation lives in `insertCriteria`, the single row-insert
path all criterion-creation paths converge through (`job add --criterion`,
`RunAddCriteria`, `job import`). Hashes stay OUT of the import
grammar — the schema is authoring grammar; the hash is server
identity. Tasks already work this way and a future re-import
function would match by title, not by hash.
tasks.completion_note: Server-mints 3-char base62 short_id per criterion via generateCriterionShortID, scoped via insertCriteria so every creation path (CLI, RunAddCriteria, import) gets one. Migration 0005 adds nullable short_id column + unique partial index; OpenDB invokes backfillCriteriaShortIDs to fill any pre-migration nulls. SetCriterionState now resolves a ref via short_id first, falling back to label, and returns the resolved Criterion. RunSetCriterion records both short_id and label on the criterion_state event detail. criteria_added events ride along with short_id per entry. RenderInfoMarkdown prefixes each list row with the short_id. JS replay-fold (forward + reverse) shares findCriterionIndex which prefers short_id then falls back to label, so legacy label-keyed events still apply. 8 Go tests + 3 JS tests cover the integration.

tasks.title: Cluster criterion_state events with their parent close in History
tasks.description:
When a task closes with multiple criteria marked in the same
`done` call, the timeline records one `done` event plus N
`criterion_state` events at near-identical timestamps. In the
web History section these render as N+1 separate rows
interleaved with surrounding events from sibling tasks. Visual
clustering — either grouping under the close, or rendering the
criteria as a sub-line of the done row — would let the dashboard
tell the same story the CLI's `job show` does after a close.

Out of scope for the original aez2c plan; surfaced here as a
follow-up because the data is already there and the dashboard
now renders criteria states.

Open question (resolve before locking the implementation
criteria): the right grouping rule. Transaction-grouping is
tight but misses criteria marked seconds before the close call
in a separate transaction. Time-windowing is loose but may
over-cluster. A small spike against real criteria-heavy close
data should pick the rule before this task is broken into
implementation children.
tasks.completion_note: History clustering implemented in handlers/tasks.go buildHistory: walks events in chronological order, finds done events, sweeps backward over the contiguous trailing criterion_state run, attaches the cluster to the done. Output preserves caller's input order (DESC for the dashboard). Cluster verbs lose trailing ' by' since the parent done carries the actor. Template renders cluster as c-history-cluster ul under the done row. Spike chose structural-trail rule over time-window because every criteria-heavy close in the live data records its criteria_state and done in the same second (note on this task). 4 unit tests + 1 HTML integration test cover happy path, standalone (no following close), non-contiguous (broken by other event), and plain-close-no-cluster regression. Log tab is structurally untouched (separate handler, no buildHistory call). CLI's job show is unchanged.

tasks.title: Implement strict-close refusal in `job done`
tasks.description:
The core of the parent task: `job done <id>` refuses to close a task whose criteria list contains any pending entries. Adds the override flag, the greppable error prefix, the pending-criteria list in the refusal, the waiver record on the done event, and the unaffected paths (tasks without criteria, --cascade, job cancel).

Sibling leaves cover the --all-passed shorthand (6zhQs) and the claim-time header (ZnNp7). Shipping this first unblocks both: --all-passed only earns its keep once strict-default exists.
tasks.completion_note: Strict-close gate landed in RunDone. Refusal uses 'cannot close: N pending criteria' prefix, lists labels per task, names --force-close-with-pending. Override path persists waived labels on done event detail under criteria_waived. Cascade and tasks-without-criteria paths unchanged. 9 internal tests + 2 CLI tests cover the gate, override, regressions.

tasks.title: import --dry-run should preview hierarchy as an indented tree
tasks.description:
Today's --dry-run output is a flat list with parenthetical 'blocked on' notes — useful for blocker validation but it loses the parent/child shape entirely. A 13-task plan reads as 13 siblings unless you mentally reconstruct the tree from the YAML.

Render the dry-run preview using the same indented-checklist shape as `job ls`, e.g.:

  - [new-1] Documentation site
    - [new-2] Scaffold the Hugo + Hextra site
    - [new-3] Wire up schema generation (blocked on new-2)
    - ...
    - [new-13] Retire DOCS.md (blocked on new-5, new-6, ...)

That gives three sanity checks at once: parenting is right, blockers point where expected, overall shape matches the authored plan. The flat form hides parenting entirely.
tasks.completion_note: import --dry-run now renders an indented checklist (matching job ls) so parent/child shape is visible at a glance. Implementation reuses the Parent field already populated on ImportedTask; depth is computed by walking <new-N> placeholders. Non-dry-run output is unchanged. Covered by TestImport_DryRun_RendersIndentedTree_MD; existing dry-run tests still pass.

tasks.title: Subway graph: row 0 should carry the LCA spine, not float the LCA above
tasks.description:
Today, when a multi-focal cluster has ≥2 in-subgraph children at the cluster LCA with no focal-leaf carve-out, internal/web/signals/subway.go:1006-1013 emits the LCA as its own top row (no stops) and pushes every in-subgraph child to a sub-row. The layout pre-seed at internal/web/render/subway_layout.go:161-185 only inlines an LCA that isn't already an anchor or stop, so when the LCA IS the row-0 anchor it ends up rendered alone above the rest of the rows.

Desired model: row 0 is the LCA spine. At every fork on the spine, the first in-subgraph child continues row 0 and the remaining in-subgraph children become sub-rows. Sub-rows recurse by the same rule. Column = tree depth falls out for free (col(branchParent)+1 with branchParent = tree parent).

Reference cases (all confirmed):

  Case A — carve-out at spine tail:
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B . [*]C

  Case B — fork at cluster LCA:
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B . [*]C
    Row 1:          | Phase 2 -> Content -> [*]X . [*]Y . [*]Z   branchParent: Doc Site

  Case C — fork deeper than LCA:
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B
    Row 1:                     | Imagery -> [*]X . [*]Y          branchParent: Phase 1

  Case D — nested forks (sub-row order is preorder):
    Row 0: Doc Site -> Phase 1 -> Setup -> [*]A . [*]B
    Row 1:                     | Imagery -> [*]X . [*]Y          branchParent: Phase 1
    Row 2:          | Phase 2 -> Content -> [*]M . [*]N          branchParent: Doc Site

Cleanest fix is at the data layer (buildOneRow): when the spine reaches a real fork (no focal carve-out, >=2 in-subgraph children), keep walking the spine through the first child and emit the remaining children as sub-rows. The layout-side pre-seed for legacy fixtures can stay as-is or retire alongside.

Visible regression today: with the documentation-site plan imported, the home subway shows 'Documentation site' floating on a ghost row above 'Scaffolding' (row 0) and 'Content' (row 1).
tasks.completion_note:
buildOneRow now walks the spine through the first in-subgraph child at every fork; remaining children become sub-rows. buildMultiFocalRows switched from FIFO queue to LIFO stack so sub-rows emit in tree-preorder (deeper sub-forks before shallower ones). The visit walk also got tightened: chain nodes descend into direct children only, and off-chain children don't recurse into their own subtrees (so e.g. an unrelated J→K,L branch stays out of the row).

Tests: 4 new TestBuildSubway_LCASpine_* cases (A: carve-out at LCA; B: fork at LCA; C: fork deeper than LCA; D: nested forks with preorder sub-row emission). 11 existing tests updated to reflect the new shape — they had documented the OLD 'leftmost-only top row' behavior, which was the bug. The render layer was unchanged; layout pre-seed for legacy fixtures still applies but is no longer load-bearing for current data flows.

Live verification: with the documentation-site plan imported, /home subway now renders 'Documentation site' on row 0 inline with 'Scaffolding' at col 1 (top=52, both labels share the row); 'Content' sits on row 1 (top=116) as a sub-row off Doc Site. The ghost row is gone.

tasks.title: Make `job status --format=json` either work or fail with a directive message
tasks.description:
`status` is deliberately human-only, but `--format=json` fails
with the generic `unknown flag: --format` — no hint about what
to reach for instead. Two acceptable resolutions:

A. Accept `--format=json` and emit a JSON shape that mirrors
   the human output: { identity, counts: {open, claimed, done,
   canceled}, last_activity_unix, roots: [...rollup rows],
   next: {id, title}, stale: [...] }. Preferred — script-driving
   agents would use it.

B. Reject with `status is human-only; use 'ls', 'show', or
   'next' for JSON output.` Cheap to ship, fixes the
   discoverability problem if (A) is out of scope.

Pick one; the current state is the worst of both.
tasks.completion_note: Adds --format=json to status with a documented JSON shape. Forest scope: {identity, counts, last_activity_unix, roots, next, stale, decisions}; subtree scope drops the preamble and returns {target, children, next, stale, decisions}. stale and roots are always arrays (possibly empty) so script consumers can iterate without a nil check; next is null when no claimable leaf exists. Unknown --format values are rejected with a directive naming the valid options (md|json). Test coverage: top-level shape, identity fields, counts buckets, roots-mirror-rollup with closed-root filtering, next leaf, next-null case, stale presence, subtree shape, unknown-format rejection. Docs updated in json-output.md (added status row), observation.md (status section), and the json-output guard at the bottom of the table is gone.

tasks.title: Direct the user toward the right fix when `job add` positional args look wrong
tasks.description:
Today's failure modes both produce misleading or silent results:

1. `job add "Child A" jTzON` (title-then-parent, transposed) errors
   with `task "Child A" not found` — accurate but misdirecting; the
   user goes looking for a missing task instead of recognizing the
   arg order.
2. `job add jTzON` (parent only, title forgotten) silently creates a
   root task literally titled `jTzON` — no error at all, and the
   slip only surfaces later when the stray root task appears in
   `job status`.

Keep the positional order strict (`add [parent] <title>`) — auto-
detecting which arg is which based on "looks like a short id" is
DWIM that fails on short titles that happen to collide with the
short-id shape. Instead, branch the error on what's actually wrong:

- Two args, leading arg doesn't resolve as a short id → `no such
  parent "Child A"; positional order is 'add <parent> <title>', or
  use --parent to disambiguate.`
- One arg, and that arg DOES resolve as an existing task's short
  id → `"jTzON" is an existing task — did you mean 'add jTzON
  <title>'? (To create a root task literally named "jTzON", pass
  --parent="" to disambiguate.)` Refuse the create until the user
  confirms intent.

The common case — one arg that doesn't resolve as a short id — stays
frictionless: a root task is created with that title.
tasks.completion_note: Branches the validation in cmd/job/add.go on what's actually wrong: a 2-arg call with an unresolved leading positional returns add: no such parent <q> with the order + --parent hint, and a 1-arg call where the arg matches an existing short id refuses with add: ambiguous single arg … and points to either supplying the title or passing --parent= for the literal-title intent. The parent flag is detected via cmd.Flags().Changed so --parent= (explicitly empty) is the escape hatch. Both errors lead with a stable, greppable prefix. Happy paths unchanged. Test coverage: all five criteria plus the --parent= escape hatch. Docs updated in reference/planning.md.

tasks.title: RunOrient domain model + assembly
tasks.description: Assemble an OrientView{Header, Tree} in internal/job/orient.go. Target resolves to the positional id, else the next available leaf via RunNextFiltered. Default scope is the whole root tree (walk GetAncestors to root, then build the subtree); --scope limits to a given subtree. Each node carries status, full description, criteria with state, and notes filtered to substance. The header synthesizes target/status/blockedBy/blocks/criteria-tally plus own_notes (target's own notes, inlined) and weigh_notes (same-parent sibling-leaf ids). Reuse RunInfo, GetAncestors, getChildren/collectDescendants, getNotesForTask, GetCriteria.
tasks.completion_note:
Built RunOrient domain model in internal/job/orient.go (8 tests in orient_test.go, all green; full suite green; gofmt/go vet clean).

PUBLIC API for the renderer (mBaVj):
  RunOrient(db, targetShortID, scopeShortID, actor string) (*OrientView, error)
  - targetShortID="" -> next available leaf (RunNext); else positional id.
  - scopeShortID="" -> whole root tree; else subtree rooted at scope. Target/scope orthogonal.

TYPES (all in orient.go, ready to render):
  OrientView{ Header OrientHeader; Tree *OrientNode }
  OrientHeader{ Target,Title,Root,Status string; BlockedBy []string; Blocks []OrientRef{ID,Title};
                Criteria CriteriaTally{Passed,Total}; OwnNotes []NoteEntry; WeighNotes []string }
  OrientNode{ Task *Task; Target bool; Blocks []string; Criteria []Criterion; Notes []NoteEntry; Children []*OrientNode }

CONVENTIONS the YAML renderer should match the design schema with:
  - Per-node field order is identity->spec->history: id,status,(closed if done),desc,labels,blocks,criteria, NOTES LAST.
  - Header.Root is the target's TRUE root even under --scope (scope only bounds Tree).
  - Notes are pre-filtered to substance via substantiveNotes(): noted events + completion note; churn excluded. NoteEntry has {Actor,Text,CreatedAt}. Completion note is appended last, attributed to the done event's actor/timestamp (both may be zero/empty - render defensively).
  - Criteria are []Criterion{ShortID,Label,State}; render as {text: Label, state: State}. State enum: pending/passed/skipped/failed.
  - target node flagged via OrientNode.Target -> emit 'target: true'.
  - 'closed' date: derive from Task.Status=='done' + Task.UpdatedAt (no dedicated closed field on Task).
  - OwnNotes/WeighNotes/Blocks/BlockedBy are nil slices when empty (render as []).

tasks.title: Scope `done --claim-next` to the just-closed task's root subtree

tasks.title: Per-actor active root ("focus") for tree-local next/claim defaults
tasks.description:
Introduce a per-actor "active root" so no-argument next/claim/status/
orient defaults stay inside the tree being worked, instead of jumping
to the globally first available leaf. Event-sourced (focus_set /
focus_released), set automatically by claiming (last-claim-wins),
auto-released when the root closes or is canceled, manually released
via `job focus --clear`. Explicit arguments always override; when the
focused root has nothing available, commands fail loudly with an
escape hint rather than silently crossing trees.

tasks.description:

attributed to an actor. GetFocus(db, actor) returns the currently
focused root task or nil, derived from the latest focus event for
that actor; a focus pointing at a deleted/canceled/done root reads
as released. Confirm the events table needs no migration; if it
does, add a numbered migration instead of hand-migrating.
tasks.completion_note: focus.go: SetFocus/ReleaseFocus/GetFocus. Events table needed no migration (generic event_type+detail). GetFocus materializes latest focus event per actor; done/canceled/deleted roots read as released with no tombstone — auto-release on completion falls out for free. Release with no focus is a quiet no-op.

focus. No event when the root is unchanged. Plain done/note/
release never touch focus.
tasks.completion_note: flipFocusOnClaim hooked inside RunClaim's tx (single choke point: claim, claim --next, done --claim-next all funnel through it). Same-root claims event-silent. Implicit release (GetFocus staleness) was already in place; the events are for tail visibility. Negative guard: closing an unfocused root emits nothing.
