tasks.title: Git-native event log
tasks.description: Make `.jobs/log/*.jsonl` the record and `.jobs.db` a disposable cache rebuilt from it, so a project's tasks travel through git across machines with no cloud, no CRDT and no merge conflicts. The vision, the design, every merge rule and the alternatives each decision beat are in project/2026-09-01-git-native-event-log.md — read it before starting any leaf. The apply refactor touches nearly every file in internal/job; those leaves are one writer, serialized.

tasks.title: Decide short id width under independent minting
tasks.description: Two replicas can mint the same five-character short id while apart, and a collision cannot be remapped safely after the fact. The doc's table gives the odds at 1k, 5k and 10k tasks. Criterion ids are three characters checked for uniqueness across the whole table, which is the larger hazard. Ruled: tasks mint six, criteria stay three and become unique per task. Close this leaf with the ruling in the note; the store leaf reads it.
tasks.completion_note:
Ruling (Ben, 2026-09-01): tasks mint six base62 characters; criterion ids stay three characters and become unique per task rather than per table.

Why six: the width is one byte slice in generateShortID and nothing resolves an id by length, so existing five-character ids are untouched and no migration runs. Six cuts cross-replica collision odds about 60x, and a collision has no safe remap once the id is in notes and commits, so cheap insurance beats a tidy column.

Why criteria stay three: every lookup is already scoped by task and every event that references a criterion carries its task, so global uniqueness buys nothing and, at three characters, is the larger collision hazard. Global addressability, if ever wanted, is task id plus criterion id, which the per-task scope supports.

Details in project/2026-09-01-git-native-event-log.md, decision 1.

Print the report described in the doc; --dry-run writes nothing. Tests build two databases from one seed, diverge them, merge, and assert every rule; a second merge of the same pair is a no-op. Reference entry in the docs.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as the commit "Adds `job merge` for two diverged copies of one database". Review fix at integration: the agent branched before migration 0008 made criterion ids per-task, so criteria were keyed on short id alone and the update was unscoped; now keyed by (task, short id) with a regression test. Documented caveat worth remembering: unions cannot express deletions, so a label or block removed on one side returns if the other side still holds it.

tasks.title: Event envelope, hybrid clock, JSONL codec and ordering
tasks.description: A new package with no SQLite dependency: the Envelope struct (v, rep, seq, ts, actor, type, task, data), the hybrid logical clock (max of wall and last_seen+1, persisted last_seen), replica id minting, a per-replica appender that takes the store lock and assigns gapless seq, a reader that parses every file under .jobs/log and returns the union sorted by (ts, rep, seq), and a parse error that names file and line. Tests: round-trip every field, ordering is total and stable under shuffle, a truncated line is reported by file and line, two appenders under the lock never interleave or repeat a seq, the clock never goes backwards across a read of a future timestamp.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as 82d8410. Reviewed the whole package: envelope, position, clock, replica, store lock, appender, reader. Two facts the store leaf must honour: use AppendLocked inside the command path (Append takes the lock itself and would deadlock), and Position.String is a cursor, not a sort key — parse before comparing. ReadFile asserts seq equals line number, so compaction (backlog) will need a per-file base seq.

Add a test that marshals every payload type and asserts no field named task_id or criterion_id carries an integer.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. Every payload already carried short ids, so the leaf was structural: EventType constants plus one struct per type in internal/job/event_payloads.go. Review fix: EditedPayload used omitempty on plain strings, which dropped an empty old_desc or new_desc; replay.mjs refuses to rewind an edit missing either half, so the fields are now pointers. Known tension for the apply leaf: done and canceled are emitted in three shapes from different call sites and share one struct with a *bool cascade; apply should decide whether those become distinct event kinds.

tasks.title: Replace sort_order with fractional sort keys

tasks.completion_note: Integrated. Keys are a 6-char base-62 integer part in ASCII digit order plus an optional fraction; KeyBetween(a, b, rep) appends the replica id plus a "1" terminator as the tie-break. Facts for the claims and relations leaves: apply(tx, Envelope) dispatches through applyTable in internal/job/apply.go; handlers run inside commit(db, func(tx, b *eventBatch) error) and emit events with b.emit(tx, type, shortID, actor, payload), which applies each as emitted so cascade planning can read its own writes. released is applied in apply_tasks.go for now because the task family emits it. tasks.title: The store — replica files, watermark, rebuild on open, reconcile
tasks.description: Opening a database resolves the .jobs/ store beside it, mints local.json on first use, compares every log file's size to its watermark, and rebuilds when they differ. Handlers append to this replica's file before applying. Add job rebuild. Add the reconcile pass: after ingesting foreign events, close parents whose children all closed elsewhere, purge children of purged roots, release the later of two live claims with reason lost-merge, and print each repair. Detect two created events for one short id from different replicas and fail the rebuild naming both replicas and titles; add job rekey <rep>:<id>, which reads the raw log and appends a rekeyed event so every later event from that replica for the old id applies to a fresh id on every machine. The lock is .jobs.db.lock, beside the cache, so the .jobs.db* ignore pattern covers it. Apply the width ruling: tasks mint six characters, criterion ids are unique per task. job status gains a store line: replica id, log files, cache state. Tests: a crash simulated between append and apply heals on the next open; a foreign file appearing triggers a rebuild; each reconcile rule.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated. Facts for adopt and cursors: commit() holds the store lock across recorder, append (AppendLocked, seq primed from the file) and the SQLite transaction, and sets log_watermarks in the same transaction. syncStore in store.go runs on every OpenDB: in sync, rebuilt, "predates the store" (any rep '' row; never rebuilt), or "log incomplete" (a replica's file missing and not writable back). Rekey is a whole-stream pre-pass. StoreSyncOf(db) gives job status its line. Appender opens its file lazily so read verbs leave no empty file.

Any difference aborts with the diff and leaves the legacy file untouched. Update job gitignore to .jobs.db* and .jobs/local.json. Test against a copy of this repo's own database and against a database that has purged tasks, criteria and provenance rows.
tasks.completion_note: Integrated as f79885a. Two corrections to the plan worth keeping: the snapshot sorts immediately before the earliest line the log already holds, not last, because positioned lines written before adoption name tasks whose created events are legacy; and applySnapshot upserts tasks by short id rather than truncating, because events.task_id references tasks without ON DELETE. data.text:
BUG FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THE DOCS (not fixed — this leaf is docs-only).

`job merge` is no longer idempotent once a store exists, contradicting the merge leaf's criterion "Merging the same pair twice changes nothing" and the text in docs/reference/setup.md and DOCS.md.

Repro, freshly built binary from be39047, two dirs:
  one/  job init --as ben; job add "Ship v1"; job add "Fix CI"
        cp .jobs.db ../two/.jobs.db          # a divergent copy, no .jobs/
  two/  job add "Only on two" --as sam
  one/  job done <Fix CI> -m "closed on one"
  one/  job merge ../two/.jobs.db            # OK: "1 task added, 0 reconciled, 1 event copied"
  one/  job merge ../two/.jobs.db            # rc=1

Second run prints:
  note: adopted this database into the store: 1 events carried across as history,
  a snapshot of 3 tasks written, replica Occ7QF. The previous cache is at .../one/.jobs.db.pre-adopt.
  Error: these databases are unrelated: their event logs differ from the first event,
  so they are not two copies of one database

Cause: RunMerge writes the merged result into the local .jobs.db directly rather than
through the log, so the next open sees a cache whose events table the log does not
explain and runs adoption on it. Adoption appends the arriving events (as legacy lines)
plus a snapshot to this replica's log file, which changes the local event history — so
the prefix walk against the other database now differs at event 1 and merge refuses.

The merge itself is correct and the data survives (.jobs.db.pre-adopt holds the
pre-merge state). It is the repeat that breaks, and it breaks loudly, not silently.

The docs no longer claim idempotence: setup.md and DOCS.md now say a merge is applied
once, name .jobs.db.pre-adopt as the way back, and point two clones of one repo at
`git pull` instead. Recorded in project/gotchas.md.

Fixing it properly means merge emitting events into the log instead of writing the
cache — worth a leaf of its own, not a patch here.

SECOND FINDING (not fixed — docs leaf, and agent-e2e owns internal/job test files).

`go test ./... -p 1` fails on `internal/job/TestAdopt_ThisRepositorysDatabase`, and it is
self-invalidating rather than a regression from any code change:

    --- FAIL: TestAdopt_ThisRepositorysDatabase (0.09s)
        adopt_test.go:221: expected a backup at .../src/.jobs.db.pre-adopt: no such file or directory
    note: this cache's events for replica GcaIeO are not a gapless run (seq 2 at line 1),
          so no log file was written for them
    note: no log file for replica GcaIeO, whose events this cache holds; the cache was
          left as it is rather than rebuilt from less

`repoDatabasePath()` walks up from the test's cwd and finds the main checkout's live
.jobs.db. That database was adopted on 2026-09-01, so `copyRepoDatabase` (VACUUM INTO,
cache only — no `.jobs/` alongside) hands `OpenDB` an already-adopted cache. Adoption
correctly does not run, so no `.jobs.db.pre-adopt` is produced and the last assertion
fails. It passed for agent-adopt because the repo's database was still legacy then; it
will fail for everyone from now on.

The fix belongs with whoever owns the file: skip when the copied database has no
unpositioned (rep '') rows, i.e. `t.Skip("this repository's database is already adopted")`,
or build a legacy fixture instead of reading the live one.

Every other package is green (`go test ./... -p 1`), and `node --test
internal/web/jstest/*.test.mjs` is 431/431. This leaf changed no .go file.

The two-replica end-to-end suite landed on branch wt/e2e (worktree .claude/worktrees/e2e). Not committed.

New files: internal/job/replica_e2e_test.go (harness + exchange/identical-dumps + the `snapshot` and short-id-collision rows), replica_rules_e2e_test.go (task lifecycle rows), replica_relations_e2e_test.go (claims and relations rows), cmd/job/replica_e2e_test.go (the happy path against the built binary). Changed: internal/job/rebuild.go (one bug fix, below).

THE HARNESS. A `pair` is two temp dirs and one shared pinned clock (merge_test.go's mergeClock). `replica.do(fn)` is one `job` invocation — OpenDB, run the body, close — so every write goes through a handler and the open is what syncs the cache with the log. `seed` writes the history both sides share and carries it across; `exchange` is carryLog both ways plus one open on each. Reused store_test.go's carryLog, adopt_test.go's legacyCache/quietNotices and apply_determinism_test.go's applyDump rather than writing new ones.

A REAL BUG THE SUITE FOUND: THE CLOCK NEVER OBSERVED WHAT IT READ. eventlog.Clock has Observe ("call it for every event read from any replica's log") and NOTHING in internal/job ever called it. LastSeen tracked only this replica's own writes, so a replica that pulled a log stamped ahead of its own wall clock minted events that sorted BEFORE the events that caused them — the exact property the hybrid clock exists to provide ("cause sorts before effect even when two machines' clocks disagree").

It is not academic. It breaks reconcile's claim repair on the second merge round. Reconcile emitted its `released` at the same millisecond as the losing `claimed` it was undoing, and the tie-break by rep put the release FIRST. On the next exchange findLostClaims walked release-then-claim, treated the loser's original claim as still live, read the winner's re-claim as a fresh conflict, and flipped the holder from the winner to the loser. Observed: holder went ben -> sam after a second exchange.

Fix: rebuildStore now calls observeLogClock(path, events) after the transaction commits, raising local.json's LastSeen to the newest event in the log. A rebuild is the only moment foreign events reach a replica, so it is the one place that has to observe them; it runs with the store lock held, so it reads and writes local.json directly rather than through UpdateLocalState (flock does not nest). Regression test: TestTwoReplicas_TheClockAdvancesPastEventsItReads — A writes with a clock an hour ahead, B pulls and replies on the slow clock, and B's reply must be stamped after what it replied to. Watched red, then green.

WHAT PASSED FIRST TIME. Every merge-rule row except the claim one: created (and the collision -> rekey -> converge path), edited per field and same field, done vs note, done/canceled/reopened plus the no-op repeat, purged vs add-child, released/heartbeat, labeled/unlabeled, blocked/unblocked in both orders, moved vs reparented with sibling keys untouched, noted interleaving, criteria_added/criterion_state, found_in latest-wins and clear, kind_changed, the adopted snapshot cloning identically, and the cascade split across replicas. The exchange-then-identical-dumps test passed first time too, with zero reconcile repairs on the happy path.

THREE BRIEF ASSUMPTIONS THAT WERE WRONG, all about how to CONSTRUCT a case rather than about a rule.
1. `heartbeat` does not extend a claim, it replaces its window with DefaultClaimTTL (30m) from now. Heartbeating a 2h claim SHORTENS it. The test claims for 5m so the heartbeat is an extension.
2. `kind_changed` is only emitted when the kind actually changes, so two replicas cannot disagree about kind unless both start from the same non-default kind. The task is seeded as an issue on both sides and B goes task-then-back-to-issue so its latest event disagrees with A's.
3. `job show` does not print the actor, so the binary test reads it from `job log`.

MUTATION-CHECKED. Making exchange one-directional fails all 15 library tests; making rebuildAndReconcile skip reconcile fails exactly the three reconcile rows (purge, claim, cascade) and nothing else.

A PRE-EXISTING FAILURE THE INTEGRATOR WILL HIT: TestAdopt_ThisRepositorysDatabase. It walks up to this repo's own .jobs.db and expects to adopt it — but agent-adopt already adopted it in place at 19:46 (.jobs.db.pre-adopt exists, .jobs/log/arMAXc.jsonl holds all 2,827 events, zero rows with rep ''). Adoption correctly does nothing on a second run, so no new .pre-adopt appears and the assertion fails. It reproduces with my diff stashed, so it is not from this leaf; the fix belongs in adopt_test.go (skip when the database is already adopted — no rep '' rows, or a .jobs/ beside it), which I left alone because wt/adopt is still unmerged.

VERIFIED. go fix / gofmt / go vet / go mod tidy / go build ./... clean; node --test 431/431; go test ./... -p 1 green apart from that one adopt test. New tests: 2.9s for the 18 library tests, 1.2s for the binary one.

data.title: job merge is not idempotent on a store-backed database
data.description: Found by the docs leaf (7W8wv) on 2026-09-01 while verifying setup.md against the built binary. `job merge` writes the other side's tail into the cache as unpositioned rows (rep ''), so on a store-backed database the next open adopts them, and the rebuilt cache orders events by position rather than by row id. A second `job merge` of the same pair then walks the two event tables from row 1, finds no common prefix, and refuses as "unrelated". The documented promise that merging the same pair twice changes nothing therefore fails on any store-backed database. Two clones of one repo should use git rather than merge, and the docs now say so; merge remains correct for its purpose, two legacy copies, applied once. Options: prove relatedness by a shared created event rather than a leading prefix, or have merge emit the foreign tail as legacy envelopes plus a snapshot through the store instead of raw rows.

data.title: Heartbeat resets a claim to the default window instead of extending it
data.description: RunHeartbeat sets claim_expires_at to now + DefaultClaimTTLSeconds (30m) absolutely, so heartbeating a claim taken for 2h shortens it by 90 minutes. The docs say heartbeat extends a claim. Found by the two-replica e2e leaf (ZeeTS) on 2026-09-01. Decide the contract: extend by the claim's original duration, or by max(remaining, default), and add a regression test on a long claim.

data.text:
Replica naming built on wt/replica (worktree .claude/worktrees/replica). Not committed.

What landed:
- `replica` EventType + ReplicaPayload{label,host,path,user} in event_payloads.go. No applyTable entry — it is recorded and writes no state.
- Minted lazily in eventBatch.emit (envelope.go): commit() runs one EXISTS ("any replica event for this rep?") after opening the tx and sets batch.needReplica; the first emit of the batch clears the flag and re-enters emit for the replica event, so it is seq 1 of a fresh file, ahead of the command's own events, in the same batch and under the same store lock. A batch that emits nothing still writes nothing. An existing replica gets its event appended at the next write, once.
- Labels are DERIVED at read time (no migration): latest `replica` event per rep, ordered by (ts, seq). internal/job/replicas.go holds ReplicaNames{Local,Labels}.Foreign(rep), LoadReplicaNames, RunReplicas, RunReplicaRename, SetReplicaName, RenderReplicas(+JSON).
- Default label = "<hostname>:<checkout path with $HOME as ~>"; the absolute path, host and OS user are recorded as their own fields so a rename loses nothing.
- Rendering: `Store: replica arMAXc "ben-mbp:~/git/Jobs" · …` in status (and `label` in status --format=json); `job log`/`tail` append " · <label>" after the actor for FOREIGN events only; the dashboard adds a muted mono `.c-log-row__replica` span inside the existing detail cell (NOT the actor cell — the actor column is a fixed 90–120px grid track and would have crushed it; the detail cell is inline-flex with room). Template + log-row.mjs + parity fixtures all updated; two new foreign fixtures (one labelled, one unlabelled falling back to the rep id) and the fixture bites — removing the JS span fails the parity test.
- New verbs: `job replicas [--format=json]`, `job replica rename <label> --as <name>`, `job init --replica-name <label>` (parks the name in local.json's new `replica_name`; renames immediately if a replica already exists).
- "replica" added to live.js KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES (the emit-site scraper demanded it).

Three existing tests changed, each for a real behaviour change:
- store_test.go TestCommitAppendsToTheLogBeforeTheWatermarkAdvances: the log now opens with `replica`, then `created`.
- merge_test.go TestMerge_RefusesUnrelatedDatabases: it put both caches in ONE directory, and two caches in one directory share that directory's .jobs/ store — so with a deterministic replica payload their first events matched and merge no longer called them unrelated. One temp dir each now, which is what "unrelated" was always meant to mean.
- database_test.go: RenderEventLogMarkdown takes ReplicaNames.

Evidence: go fix / gofmt / go vet / go mod tidy / go test ./... / go build ./... / node --test internal/web/jstest/*.test.mjs all clean. Two real stores exchanged by hand with a built binary: `job replicas` listed both with host/user/path/counts and marked this checkout, `job log` named only the foreign machine, `job status` carried the label. sleepy query on /log found the two `.c-log-row__replica` spans and zero console errors; screenshot reviewed.

Docs: concepts/the-store.md (Replicas), concepts/events.md (the type), reference/setup.md (replicas + replica rename sections, init --replica-name), reference/observation.md and machine-interface/json-output.md (store JSON gains `label`), DOCS.md (two table rows, init and status entries), plus the getting-started/observation status transcripts re-labelled and their event counts bumped by the one replica line per replica.

The replica event is minted lazily in eventBatch.emit ahead of a batch's first real event, so a command that writes nothing announces nothing; labels are derived at read time from the latest replica event per rep. Foreign events show the label beside the actor in job log and the dashboard; local ones are unchanged.

data.title: Older job binary dies on a newer cache instead of saying it is out of date
data.description: An older `job` opens a cache whose schema_migrations table records versions it does not ship, proceeds, and dies on the first query that touches a column it does not know — e.g. the binary built 2026-09-02 06:30 (migrations 1–8) against this repo's cache (1–11) fails `job orient` with "SQL logic error: no such column: t.sort_order", which reads as corruption. RunMigrations only asks which of ITS files are unapplied; it never notices the database is ahead. Fix: after loading applied versions, if the highest applied version exceeds the highest the binary ships, refuse to open with a message that names both versions and says the binary is older than the database — rebuild with `make install` or upgrade job. Refuse rather than warn: an older binary that proceeds writes events and rewrites the cache under a schema it does not understand, and the log is the record. Both the CLI and the dashboard go through OpenDB, so one check covers both. Regression test seeds a version above the binary's and expects the hint.

data.title: Old binary silently applies a newer log as no-ops: needs a store format version
data.description: The schema-ahead check (sibling issue) guards a cache that is ahead of the binary, but a fresh clone builds its cache fresh at the binary's own schema, so an old binary meets a newer .jobs/log with no warning: event types it does not know apply as no-ops (by design, for forward tolerance), so it renders the record incompletely and then appends events computed from that incomplete state. The hook is a store format version carried in the replica event that opens each log file: an old binary refusing to rebuild when a file declares a format newer than it knows. Needs a contract decision before building: what bumps the format (any new event type? only a semantic change to apply?), and whether a partial read should refuse or warn. Decide with the user, then build.

data.text: Decision (2026-09-02, main thread): heartbeat never shortens a claim. New expiry = max(current claim_expires_at, now + DefaultClaimTTLSeconds). The claim's original duration is not stored on the task row, so re-granting the original window would need schema or an event read; max(remaining, default) needs neither and is the least surprising: a 2h claim heartbeated early keeps its 2h, one heartbeated near the end gets the default window from now. Check whether the "any write by the holder extends the claim" path shares the bug and align it to the same rule.

Main thread, 2026-09-02: not dispatched with the other issues. Both fixes are real design work, not a bug fix: proving relatedness by a shared created event changes merge's safety argument, and routing the foreign tail through the store means merge becomes a log-level operation with its own envelope rules. Meanwhile merge's remaining purpose is one-shot: two legacy copies, applied once, and the docs already say so. Recommendation: park in project/backlog.md with "un-park if a legacy-copy merge ever needs to be re-run, or if merge is retired in favour of adopting the other copy's log". Waiting on the user's call before cancelling.

RunMigrations now refuses a database whose highest recorded schema_migrations version exceeds the highest embedded migration, returning a typed *SchemaAheadError{Path, DBVersion, BinaryVersion}. openCache fills in Path so the message names the cache file; that covers OpenDB, OpenDBForRecovery, the CLI and the dashboard through one check.

Message: "<path> is at schema N but this job only knows schema M: the binary is older than the database. Rebuild it (make install) or upgrade job."

Tests in internal/job/migrations_version_test.go compute the shipped version from migrations.FS() rather than hardcoding it. Red confirmed before implementing. End-to-end: a binary at schema 11 against a cache seeded at 99 exits 1 from `job orient` with that message.

Implemented on wt/FW0tDU. New helper job.extendedClaimExpiry(current) = max(now+DefaultClaimTTLSeconds, current); RunHeartbeat now computes it per task (a batch can mix a 2h claim with a short one) instead of one absolute now+30m for the batch. maybeExtendClaim (the write-extends path) already had the rule inline and now calls the same helper — no behaviour change there.

The heartbeat event payload and HeartbeatResult both carry the computed expiry, so both stay truthful.

Four cmd/job tests encoded the old behaviour. TestHeartbeat_TtlIsAlways30m ("always +30m" on an 8h claim) is the bug itself; rewritten as TestHeartbeat_NeverShortensALongerClaim. The three format-shape tests claimed 1h and asserted "expires in 30m"; they now claim 10m so they test output shape rather than TTL policy.

Docs: leaves-and-claims.md, reference/execution.md, DOCS.md and the cobra Short/Long for `heartbeat` all said "by 30 minutes"; all now say "to at least 30 minutes from now, never shortening a longer claim".

data.title: Dashboard-triggered claim expiry records an empty actor
data.description: Found by the 9Ed0cE audit (2026-09-02). internal/web/handlers/plan.go calls job.RunListFiltered(deps.DB, job.ListFilter{ShowAll: true}) with no Actor, so loading /plan or /issues can fire the read-time claim-expiry sweep and record claim_expired with an empty actor ("claim expired @" in the log). The dashboard has no per-request viewer identity, so the CLI fix does not copy over. Decide who the actor is for a sweep the dashboard triggers: the database's default identity (what an unflagged CLI call would resolve to) is the obvious candidate, since the dashboard runs on the same checkout; a system actor is the alternative. Then thread it through every dashboard call that can sweep, with a regression test on the recorded actor.

data.note: Integrated on main. Heartbeat and write-extend share extendedClaimExpiry: max(current deadline, now + default). Note: a retired cmd/job test named TtlIsAlways30m had encoded the old behaviour as a contract; the recorded decision and the docs both say extend, so it was rewritten.

data.text: Decision (2026-09-02, with the user): not full idempotency and not a --force flag; a set check when the positional prefix is zero. Compare the two event key sets (mergeEventRow.key). Other ⊆ local: report "already merged: all N of the other database's events are in this one, nothing to do", exit 0. Overlap but no prefix: the other copy was written after the merge and this side has since been adopted; refuse with a message saying merge cannot fold that tail and pointing at getting-started/across-machines (adopt the other copy in its own checkout, share the log via git). Disjoint: keep today's "unrelated" error. --force rejected: merge is state-based, forcing past a zero prefix would re-plan every event as foreign and duplicate rows.

Decision (2026-09-02, with the user): the actor for a sweep the dashboard triggers is the database's default identity, what ResolveIdentity(db, "") returns; a reserved system identity was considered and passed over. Resolve per request through one helper on the handler deps, not cached at startup, since the default can change while the server runs.

Decision (2026-09-02, with the user): an integer store format carried in the replica event that opens each log file (ReplicaPayload gains a Format field). Today's log is format 1. Bump it whenever a new event type lands or apply semantics change, since an old binary treating a new type as a no-op is exactly the silent case; the constant lives beside the event type list so the diff that adds a type is the diff that bumps it. A binary that meets a file declaring a format newer than it knows refuses the rebuild with the same "binary is older" wording the schema check uses (SchemaAheadError is the model). Existing files with no format field read as format 1.

Audit of internal/web for sweep-triggering job entry points (grep for RunListFiltered, ListFilter, BuildRollup, FindStaleClaims, RunSearch, and every job.* call in internal/web): the only call in internal/web that reaches expireStaleClaims is internal/web/handlers/plan.go:150 (job.RunListFiltered, used by both /plan and /issues, since Plan()/Issues() share planHandler). No other internal/web file calls RunListFiltered, RunListWithTail, RunClaim, RunClaimNext*, RunStatus, RunClosedTail, or RunIssueRoot* — those are the other expireStaleClaims callers in internal/job. RunSearch (used by search.go) does not call the sweep.

Fix: added `sweepActor(deps Deps) string` in internal/web/handlers/handlers.go, calling job.ResolveIdentity(deps.DB, "") fresh per call (not cached at server start). Threaded it into plan.go's RunListFiltered call as Actor. No other internal/web callsite needed it.

Regression test: internal/web/handlers/plan_claim_expiry_test.go — claims a task, forces claim_expires_at into the past via UPDATE (mirroring internal/job/issueroot_test.go's TestLiveClaims_ExcludesExpiredClaims pattern), sets a default identity with job.SetDefaultIdentity, fetches /plan, and asserts the recorded claim_expired event's Actor equals the default identity. Ran red (failed: actor = "" want "ben") before the fix, green after.

data.text:
Implemented on wt/vkDTEN. classifyMergeRelation replaces commonEventPrefix: when the positional prefix is zero and both sides hold events, it compares the two key SETS and returns one of mergeAlreadyApplied (other subset of local -> report "Already merged: all N of the other database's events are in this one, nothing to do.", exit 0, nothing written), mergeDivergedTail (overlap, no containment -> refuse, pointing at docs/content/docs/getting-started/across-machines.md), mergeUnrelated (disjoint -> today's message). No --force. Planner untouched.

Decision on bookkeeping events: `snapshot` and `replica` are EXCLUDED from the set comparison. Neither is shared history — a snapshot is one replica's compaction of state it already holds, a replica event names a checkout's cache path and label — and both are minted per replica, so the two sides never hold the same ones. Including them would make an already-merged pair look permanently diverged (local gains a snapshot on adoption; the staged copy of the other file is opened through OpenDB in a temp dir and can mint its own). Cost: a bare replica-rename on the other copy is not folded; that is per-machine bookkeeping and meaningless on this side.

Tests: internal/job/merge_repeat_test.go (case 1 and case 2, both driven through the real OpenDB adoption + position-ordered rebuild), cmd/job/merge_repeat_test.go (exit 0 + "Already merged" via two real CLI invocations). All three ran red first (cmd one verified red by stashing merge.go/merge_snapshot.go). Case 3 still covered by TestMerge_RefusesUnrelatedDatabases.

Docs: setup.md now states the three outcomes; DOCS.md merge row corrected; the cobra Long text keeps "merging the same pair twice changes nothing" because it is now true. Deleted the obsolete gotchas entry "2026-09-01 — job merge is a one-shot on a store-backed database".

go fix / gofmt / go vet / go mod tidy clean; go test ./... all green.

data.note: Integrated on main. classifyMergeRelation falls back to a set comparison when the prefix is zero: already merged (exit 0, nothing written), diverged tail (refused, points at across-machines), unrelated. snapshot and replica events excluded as per-replica bookkeeping. Mechanism note from the agent: adoption re-fires after a merge because applyMergePlan inserts the foreign tail with rep "", which probeLegacy reads as a legacy marker; a future log-routed merge must clear that trigger.

data.text:
Built on wt/uTfC1F. StoreFormatVersion + `const StoreFormat = 1` live beside the event type list in event_payloads.go, with `storeFormatAdded map[StoreFormatVersion][]EventType` as the golden vocabulary (types listed under the format that introduced them; a format that only changed apply semantics gets an empty entry). ReplicaPayload gains `Format StoreFormatVersion json:"format,omitempty"` — typed rather than the brief's plain int; newReplicaPayload writes StoreFormat, absent reads as 1.

internal/job/store_format.go holds StoreFormatAheadError (modeled on SchemaAheadError), fileStoreFormat (latest replica event wins, none = 1) and checkStoreFormat. rebuildStore calls it per file as each file is read, before anything is applied, so a file from the future stops the whole rebuild.

The golden test parses event_payloads.go with go/ast rather than keeping a second hand-written list, so the diff that adds a constant is the diff the test sees; verified by mutation (adding a type fails it with "bump StoreFormat and list them under the new format").

`job replicas` now shows "N events · format 1 · last …" and ReplicaInfo carries Format in JSON. `job status`'s store line was left alone.

Known gap, deliberate: the check is on the rebuild path only. An old binary opening a cache another binary already built in-sync (watermarks match) takes the hot path and never reads a log file, so a pure vocabulary bump with no accompanying migration is not caught until the next rebuild. Cache state is correct in that case, since the newer binary applied it.

Suite: go test -p 1 ./... green; go fix/gofmt/go vet/go mod tidy clean.

data.note: Integrated on main. StoreFormat = 1 on ReplicaPayload.Format; rebuildStore refuses a file declaring more, with StoreFormatAheadError. The golden vocabulary test parses event_payloads.go so adding a type forces a bump. Hot-path gap (cache already rebuilt by a newer binary is opened without a format check) parked in project/backlog.md.
